The mark X stands for a spot to be found. This Unown floats at the center of the room and does not move for hours.
It has the form of a letter Y, two arms joined to a single stem. It raises its arms like a branch against the wall.
The mark Y is a fork in the path. This Unown hovers where two halls meet, waiting for a visitor to choose.
It is shaped like a letter Z, a bolt between two bars. It darts about in sharp turns and leaves a flicker behind.
The mark Z is the last of the line. This Unown sits quietly in a corner and has the look of an ending.
It has the form of a mark, a tall line with a dot under it. It appears suddenly in a doorway and startles anyone who sees it.
The mark makes a sound of surprise in the old writing. This Unown pops out of the dark and then vanishes.
It has the form of a hooked line with a dot underneath. It tilts as though asking something, and it waits for an answer that never comes.
The mark asks a question in the old writing. This Unown circles curious visitors and peers at them with a puzzled eye.
Wobbuffet is endlessly patient and will stand in one place for hours without complaint. It salutes with one arm when it is ready.
Wobbuffet's body is soft and rubbery, and blows seem to bounce right off it. It lives in quiet caves.
It stretches its long neck to reach the tender shoots at the tops of trees. Herds on the plains move slowly, stopping wherever the canopy is greenest.
It grazes on the leaves of tall trees on the open plains. When the tail is hungry it nibbles grass, and the front head pretends not to notice.
Pineco's shell is made of overlapping scales like a cone. It keeps its tiny face hidden in the gap between them.
When it feels threatened, its shell can burst open with a loud bang. It lives in forests of tall conifers.
Forretress is wrapped in a heavy shell of steel-gray plates. The shell is so dense that it weighs more than a hundred kilograms.
Forretress seldom wanders far and spends long stretches sitting perfectly still. When it opens up, sharp spikes poke out to ward off foes.
Dunsparce has a pale yellow body with blue stripes and tiny wings. It wriggles along the ground like a snake.
Few people have spotted one, since it keeps to dim, quiet places. Its stubby wings flutter when it is nervous.
It nests in cracks high on sheer cliffs, where nothing that walks can reach it. Its pale membranes catch the wind like small kites when it leaves.
A Gligar's pincers grip so firmly that it can hang from a single claw through a storm. It tucks its tail under its body to keep warm.
It sleeps coiled around a stone pillar deep underground, and in time the pillar is polished like a mirror. Miners treat such pillars with great respect.
An old Steelix moves slowly and rests for weeks between journeys. Its shining coils are sometimes mistaken for a buried iron rail.
Its body turns into crystal-hard steel, and it digs through rock as if through soft earth. Its length stretches farther than ever.
In this form its mighty body hums with the sound of grinding stone. It cracks open the mountain and sends sand flying as it rises.
Snubbull has a wide jaw and a gruff little growl. Despite its looks it loves to be petted and fussed over.
Snubbull is often kept as a pet in towns. It hates being alone and sulks if it is ignored.
Its huge lower fangs make it look fierce, yet it is loyal to those it trusts. Many Granbull guard homes in towns.
Its jaw is very strong, and it can bite through thick wood. It prefers to frighten foes away with a deep growl.
Qwilfish swells up into a spiky ball whenever it is alarmed. Its round eyes give it a permanently surprised look.
Its toxic spines can make a person ill for days. Fishermen handle it carefully when it ends up in their nets.
It lives in cold, dark waters and bristles with venomous spines. The dark scales help it hide as it drifts with the current.
A spiky fish that inflates itself when threatened. It struggles against strong currents and gets tangled in nets.
Its steel shell rings like a bell when struck, and it uses the sound to warn others away. A dented Scizor rests for days while the metal hardens again.
Its pincers snap with a sharp ring that echoes across open fields. Rivals often back down after hearing a single clap.
Its pincers grow large and sharp like great scissors. It snips with the speed of a machine and rarely misses.
In this form its armor shines like polished steel. It hovers with a quick, even buzz and cuts down whatever stands in front of it.
Shuckle's red shell is dotted with holes, and its yellow limbs poke out through them. It moves very slowly.
Its shell is hard enough to protect it from almost any blow. It spends long days tucked into crevices among sea rocks.
Its claws grip bark so firmly that it can sleep upright on a trunk through a gale. Children hunt for the deep scratches it leaves on the bark.
It is peaceful by nature and spends whole days on the same tree trunk. Only a rival intruding on its favourite tree will make it raise its horn.
Its horn grows to a size larger than its body. It picks up a foe many times its weight and hurls it with ease.
In this form its arms sprout two more horns, and it strikes many times in a single blow. It charges ahead with the force of a truck.
It leaps between icy rocks on silent paws and leaves no tracks behind. Its red head feathers are the only flash of colour in the snow.
A Sneasel will hide food in the cracks of glaciers and remember dozens of spots. Thieves of its own kind are chased off with furious hisses.
It lives in the snowy mountains and tears at prey with sharp claws. It carries poison on those claws and can strike down larger foes.
A nimble climber of cliffs, it prowls on the cold slopes. Its fur is dense and wild, and it hides among the rocks.
The crescent mark on its forehead shines like a little moon. It wanders the woods snacking on sweet berries and nectar.
It looks cuddly, but it scratches hard if anything tries to take its food. Mothers keep their cubs close as they forage.
The ring-shaped mark on Ursaring's chest stands out against its brown fur. It rips into hollow logs with its massive claws to reach grubs.
Ursaring hibernates through the coldest months. Before sleeping, it eats huge amounts to build up fat.
Slugma creeps through volcanic areas at a slow, steady crawl, leaving the ground scorched behind it.
Slugma's body is so hot that it can set dry grass on fire. It dislikes rain and hides in rocky hollows when clouds gather.
Magcargo carries a lumpy shell of cooled magma on its back. Its whole body is hot enough to melt snow it touches in moments.
Magcargo lives in volcanic craters and moves slowly through the heat. Rain falling on it turns instantly into steam.
Its shaggy coat keeps it warm in freezing caves, and it sleeps buried to the eyes in snowdrifts. Only its pink snout pokes out to breathe.
Young Swinub follow their elders through the snow in a line, nose to tail. One that falls behind squeals until the others stop and wait.
It stamps on the ice ahead to judge how thick it is before crossing. A Piloswine that hears a crack turns back at once and finds another way.
A herd of Piloswine walks in single file through deep snow, each stepping in the tracks of the one ahead. The leader changes every few hours.
Corsola clusters in warm, shallow reefs, where groups of them form colorful beds. Small fish dart in and out among their branches.
Corsola moves slowly along the seabed on stubby legs. When frightened, it pulls back into a crack in the reef.
It is a ghostly coral that was caught in a long-ago change in the sea. Its branches have turned pale and it gives off a sad glow.
It drifts along the cold shore with a hollow stare. Its brittle body crumbles easily, and it sheds bits of itself as it goes.
It drifts beneath rafts of floating seaweed in large schools, and the whole school turns at once at the faintest shadow overhead.
A Remoraid's fins flutter rapidly to keep it steady in rough currents. It can hang in one spot even while waves crash overhead.
It decorates the rock around its den with bits of shell and coloured glass. Divers recognise each Octillery by the patterns it has made.
An Octillery is clever with its tentacles and can open shells that other Pokémon cannot. It sometimes carries a favourite stone with it from den to den.
Delibird is a cheerful bird of snowy mountains with a sack-like tail. It hops along icy ledges rather than flying.
Delibird sometimes leaves gifts for those who have treated it kindly. It nests in sheltered hollows among the rocks.
It glides through calm seas with slow beats of its wide fins, its shadow sliding over the sandy bottom. Fish below dart for cover as it passes.
A Mantine can travel for days without resting by riding warm currents. Sailors take its broad, dark shape as a sign that the weather will hold.
Skarmory's feathers are edged like blades of steel and ring when they clash. Its red-lined wings flash in sunlight.
Skarmory nests high on cliffs, out of reach of other Pokémon. Its cry is harsh and metallic.
Its wings grow into great blades of steel, and it rides the wind with a thunderous clatter. It dives from the clouds at a terrifying speed.
In this form it is as heavy and hard as a fortress, and it takes the hardest blows without a scratch.
It marks the borders of its range with scorch marks on rocks. Travellers in the hills learn to read those black smudges as a warning.
Its breath smells of soot, and wisps of smoke curl from its nose on cold mornings. Young Houndour play by chasing each other's tails through the scrub.
It dens in hollows under rocky ledges, and the stone there is blackened from years of its breath. Its paws are tough enough to cross hot embers.
It keeps its embers banked low while resting, so only a dull red glow shows between its teeth. A sudden flare means it has caught a scent.
Its horns grow long and its body burns with a fierce heat. It stalks about with a low growl and fire in its mouth.
In this form the blaze on its back turns white-hot. It lights up the night, and its howl strikes fear into all who hear.
Kingdra is a proud dragon of the sea with a long, curled tail. It moves with great power through the water.
Its scales are smooth and tough. Sailors who glimpse it consider the sight a sign of good fortune.
Phanpy loves to play in muddy rivers, and it rolls about on the banks until it is covered in mud.
Young Phanpy follow their parents in a line, each holding the tail in front with its trunk. They squeal when separated.
Donphan's gray hide is thick and rough, like a suit of armor. It digs for roots with its tusks.
Herds of Donphan travel across dry plains in search of water. They rest together in the shade at midday.
Its rebuilt body is smoother and rounder than its first form's, and it bobs gently as it floats. Its eyes follow movement with a faint whirr.
A Porygon2 sometimes freezes for a moment, as if thinking. It hums with a soft electronic tone while it sorts through what it has learned.
Stantler's antlers curve back into rings, and a dark orb sits in each one. It lowers its head and stares when it feels uneasy.
Stantler lives in herds in quiet woods and meadows. It is wary and bolts at any unusual noise.
Smeargle loves to draw and dabs its tail across rocks and walls. Each one paints in its own style.
It is curious and studies other Pokémon closely, copying what they do. Its tail fluid changes color with its mood.
Tyrogue picks scuffles with anything it meets just to test itself. Its style of fighting changes as it learns, deciding what it will become.
Tyrogue is small but scrappy, and it hates sitting still. It is often found in gyms and dojos where people train.
Hitmontop balances upside down on the horn on its head, with its legs pointed at the sky. It practices for hours.
Its head horn is worn smooth from all its spinning. It is calm and focused outside of battle.
Smoochum hums little tunes as it wanders through the snow. It prefers cold places and avoids the heat.
Its lips are cold to the touch and can numb whatever they press. It is fond of people who play gently with it.
It loves to touch electrical outlets and plugs, giggling at every spark. Households with an Elekid keep their sockets covered.
The plug-shaped horns on its head crackle when it is excited. Two Elekid that meet will touch horns, trading a quick snap of sparks by way of greeting.
Its body is warm enough to melt snow around it in a wide circle. Magby often curl up near hot rocks and sleep through cold nights.
A Magby chases its own sparks across the ground until it trips over its feet. It sulks for a moment, then starts the chase all over again.
Miltank is a steady, good-natured Pokémon that farmers have kept for generations. It hums contentedly while grazing.
When it feels threatened, Miltank tucks itself into a ball and rolls into foes at speed. Its pink hide is thick.
Its soft fur muffles every sound, so its arrival is felt more than heard. Patients say a room grows warmer the moment a Blissey walks in.
A Blissey lines the pouch on its belly with fresh fluff every spring. The old fluff is gathered by Pokémon Centers to stuff their pillows.
Raikou bounds across the land in great leaps, gone before the eye can follow. Storms seem to gather wherever it pauses.
The cloud-like mane on its back crackles with static. Old stories tie its first appearance to a tower that burned.
Entei roams the land without rest, and the air around it shimmers with heat. Its eyes burn with a fierce, steady light.
Legends tie its birth to a great fire. Flames that it breathes are hotter than molten rock.
Suicune moves with quiet grace, its flowing tails trailing behind it like ribbons. It appears briefly and then is gone.
It is drawn to clear lakes and springs and lingers at their edges in the early morning. Few have seen it twice.
Larvitar has a tough, mossy green hide and a single horn. It is small but very heavy for its size.
Its hide is as hard as stone. It fights with stubborn courage against much bigger foes.
Pupitar's gray shell is sealed tight except for a few small holes. It sometimes shoots off without warning and crashes into things.
Inside its shell, its body is preparing for a dramatic change. It thrashes wildly when disturbed.
Tyranitar's armored body shrugs off almost any attack. Its heavy tail sweeps boulders aside as it walks.
When it stamps its feet, boulders tumble and cliffs collapse. It has little patience for weaker creatures.
It is built like a mountain, with spikes along every side. Its roar can level a cliff and its fury is endless.
In this form its strength is overwhelming, and it can reshape the land with a swing of its tail. Nothing stands in its way.
Lugia's silver-white body gleams as it glides above the waves. It surfaces only rarely, and its arrival calms the sea.
Old songs in coastal villages tell of a great silver bird rising from the sea. Its cry is low and haunting.
Ho-Oh's plumage shimmers in shifting hues of red, gold and green. A single feather it drops is said to stay warm for years.
It is said to have brought three Pokémon back to life after a great fire. It roosts atop a tall tower.
Celebi drifts through time and visits peaceful woods. Its delicate wings shimmer like dew in the morning light.
Celebi is small and shy, and it vanishes in a shimmer of light when approached. Old shrines in the forest were built in its honor.
Tiny hooked pads on its feet let it cling to bark and even to smooth walls. It scampers up trunks to watch the forest floor from above.
Treecko keeps its tail raised like a small flag and swishes it to talk to others of its kind. A calm, patient hunter, it waits for insects to wander close.
Leaves along its arms are sharp enough to slice twigs clean through. It crosses the canopy in long, quiet leaps and seldom touches the ground.
Grovyle guards a stretch of woodland as its own and chases off anything that tramples the saplings. Its tail sways in time with its steps.
The seeds growing along its tail are a mark of pride, and it grooms them every morning. It moves through thick trees faster than most birds can fly.
Sceptile stands very still on a branch until prey is within reach, then strikes with the blades on its forearms. It is a fiercely loyal partner.
Leaves spread out from its back like a pair of wings, and it moves like a streak of green light. It races across the treetops in an instant.
In this form the seeds on its tail ripen and rattle as it runs. Its blades cut through the air with a whistle.
A warm glow lives in its belly and keeps its downy body cozy on cold nights. Hold it close and you will feel a gentle heat, like a hand warmer.
Torchic trails after whoever feeds it, peeping all the way. When startled it puffs out a few sparks, then looks quite embarrassed about it.
It trains by kicking at fence posts and stones, over and over, until the dust rises. Its legs are far stronger than its small size would suggest.
Combusken lets out a shrill cry to hearten its allies and to unsettle rivals. The feathers on its head stand up when it gets excited.
Flames burst from its wrists when it fights, and a single leap can carry it over a house. It prefers a clean, fair match against a strong opponent.
Blaziken's kicks hit with the weight of a falling beam. It grows restless if it goes too long without a worthy challenge.
Flames pour from its wrists and ankles and its speed is almost too much to follow. It kicks and punches in a blazing blur.
In this form it fights faster the longer the battle goes on. The heat from its body makes the air around it dance.
The fin on its head feels the slightest change in the water and warns it of what is coming. It spends sunny afternoons dozing half buried in warm mud.
Mudkip is strong enough to heave a boulder aside with its sturdy little legs. It follows trainers around the shore, splashing in every puddle.
Its hind legs are much stronger than the front ones, so it pushes through mire with ease and stays steady where others sink.
Marshtomp likes to sit with its feet in wet soil, and it grows cranky if the ground dries out. A rainy day makes it lively and playful.
Its great arms can drag a boulder out of the way or tow a ship that has run aground. It reads the tide from the sound of the waves.
Swampert keeps a watchful eye on the shore and will carry stranded travelers back to dry land. It is happiest wading through a storm.
Its arms swell into mighty clubs, and it moves through water like a torpedo. A single sweep of its arm can sink a ship.
In this form its power is unstoppable. It wades through the roughest seas and can reshape a shoreline with a stomp.
It will chase anything that moves, nipping at heels and tugging at cloth. A scolding makes it back off for a moment, but only a moment.
Poochyena roams in loose gangs and is bold about eating scraps left by travelers. Its ears swivel at every sound while it sniffs for a trail.
A pack follows one leader, and each member knows exactly where it stands. They herd prey together and never leave a wounded packmate behind.
Its growl is low and steady, and its stare can freeze a careless hunter in place. A trained Mightyena obeys its trainer without a bark.
It cannot walk in a straight line and weaves from side to side, nose to the ground. Anything shiny or tasty it finds goes into a hoard.
Zigzagoon rubs its back against tree trunks to leave a scent and to scratch an itch. It often trots along beside travelers for company.
It is a mischievous raccoon with a black and white pattern that winds about its body. It runs about in a straight line, and bumps into things.
A wanderer of the countryside, it dashes about with an eager look. It tries to bite anyone who gets in its way.
Once it spots prey it dashes in a dead straight line at a speed that blurs its stripes. Turning is not its strong suit, so it often overshoots.
Linoone covers a whole meadow in a few seconds when it runs. After a hunt it flops down in the grass and naps with its legs splayed.
It runs at a fast speed in a straight line and slams into anything ahead. Its long body flows over the ground like a snake.
A fierce fighter that charges at a foe with a wild glare. It is aggressive and does not back down once it has started to attack.
It chews neat crescents out of the edges of leaves, always starting at the tip. A tree full of Wurmple looks as though someone has been at it with scissors.
Wurmple sway their heads from side to side as they crawl, tasting the air for the scent of fresh growth. They hatch in spring by the hundred.
Dew beads on its pale, smooth cocoon like pearls in the morning. Birds that peck at one find the silk far tougher than it looks and soon give up.
Children count the Silcoon in a wood each spring and wait eagerly to see which of them will be the first to crack open.
Its wings carry bright eyespots that it flashes at anything that comes too close. A startled foe often freezes long enough for it to flutter away.
It drifts across meadows in loops, visiting the same flowers in the same order every day. Gardeners can set their watches by its rounds.
Its dark cocoon is rough and knobbly, blending with the bark of the tree it clings to. Woodcutters are careful to check a trunk before they swing an axe.
A Cascoon inside its shell stirs now and then, making the whole cocoon rock gently. It seems to be stretching in readiness for what comes next.
It flies only after sunset, its wings beating with a soft, papery rustle. The green dust it sheds glows faintly as it drifts down through moonlit trees.
A Dustox rests through the day pressed flat against the underside of a leaf. Its drab markings make it all but invisible among the shadows.
A wide leaf rides on top of its head and serves as a little raft, so it floats lazily across calm ponds. When the water dries up it grows weak and droopy.
Lotad sips rain from its leaf and now and then lets a drop roll off. Children like to balance it on their heads as a funny hat.
It loves to tease fishermen by tugging their lines from below, then giggling at the reaction. Its webbed hands make it a very quick swimmer.
Lombre's smooth skin is slick with a cooling film that feels pleasant on a hot day. It dislikes dry, dusty roads and stays near streams.
Cheerful music sets it dancing, and a whole group will sway and clap along together. The merrier it is, the more energy it seems to have.
Ludicolo wears a hat of broad leaves and a long, flowing fringe. It greets the morning sun with a stretch and a swaying little jig.
It hangs from a branch by the stalk on its head and looks just like an acorn. When a person walks beneath, it drops down to play a trick.
Seedot soaks up water through its feet to plump itself up, then shakes it off in a spray. It grows fussy when its shell gets dirty.
It plays a thin tune on a leaf flute at night, and the sound can unsettle travelers in the dark. It is clever and a little mischievous.
Nuzleaf's long nose wags as it sniffs for ripe berries. It shies away from crowds and watches the world from tall trees.
A single wave of its great leaf fans can whip up a gust that tosses grown people aside. It lives deep in the woods, far from any town.
Shiftry carries itself like a stern old hermit and chooses its companions with great care. Its mere shadow makes smaller creatures hush.
Brave beyond its size, it will dive at much bigger foes to defend its nest. It sulks and fluffs its feathers when it is hungry.
Taillow darts from warm lands to cool ones with the seasons. A trained one will perch on a shoulder and sing the moment it sees dawn.
It glides in wide circles, then folds its wings and drops like a stone on its target. Its glossy plumage is kept neat and spotless.
Swellow's call carries across whole valleys. It holds its head high when it lands, proud of the speed that brought it there.
It wheels over harbours crying out whenever a boat comes in. Flocks squabble loudly over anything the fishermen throw back into the water.
A Wingull sleeps floating on the waves, its head tucked beneath one wing. Rough weather barely disturbs it, since it simply rides each swell up and down.
Its bill can hold an astonishing load, and it uses it to haul home anything it fancies, from fish to driftwood. Harbour children have found lost shoes in its stash.
A Pelipper perches on harbour posts for hours, keeping a patient eye on the nets. It has learned exactly when the boats come home.
Its round head is heavy for its small body, so it often sits down to rest after a short walk. Its red horns tilt toward whatever has caught its interest.
A Ralts that is content hums so quietly that only those close by can hear it. It often falls asleep in a sunny window with its head on its arms.
Its skirt-like body flares out when it turns, and it practises slow turns for hours in empty rooms. A Kirlia that is being watched stops at once and looks elsewhere.
Kirlia grow attached to a single place where they feel safe. A Kirlia that is moved to a new home may stand by the window for days before it settles.
It moves so smoothly that its feet never seem to touch the floor, and its gown-like body barely stirs. A Gardevoir can cross a crowded room without anyone noticing.
Its arms are thin and elegant, and it uses them to sketch shapes in the air while it thinks. Those it has bonded with say they can almost read the shapes.
Its gown flares wide like a bridal veil, and it holds a sorrowful, caring look. It would give up everything to keep its trainer from harm.
In this form its devotion knows no bounds. It warps the very space around itself to shield those it loves.
It skims across the surface of ponds as if on ice, never sinking. A sweet syrup oozes from its head and draws smaller creatures near.
Surskit prefers calm, clean water and will leave a pond that turns muddy. On a bright day you can see its reflection racing along beside it.
The eye patterns on its antennae look like fierce staring eyes and frighten off foes. It hovers over lakes, beating its wings to stay aloft.
Masquerain flies far out over the water in rain, its fine wings wet and shining. It folds its antennae down when it wants to rest.
It lives in damp, dark soil beneath fallen leaves and wears a cap that scatters fine spores when shaken. The cap is its pride.
Shroomish sleeps much of the day, only wandering out when the air is cool and moist. It dislikes bright sun and dry wind.
Its quick, snapping punches fall faster than the eye can follow, and its tail curls and uncurls as it strikes. It never fights without good cause.
Breloom balances on a thick springy tail, bouncing lightly from tree to tree. The cap on its head grows a bit with every year.
It hangs from a branch for most of the day and moves only a few steps before resting again. A full night's sleep is never enough for it.
Slakoth chews leaves at a snail's pace and sighs as it does. Its calm face makes an onlooker feel sleepy too.
It cannot sit still and runs about in circles, scratching at the earth and the bark. If it is made to rest it grows tense and edgy.
Vigoroth's claws leave deep marks on any tree it passes. It thrives on activity and sleeps only when it has worn itself out.
It spends its days sprawled on the ground, munching whatever is within arm's reach. When it finally stirs, the whole ground seems to shake.
Slaking is the very picture of laziness, yet one swipe of its massive arm can fell a sturdy tree. It naps until a meal comes by.
It spends long years underground, drinking from tree roots and slowly growing. Sunlight is hard on its pale eyes, so it hides in the dark.
Nincada's shell is tough but its body inside is tender. When the time is right it climbs out of the soil and cracks open.
Its wings beat so fast that its body is only a blur, and the buzz they make is deafening. Few can keep it in sight for more than a heartbeat.
Ninjask is rarely still, and it will fly all day without a pause. It is shy of crowds, and its cry rings sharply over the treetops.
A hollow shell with no breath and no pulse, it drifts about silently. People who stare too long into the dark gap of its back feel uneasy.
Shedinja does not eat or drink, and it seems to live off nothing at all. Superstitious villagers keep one far away from their homes.
Normally it speaks in a whisper, but a sudden fright makes it howl at a volume well beyond its small body. It covers its own ears when it does.
Whismur lives in quiet caves where its voice echoes. It practises squeaks and murmurs for hours and gets shy when others listen.
Heavy stamps of its feet send shock waves through the rock, and its bellow makes them stronger. A blast from its voice can rattle windows and shake pebbles loose.
Loudred listens for echoes to learn the shape of the dark places it explores. A pair of big ears stand up whenever it hears a new sound.
The tubes along its body gather air and fire it out as a roar that can be heard across a mountain. Its mouth gapes wide when it shouts.
Exploud uses different calls to signal to its friends, and a trained one can sing along with music. The sound it makes is gentle at a short range.
It slaps at tree trunks and boulders for hours to harden its palms, and it eats big meals to build up its strength. It never complains of tiredness.
Makuhita is a cheerful, stubborn fighter that gets back up every time it is thrown. It dreams of one day becoming a champion.
Its thick palms can slam with enough force to topple a truck. A bout against a human champion is a pleasure it seldom refuses.
Hariyama keeps a calm, dignified manner and trains on cold mountain slopes. It stomps the ground to settle itself before a match.
It plops down on its round tail like a cushion and rocks back and forth. An Azurill that tips over rolls about in circles, giggling all the while.
It splashes in puddles after rain and stamps until every drop has flown out. Its parents watch from nearby, ready to fish it out of deeper water.
It stands so still that minerals slowly gather on its body over the years. Cavers have chipped crystals the size of a fist from an old Nosepass.
Iron filings in the soil around it form neat lines that point to its nose. Prospectors follow these lines to find where a Nosepass is resting.
Round and round it spins after its tail, and when the world starts to swim it topples over and begins again. Anything that sways or dangles is fair game for its paws.
Skitty has a gentle purr and a bright, curious eye. Many a household keeps one because it makes such good company.
It sleeps wherever it likes and wakes only when it wants to, and no one tries to tell it otherwise. Its soft fur is groomed with great care.
Delcatty keeps to quiet corners and lets its trainer see it only at the right moments. It stalks about with its tail held high and its nose in the air.
Its gleaming eyes are really gems, and they glow in the gloom. It scrapes at cave walls for stones to eat, leaving glittering dust behind.
Sableye hides in the dark and leaps out with a grin. It is happiest in places where no light ever reaches.
A big gem sits in front of it and its eyes glow with greed. It keeps its treasure hidden behind a cunning grin.
In this form its body has grown heavy with jewels. It is too weighed down to run, but it dodges every blow with a wicked trick.
The big jaws on its head are really horns shaped like a trap. It looks sweet and harmless, then snaps without warning.
Mawile smiles shyly to lure in the unwary. Behind its pleasant face is a stubborn will, and its jaws can bite through thick iron.
It now wields two great jaws, and each one hungers for a bite. It smiles sweetly and crushes anything that comes near.
In this form its power is doubled, and the fierce jaws shut with a mighty clang. Its looks are kind but its heart is cruel.
It eats iron ore and rails alike, and the metal builds its armor plating. Where trains run it can be found chewing the tracks.
Aron is a headstrong youngster that charges into trouble. It likes to sleep in mountain hollows with its plates tucked in.
It digs for ore in mountain slopes, and where it feeds, the ground may be left bare and scarred. Its steel hide is polished by constant rubbing on rock.
Lairon plods about with its heavy head lowered and rams anything that blocks its path. It drinks from clear mountain streams.
It defends its mountain territory fiercely, and if its armor is damaged it hurries to mend the scar with fresh ore. It tends the land it lives on.
Aggron's head and horns are mighty enough to splinter solid stone. After a landslide it clears the rubble away and plants new trees.
Its armor grows thick and heavy, and the horns spread like a wall. Nothing can dent it, and it holds its ground against anything.
In this form it has no weak points and takes no damage. It crashes into the foe like a falling cliff.
Snow can pile up on its head while it sits with its eyes closed, and it never brushes it off. A Meditite sneezes only once it has finished for the day.
A Meditite stretches its limbs into strange, slow poses as the sun rises. Each movement is held until its whole body trembles with effort.
It trains on narrow ledges where one wrong step would mean a long fall. A Medicham can balance on a single toe for most of an afternoon.
Medicham are said to train in pairs, each mirroring the other's movements exactly. Onlookers cannot tell which of the two is leading.
Its mind has been sharpened by meditation and its power has risen to new heights. It floats as it fights and its movement is perfectly composed.
In this form its arms are wrapped in a flowing energy. It strikes with calm precision and its focus never wavers.
It stores energy in its fur and discharges it with a crackle when it pounces. On dry days, its mane stands up in a wild burst.
Electrike races across the plains faster than a thrown ball, sparks flickering behind it. It tires if it cannot stretch its legs.
Lightning leaps from its mane when it gets angry, and storm clouds gather above it as it runs. It darts over the fields like a flash.
Manectric's glowing mane lights up a path at night. It races ahead of storms, scouting the way for its pack.
Its mane streams backward like a flowing cape of lightning. It races so fast that it leaves a trail of thunder.
In this form it is aggressive and bold. The blue fire of its mane lights up the night as it charges.
Small sparks pop between its paws whenever it is excited. It dashes to the side of any friend in trouble and waves its arms as if to cheer them up.
Plusle's red cheeks hum with a faint charge. It loves a crowd and will jump about at a festival, dropping little static shocks on anyone who pets it.
Its blue cheeks crackle when it is in high spirits. It is shyer than its look-alike, peeking at strangers from behind its trainer's legs.
Minun hops and claps for whoever it likes, and a handful of sparks trail its fingers. Alone, it sulks quietly in a corner.
On warm summer evenings its tail lights up, and swarms of them draw shapes across the sky. A few quick blinks can say a surprising amount.
Volbeat is drawn to the sweet smell of its partner and follows it around on soft nights. By day it rests in the reeds with its light dimmed.
It tends meadow flowers by night and sprinkles a scented dust over them. Its wings hum like a distant song as it lights its way.
Illumise is a gentle flyer that orders the dance of every glow in the field. Every lamp in the swarm follows its lead.
Its two flowers open and close with the sun. On cloudy days a Roselia hangs its head and refuses to move until the light returns.
It is fussy about where it grows and will walk for days to find the right soil. Gardens with a Roselia in them always seem to bloom more brightly.
Nearly everything it has is stomach, and it swallows scraps whole. A bit of fruit or a fallen berry vanishes in one gulp.
Gulpin sits with its mouth hanging open, humming gently to itself while it digests. A faint sour smell hangs around it.
Its huge mouth can stretch around a large tire and bite it out of shape. Every dribble of its slime stings the skin.
Swalot lumbers through the grass with its jaws parted and its two small arms swinging. It sleeps in the shade after a big meal.
A school can strip a drifting plank to splinters before it sinks. Its bite is out of all proportion to its length.
Carvanha waits near river mouths and rushes anything that splashes. Fishermen toss out chum to keep it away from their boats.
It swims at the speed of a speedboat and rams its targets with its pointed snout. The thick scales along its flank repel almost all attacks.
Sharpedo cruises far from shore and shows up when the sea is rough. Its fangs break off often, but new ones keep growing in.
Its jaws grow huge and strong enough to crunch through a ship's hull. It slices through the water with a terrifying grin.
In this form the spines on its back sharpen and it becomes even faster. It hunts without mercy.
When it takes in a great gulp of seawater, it swells like a ball and bounces across the waves. Children love to chase it on the beach.
Wailmer spouts a tall fountain from its blowhole to greet its pod. It eats huge piles of small fish every single day.
It is among the longest creatures in the world, and a whole pod seems like a moving island. Its call rolls across the ocean for miles.
Wailord is gentle and unhurried despite its bulk. Great flocks of birds ride on its back when it surfaces for air.
Magma burns inside its hump, but it is a dull, sluggish creature that is slow to notice danger. Dozing on warm rock suits it best.
When the weather turns cold, Numel curls up and its hump grows hard. It trudges up volcano slopes to graze on mineral-rich shrubs.
Twin humps on its back can erupt with molten rock when it is angry, and it must rest to cool them. Quakes are said to follow its footsteps.
Camerupt's body temperature climbs when it is upset, and the steam rising from its hump warns others to stand back.
The two humps on its back become a roaring volcano, and the magma inside can burst out any time. Its body is hotter than ever.
In this form it is as mighty as a mountain, and it carries a burning crater on its back. The ground melts under its feet.
It burns coal in its shell for fuel and puffs out thick black smoke when it wants to hide. Farmers keep a few to warm their barns in winter.
Torkoal digs shallow holes in the ground to nap in, and when it is startled it pulls its limbs inside and lets off a hiss of steam.
It bounces without stopping on its spring-like tail, because the beat of each hop keeps its small heart going. If it stops, it can grow weak.
Spoink carries a pearl on its head and treasures it above all else. It leaps along on every path in a cheerful rhythm.
Dancing helps it gather a strange energy, and the dark pearls set into its skin shine as it sways. Each step is slow and deliberate.
Grumpig sways in circles under the moon and seems to enjoy itself. Its stomping makes strange patterns in the dirt.
No two are marked alike, and the spots on its face give it a different expression each time. It sways in an unsteady lurching walk.
Spinda wanders in a dizzy zigzag as though lost, but somehow reaches its destination. Collectors like to compare their patterns.
It digs a funnel of loose sand and sits at the bottom with its great jaws open. Whatever slides down is its meal, and it can wait for days.
Trapinch has a huge head and tiny legs, and it walks with awkward little steps. In hot deserts it stays in its pit and keeps cool.
Its immature wings do not carry it far yet, but they thrum to make a ringing note. The sound confuses anyone who listens too closely.
Vibrava flaps at the edge of the desert, gaining strength. It leaves the burrow only on calm days when the sand is still.
Its wings stir up clouds of sand as it flies, and from the ground it looks like a shimmering green ghost in the dust. It is rarely seen.
Flygon's song floats over the dunes, and travelers in a sandstorm sometimes follow the sound to safety. It rests among dry rocks.
It lives where rain seldom falls and holds water in its prickly body. It enjoys hearing music and sways a little when a tune drifts by.
Cacnea likes to stand still at night and bask in the cool air. Careless hands that touch it pull back with a yelp.
At dusk it wanders the sands to follow tired travelers, waiting until they falter. In daytime it holds so still that it looks like a scarecrow.
Cacturne's body is mostly dry fibers and thorns, and it needs very little water. A pack will gather quietly under a full moon.
Its wings are so light that a strong gust can tumble it across a meadow. It rights itself with an indignant chirp and flies straight back.
Flocks of Swablu chirp in a soft chorus at sunrise, perched in neat rows along the branches. Each bird sings a slightly different note.
It soars on warm air rising out of the valleys, barely moving its wings. Hikers lying in mountain meadows sometimes realise that one of the clouds above is watching them.
It nests on high mountain ledges, building beds of feathers and moss. In stormy weather it shelters its young beneath its wide, downy wings.
Its wings become a dazzling cloud of pink and white. It sings in a sweet voice and floats like a drifting cloud.
In this form it is gentle and fair, and a soft light shines about it. Its song can put a whole valley at ease.
It tears into battle with claws spread wide, ruffling its white fur and showing its fierce red markings. It is quick to anger, and quick to leap.
Zangoose lives in grassy valleys and treats a certain snake as its lifelong rival. The two never pass without a scuffle.
Its tail ends in a blade that it sharpens against stones. It rears up and hisses when it spots anything that looks like its old rival.
Seviper slides through tall grass without a sound and strikes from cover. A scar across its body is a trophy of old fights.
It floats in the dead of night with a pale glow, and its power grows stronger when the moon is full. Locals say it fell from the sky long ago.
Lunatone's blank stare gives nothing away. It hovers in caves, and the more the moon waxes, the more restless it becomes.
It basks in sunshine and glows warmly when the sun is high. It is a patient, quiet traveler that spins slowly as it rests.
Solrock's rays can warm a cold cavern, and it floats toward any sunny spot. Some people say it came here from far beyond the sky.
It spends the winter dozing in the soft silt of a riverbed, its body slowed almost to a stop. The first warm days of spring wake it with a great appetite.
Young Barboach gather in the shallows where the water is warm, darting about in tight little groups. A passing shadow sends them all into the mud at once.
It surfaces only at dusk to gulp a breath of air, sending ripples across the whole pond. Its long whiskers trail behind it like weeds in the current.
An old Whiscash may live in the same pond for many decades. Villagers give them names and speak of them like respected neighbours.
It is tough enough to live in dirty ponds where nothing else can. Its sturdy pincers clamp onto an enemy and refuse to let go.
Corphish was brought in from overseas and spread quickly through the waterways. It will snap at a finger offered carelessly.
It claims a pond as its own and fights off anything that wanders in. Its claws are so strong they can snap a plank.
Crawdaunt is cranky and tends to lash out first. After a victory, it sheds its old shell and grows a bigger one.
It spins on its single foot and glides across the ground without a trace. Old ruins hold many of them, standing in rows.
Baltoy sleeps standing upright. In a gentle breeze it wobbles a bit, and if it tips it simply rights itself.
It was made long ago and has outlived its makers, and it seems to remember nothing. Strange beams shoot from its hands.
Claydol floats over ancient floors with its eyes unblinking. Scholars still debate what it is for.
It lived on the sea floor in ancient times and waited, rooted to a rock, for food to drift by. It has now come back from fossils.
Lileep's petal-like arms wave gently in the current. Its body is anchored to a stone while its mouth catches what the water brings.
It sways its long, flowing arms to catch fish, and its tentacles lash out at anything that grazes its anchor. It rarely moves around.
Cradily was once at home in warm shallows. Revived from a fossil, it still keeps close to the water.
Eight tiny claws drag it across the sea floor, and two larger ones scoop up prey. It was once a lively swimmer in shallow seas.
Anorith is tough but hesitant, and it curls its tail under when faced with something big. It is revived from an ancient stone.
It once walked on land and sea alike, and its armor shows many battle scars. The plates on its body are as hard as rock.
Armaldo swings its heavy claws and rarely misses. When angry, it rises on two legs and stands tall.
It hides among the weeds in the darkest corners of ponds and lakes and seldom comes out into open water. Few anglers have ever hooked one on purpose.
A Feebas drifts near the bottom and eats whatever sinks from above. It seems to favour certain stretches of water and to ignore the rest of a lake entirely.
Its long, shimmering body glides through deep lakes like a ribbon of light. Those who see one surface at sunset speak of it for the rest of their lives.
Milotic rest in the calmest part of a lake, their tails gently curled. The water around a resting Milotic is always perfectly clear.
Its body looks like a cloud and changes with the weather around it, becoming sunny, rainy or snowy. Each change is quick and complete.
Castform is delicate and drifts easily in the air. Weather watchers carry one along to check the forecast.
Under the bright sun it takes on a fiery form, and a blaze burns on its body. The heat makes it cheerful and bold.
A hot, glowing Castform that shines like a small sun. It dances in the light and warms the air around it.
In the rain it becomes a gray cloud with raindrops dripping from its body. It hums a quiet song as it floats along.
A damp, bluish Castform that thrives on a downpour. It drifts about with a sleepy smile as the rain falls.
In a snowfall it turns white and frosty, and small flakes drift around it. It moves slowly in the cold, like a drifting snowball.
A pale, chilly Castform that looks like a lump of snow. It shivers a little as it floats through the freezing air.
It changes its coloring to match its surroundings and vanishes from sight. The only part that stays is the zigzag mark on its belly.
Kecleon sneaks up on insects while hidden, then flicks out its long tongue. When it is surprised, it goes red with embarrassment.
It drifts toward dark houses and feeds on the gloomy feelings of the people inside. Its single horn is said to attract such feelings.
Shuppet hides in the shadows and peers from behind curtains. A good laugh sends it scurrying away.
It is a discarded plaything that has come alive, and it searches for the child who threw it away. Its mouth is held shut by a zipper.
Banette is a restless wanderer that moves at night. If it is hugged and treated well, its anger can melt away.
The zipper on its mouth comes undone and its grudges pour out. It floats in the dark with a hateful stare.
In this form it has grown big and fierce. A curse swirls in the air around it, and it chases down the one who wronged it.
It drifts between gravestones at dusk, its single red eye swinging from side to side. Its body makes no sound at all as it moves.
A Duskull loves to tease, slipping behind people and then vanishing when they turn. It giggles faintly from somewhere out of sight.
It drifts silently through forests at night, beckoning with its long grey arms. Travellers who see the gesture are wise to walk on without looking back.
A Dusclops moves at a slow, unhurried pace and never seems to tire. Its single eye glows dimly in the dark, the only sign that it is there.
Its deep, slow calls echo through the canopy at dawn, answered by others far away. A Tropius may stand munching leaves in the same grove for weeks.
The bunches of fruit on its neck ripen in summer, giving off a sweet smell that attracts other Pokémon. It is happy to share them with those it trusts.
Its chiming body rings softly with every gust, and mountain villagers find the sound comforting on long winter nights. Each Chimecho has a tone of its own.
A Chimecho floats in the cold air of high slopes, drifting slowly on the breeze. Its call carries far across the valleys on quiet evenings.
Its body is shaped like a delicate bell, and a pure chime rings out as it floats. The sound is so clear that it calms a whole room.
In this form it has grown icy and fine. Its song is a high, thin ringing that can cut through steel.
Its white fur blends into snowfields, and only the dark blade of its horn gives it away. It moves along ridgelines in long, silent strides.
An Absol keeps watch from high crags for hours without moving. Mountain folk who once feared it now leave food on the rocks where it rests.
Wings of white fur sprout from its back, and it glides over the mountain peaks. It brings word of the dangers to come.
In this form it is graceful and calm. It soars in the sky and watches over those it wants to warn.
A shadowy mane streams behind it, and its eyes glow with a cold purple light. It moves like a ghost through the dusk and leaves a shiver in its wake.
In this form its blade is long and thin, and it slashes with chilling skill. It appears before disasters, and its silent step has a haunting weight.
It likes to huddle with others in quiet places, and it gets cross if it is left alone. Its tail wags when it is pleased.
Wynaut hops up and down to stay warm, and it grins at nearly everyone. It sticks together with its fellows in dark caves.
Its body is always cold to the touch, and it shivers happily on freezing days. A Snorunt that wanders somewhere warm sits in the shade and sulks.
A Snorunt likes to burrow into snowdrifts with only its pointed head poking out, watching the world go by. Its eyes glint like two dark pebbles in the white.
It drifts through frozen caves with its great jaw hanging open, and the walls glisten with fresh frost as it passes. Its roar cracks icicles from the ceiling.
A Glalie rests for weeks in the coldest chamber it can find, hardly moving at all. Cavers who mistake it for a boulder of ice get a nasty fright.
Its jaw widens into a gaping maw, and its body turns as hard as ice at the bottom of a glacier. A freezing breath spills from its mouth.
In this form it swallows a foe whole and freezes it in an instant. The air around it fills with glittering shards of frost.
It is round enough to roll along the ice, and it claps its flippers together for joy. Its fur is thick and keeps out the cold.
Spheal likes to bob in icy water and flick drops at passersby. A rolling Spheal will follow a family down a snowy hill.
It plays by balancing things on its nose, and it licks the object to learn what it is. It can keep a ball in the air for ages.
Sealeo hunts through cracks in the ice. The fat on its body is thick and keeps it comfortable even in deep frost.
Its long tusks can smash through thick ice, and its blubber makes it nearly impervious to the cold. It leads its family through frozen seas.
Walrein is protective of its young and charges at anything that comes close. It stays calm and quiet at other times.
It rests deep underwater inside a hard shell, which snaps shut at the slightest threat. A gem is said to form within it as it ages.
Clamperl sits in a bed of sand and rarely opens up. It grows a precious stone, slowly, over many years.
Its tail looks like a small fish, and it uses it to lure prey out of the murk far below. Whatever follows the lure never sees the long body behind it.
Huntail slips through narrow cracks in sunken wrecks, its long body bending to fit wherever the fish are hiding. It swallows its meal whole.
It uses its slender mouth like a straw to drink what lies inside a small creature's shell. Its pink body glows faintly beneath the waves.
Gorebyss swims through warm, sunny seas, gliding with an elegant, easy motion. The color of its body fades after it feeds.
It has lived on the deep sea floor for ages with little change. Its scaly body resists the crushing weight of the water.
Relicanth moves little and eats slowly, and scientists value it for what it shows about the distant past.
Its body is shaped like a heart, and couples of sailors take it as a lucky sign to see two swimming side by side. It darts away at the first splash.
Luvdisc keeps to warm, shallow waters and swims in tidy pairs. Small and quick, it slips between the coral without a ripple.
It dreams of flying and leaps from cliffs again and again, only to tumble and bruise its hard head. It never seems to learn from the falls.
Bagon butts its head against boulders to wear them down. Its stubborn temper makes it hard to train, but it is loyal in the end.
A shell of heavy plates covers its body, and it hides in a cave for long stretches while it changes inside. Nothing it meets can scratch it.
Shelgon rarely moves and eats little. Under its armor, something large is being built piece by piece.
At last its wish has come true and it soars on great wings, with a fierce rage that burns whenever it is cornered. It swoops down on anything below.
Salamence flies in tight loops and spits fire in the air in sheer joy of flying. Its roar echoes over the peaks.
Its wings fuse into a single great sail, and it flies faster than it ever did before. It tears across the sky with a howl of delight.
In this form it is wild and fierce. It dives at a foe and spins like a storm, and the sound of its flight can shatter glass.
Its body is a heavy ball of iron with a single red eye. It floats using magnetism and clusters of them cling together for company.
Beldum rests in the air with its claws folded in. When it spots something, it stares for a long time before making a move.
Two Beldum have fused together by magnetism, and the new body is bigger, heavier and smarter. It floats with its claws tucked up against its chest.
Metang thinks by combining the minds of its two halves. It flies in absolute silence, trailing a faint hum.
Four legs, four brains and a crushing weight: it solves problems faster than a computer. It pins down prey under one foot and finishes it with another.
Metagross hovers above ground and drops onto foes like a falling anvil. It is coolly efficient and rarely shows any emotion.
Its four legs grow into great claws and its body gains a long, armored face. It calculates every move and crushes a foe with ease.
In this form its brains work as one and its mind is faster than a machine. Each stomp of its legs makes the earth shake.
An ancient figure built entirely from stones and boulders. When damaged, it repairs itself with fresh rocks gathered from around it.
Regirock sleeps in a cavern deep underground and wakes only to answer a call. A single, faint glow shines from its face.
Frost that never thaws forms the whole of its body, cold enough to turn the air around it into glittering dust. Fire hardly scratches it.
Regice stands motionless in a frigid hall. A thin fog of frost curls from its shoulders and drifts along the floor.
Legend holds that its frame was forged deep under the ground from a metal harder than any other. Nothing known can pierce it.
Registeel sits silent in a chamber, with a line of lights across its face. It is thought to be an ancient guardian.
It is clever and can understand human speech. It folds its wings to become nearly invisible and glides low over the waves.
Latias is gentle and shy, and it is said to grow close to those it trusts. It flies faster than a jet when it wants to.
Its wings spread wide like a jet and its body gleams like a pearl. It can read a person's heart and share its thoughts with them.
In this form it is graceful and quick, and it spins through the air in a streak of red. Its soft voice is a comfort to those in need.
It can link its mind with people and show them pictures from far away. It is a swift, proud flyer that rarely lands.
Latios tucks its arms in as it speeds across the sky. It keeps a close eye on its sibling from a distance.
Its wings sweep back like the blade of a jet, and it flies at a speed that cannot be followed. It shows others scenes from far away.
In this form it is cool and focused. It dives with a roar of wind, and its powerful mind overwhelms foes in a flash.
Legends say it enlarged the oceans by calling down storms for ages. It sleeps in the deepest trench, and rain falls when it stirs.
Kyogre's markings glow when it uses its power. Its mighty form fills the whole sea whenever it wakes.
It returns to the form it had at the dawn of time, with glowing lines on its body. A deluge pours from the sky and the sea swells over the land.
In this form it calls up endless rain and turns the world into one great ocean. Its roar is the sound of the tide coming in.
It is said to have raised the land itself and dried the earth with scorching heat. It sleeps in a molten pit beneath a volcano.
Groudon's red armor sheds burning dust, and its mighty claws can tear the ground apart. Droughts follow in its wake.
It takes the form it had in the beginning, with blazing lines across its armor. The sun beats down and the land cracks and burns.
In this form it brings a terrible drought and a scorching heat. The earth turns to magma under its feet.
It has lived for ages in the ozone layer, high above the clouds, and is almost never seen from the ground. It eats only the water and dust of the sky.
Rayquaza is said to calm the two great titans of land and sea when they clash. Its long body glides through the air like a green ribbon.
It stretches out as long as a tower and fills the sky with golden light. It rises above the clouds and the ozone swirls around it.
In this form it tames the storms between the land and the sea. Its unleashed power is so great that the air itself seems to tear.
It sleeps for a thousand years and wakes for a short week when the pure of heart sing to it. A third eye opens on its belly when it is time to grant a wish.
Jirachi wears small paper strips on its head that are said to carry wishes. When it dozes, it tucks itself into a ball.
A strange life form that came from a virus out in space, it can shift its shape to fight or defend. The crystal in its chest is its core.
Deoxys fires beams of light from the crystal, and its body takes on different forms in an instant. It was last seen after a meteor fell.
It trades its guard for might, and its body sharpens into a lean frame. It hurls itself at a foe with a blast of power.
In this form it is a fierce and bold fighter. Its crystal glows bright as it strikes with all of its strength.
It forms a hard shell of crystal over its body, and it stands firm against any strike. A calm, steady glow shines from its core.
In this form it plants its feet and shrugs off blow after blow. Its barrier shimmers as it holds the line.
Its body is long and slim, and it zips about in a blur. It is so fast that it seems to be in two places at once.
In this form it flits from one spot to another and strikes before the foe can react. Its tentacles trail behind like streamers.
It likes to nap in patches of sunlight on the forest floor, its shell tilted toward the light. It grumbles softly whenever a cloud passes over.
Turtwig nibble on the tender tips of ferns and moss. They are slow walkers, but they plod on for hours without stopping once they have chosen a direction.
The shrubs on its shell flower in late spring, and small bird Pokémon often perch among them. Grotle seem to enjoy the company and walk especially carefully that season.
A Grotle digs its feet into soft earth to drink from the damp soil beneath. It can tell good ground from poor by the taste alone.
The tree on its back drops its leaves every autumn, and they rot down to feed the moss on its shell. In spring new shoots sprout between its plates.
Its footsteps are slow and heavy, and the ground trembles faintly with each one. A Torterra rarely hurries, but nothing can push it aside once it has set off.
Young Chimchar race each other to the top of every boulder they find, shrieking with glee. The loser has to fetch berries for the winner.
It holds its flaming tail close when it eats, using the heat to toast hard nuts until they crack. A Chimchar's den smells of roasted shells.
It practises its leaps along riverbeds, springing from stone to stone without wetting a toe. A misstep into cold water leaves it hissing and steaming.
The blue and gold markings on its face grow bolder as it matures. Monferno compare them in noisy displays, each trying to look the most impressive.
It sits on high peaks at dusk, the fire on its head burning low and steady. Villagers below take the small glow on the summit as a sign of fair weather.
It trains alone on mountain peaks, repeating the same sequence of strikes until it can perform them with its eyes closed. Its footwork is light and swift.
It waddles along icy shores with its chest puffed out and its flippers held stiffly at its sides. It squawks sharply at anything that blocks its way.
It often stands at the water's edge staring out to sea, as if it were waiting for something. Piplup chicks huddle together in a tight ring on stormy nights.
Its flippers have sharpened edges, and it practises swiping at floating ice to keep them keen. It is stubborn and rarely asks for help.
A Prinplup keeps a careful eye on its reflection in tide pools and smooths its feathers whenever they are ruffled. It is proud of its neat appearance.
It dives deep beneath the ice to hunt, steering with sweeps of its stiff wings. It can stay below for a long time before it bursts back to the surface.
It stands on the highest rock of the shore to survey its stretch of coast. Smaller water Pokémon gather in the shelter of its territory.
It hops along the ground with its head bobbing at every step, flicking over leaves in search of a meal. A Starly on its own is easily frightened.
Starly gather on rooftops and fences at dusk and bicker loudly over the best spots. Each evening the same birds return to the same perches.
It flies in tight formations over open country, turning sharply in perfect unison. Watchers below see what looks like a single great wave of wings.
Its plumage grows darker and glossier as it matures. A Staravia preens for a long time after rain, combing each feather until it shines.
It dives on prey from a great height, folding its wings close to its body. The rush of air as it pulls up can knock a hat clean off a passer-by.
Pairs of Staraptor claim a stretch of cliff and patrol it in wide circles every morning. Their shrill calls carry for kilometres when an intruder crosses the line.
Its crest sweeps up like a crown and its wings grow broad and strong. It dives at a target with a blow that can snap a thick tree.
In this form it flies with fierce abandon and takes on any rival. It dives without hesitation, no matter how much bigger the foe.
It ambles through meadows chewing on grass stems, its round body swaying from side to side. A Bidoof can keep the same plodding pace from dawn to dusk.
Bidoof families share long stretches of riverbank without any quarrelling. Their single cheerful squeak serves for everything from a greeting to a warning.
Its broad, flat tail makes a loud slap on the water when it senses danger. Every Bibarel within earshot dives at once.
It works through the night and rests by day, dozing on its back in the shallows. Its front teeth are stained orange from all the bark it chews.
It hides in long grass during the day and comes out to chirp in the evening. Its feelers wave slowly as it listens for others of its kind.
Kricketot nibble on dewy grass and are easily startled. They spring away in short, clumsy hops that make their round bodies wobble.
On summer nights it plays a long, rising tune that carries over the fields. Its music grows faster as the night grows warmer.
A Kricketune perches on a single tall stem to perform, and rivals answer from neighbouring stems. Farmers fall asleep to their duets every summer.
Its fur crackles with static when it is excited, and sparks fly when it shakes itself. Young Shinx play by pouncing on one another in the grass.
It rubs its cheek against things it likes, leaving a faint tingle behind. A Shinx that trusts its trainer greets them by rubbing against their legs.
It patrols the edge of its territory each dawn and marks it with long scratches on tree bark. Its fur bristles at any unfamiliar scent.
Luxio hunt in pairs, one driving prey while the other lies in wait. They communicate with low rumbles that are almost too deep to hear.
Its golden eyes glow in the dark, and it watches from the shadows before moving. A Luxray can wait without blinking for an astonishingly long time.
It lies on high rocks overlooking the plains, its black mane stirring in the breeze. Lesser Pokémon give it a wide berth when it comes down to drink.
Its tight green bud is soft to the touch and smells faintly of spring. A Budew tucks its bud under its leaves when it is caught in the rain.
Budew gather in sunny hollows in great numbers. When one of them sneezes, a puff of yellow dust drifts across the whole patch.
Each of its bouquets has a scent of its own, one sweet and one sharp. It waves the sweet one at friends and the sharp one at anything it dislikes.
A Roserade tends a patch of wild roses as if it were a garden, plucking weeds and shooing away pests. It is fiercely protective of its blooms.
It paws the ground and snorts before every charge, giving fair warning to anything in its way. Its eyes water after a collision, but it never backs down.
Cranidos was brought back from a fossil, and it has no fear of anything. It will test its head against any creature, no matter how much larger.
It lowers its head and runs at full speed, and the crash can be heard for miles. A Rampardos that has charged a cliff often leaves a hollow in the rock.
A Rampardos that is not charging is usually eating, stripping leaves from low trees with its blunt teeth. It pays little attention to anything else.
Its broad face is cool to the touch and smooth as river stone. Shieldon spend the warm part of the day dozing with their faces pressed against shady rocks.
It shuffles about on short legs and moves in brief bursts between rests. Brought back from a fossil, it took to modern berries without any fuss.
Its great face is pitted and scratched from ages of rubbing against rock walls. It moves slowly and deliberately, as if every step had been thought through.
A Bastiodon sleeps standing beneath an overhang, its head lowered almost to the ground. Moss sometimes grows in the ridges of its face.
Its cloak can be leaves, sand or scraps of cloth, and it seems to pick each piece with great care, turning it over before tucking it in.
It hangs quietly from branches and walls, swaying in the breeze. A Burmy without its cloak is so shy that it curls up and refuses to move.
It wraps itself in a cloak of sand and pebbles and tries to blend in with the ground. The cloak rattles faintly when it moves.
This Burmy lives in a dry spot and covers itself in dust and grit. The cloak is rough to the touch and shields it from the sun.
It builds a cloak out of scraps, bits of paper and bright rubbish. The odd collection rustles and crackles as it creeps about.
This Burmy lives near towns and collects what people throw away. Its outfit is a patchwork that no two share.
A Wormadam is a homebody that rarely strays more than a short walk from where it was born. It knows every branch and stone of its patch.
It spends its days hanging still from a branch or a wall, and few notice it until it moves. When it does, it sways forward in small, careful lurches.
It wears a cloak of hardened earth, and its sturdy body tunnels easily into the soil. The cloak is as dry as a desert.
This Wormadam lives in a place where the ground is bare. It burrows to escape the heat and tends to its sandy coat.
Its cloak is built out of scrap metal and old parts. It rattles and clanks as it moves along, and it is tough as nails.
This Wormadam makes use of what it finds. A fine lining of steel shields it from harm, and it hums to itself as it works.
Its wings carry dark eyespots that seem to watch from the shadows. Mothim sometimes follow lantern light for a long way before losing interest.
It never settles anywhere for long, wandering the woods from dusk until dawn. Its wingbeats are so soft that it can land on a sleeping face without waking it.
A moth of dusty wings that flutters low over the ground. It follows the scent of nectar across dry plains.
It remembers the cloak it wore as a larva and keeps a faint trace of sand on its wings. It flies in lazy loops.
A moth with a ragged, patched look that clings to the edge of the city. It darts after the scent of sweet things in the trash.
Its wings still carry the bright colors of the scraps it once wore. It slips through narrow gaps and flutters at night around lights.
Three of them share one body, and they argue constantly about which way to fly. The one on the bottom usually gets its way, since it does the most work.
Combee from the same hive fly in identical loops, like dancers following a routine. A Combee that gets lost circles slowly until it hears the hive's hum.
It rarely flies far, keeping to a perch near the hive's entrance where it can watch everything that comes and goes. Its wings hum with a deep, steady note.
A Vespiquen's colony may live in the same hollow tree for generations. Beekeepers say the honey from such a tree tastes faintly of wildflowers.
It darts up and down tree trunks in a blur, its tail crackling with sparks. A Pachirisu that is startled leaves a trail of static behind it.
It spends autumn dashing about with its cheeks stuffed full, getting ready for the cold. In winter a Pachirisu sleeps curled in its own tail like a blanket.
Its curiosity often brings it close to boats, where it watches the crew with bright eyes before vanishing in a swirl of bubbles.
It loves to splash anyone standing on the shore and then dart away before they can splash back. Buizel play this game for hours on warm afternoons.
It hunts in swift dashes through harbour waters, turning so sharply that fish rarely see it coming. It eats its catch floating on its back.
Floatzel are fond of people and often follow ferries for miles, leaping beside the bow. Sailors toss them a fish for luck.
It clings to low branches in the sun, swinging gently from its stem like a ripe fruit. Its red skin darkens as the summer goes on.
Cherubi often nod off in warm afternoon light and wake with a start when a breeze swings them. They squeak indignantly before settling down again.
On dull days it keeps its petals wrapped tightly around itself and barely moves. It stays hunched and gloomy until the clouds clear.
Once the sun breaks through, it twirls about the clearing scattering pink petals. Travellers who walk through such a shower are said to have a lucky day.
When the sun shines bright, it opens its petals and blooms into a radiant flower. Its face shines with delight and it dances in the light.
In the warm light, it is cheerful and full of energy. Its petals glow a bright pink as it twirls about.
It slides over wet rocks at the tide line, leaving a glistening trail behind it. A Shellos can cling to a rock so firmly that the waves cannot wash it off.
After a storm, children hunt for Shellos in the tide pools and carry them gently back to deeper water. They squirm and wriggle the whole way.
A sea slug of the eastern waters that has a bright blue body. It slides across the shore and leaves a trail of slime.
This Shellos is shaped by the cold currents of the east sea. It hides in a tidal pool and clings to the rocks.
It glides slowly across sandy seabeds, grazing on the tiny plants that grow there. It can stretch its body to reach into narrow gaps between rocks.
When the tide goes out, a Gastrodon simply waits on the wet sand for it to come back, unbothered by the gulls circling overhead.
A big, bluish sea slug of the east that crawls over the rocks. The leaves on its back sway as it moves.
This Gastrodon lives in the cool water of an eastern shore. It is calm and lazy and sleeps in the sun.
It hangs from high branches by one tail and swings to the next tree in a long, looping arc. Its arms dangle loosely as it goes, almost forgotten.
Ambipom gather in noisy groups at the tops of trees and play elaborate games of catch with nuts. Anyone walking below is advised to keep their head covered.
It appears most often at dusk, bobbing slowly along hedgerows at head height. The string beneath it sways even when there is no wind.
A Drifloon that is pricked by a thorn lets out a long, mournful wheeze but comes to no harm. By the next evening it is round and full again.
It hangs in the air above quiet fields for hours, turning slowly in the breeze. Its striped arms trail beneath it like ribbons.
A Drifblim's body swells and shrinks with the temperature, so it floats higher on hot afternoons and lower on cool mornings. In frost it barely leaves the ground.
It hops through woodland clearings with its ears flopping at each bound. Buneary greet one another by tapping their fluffy paws together.
Buneary nibble on clover and soft grasses, keeping close to the shelter of bushes. A sudden noise sends them diving into their burrows.
It grooms its long ears with great care, combing the soft fur with its paws. A Lopunny with tangled fur will not rest until it is smooth again.
Its powerful legs let it bound across meadows in long, floating leaps. Lopunny race one another at dawn simply for the joy of it.
Its fur turns sleek and its ears grow tall. It leaps and kicks with a speed that makes it hard to keep in sight.
In this form it is nimble and bold. A graceful kick from its long legs can knock a foe flat.
It drifts through the darkest parts of old forests, its ragged hem trailing like a cape. The jewels around its neck catch the faintest light.
A Mismagius is said to keep a hoard of lost trinkets hidden in a hollow tree. Things that go missing in villages near the woods sometimes turn up there.
It perches in the tallest dead tree of a forest and surveys the land below with half-closed eyes. Its hat-like crest never seems to ruffle in the wind.
A Honchkrow eats slowly and with great dignity, taking one small bite at a time. It seems to consider hurrying beneath it.
It struts through town with its nose in the air and stops only for the sunniest windowsills. Shopkeepers know it by name and leave a saucer out.
It can leap onto a high wall from a standing start and land without a sound. It is fussy about its food and turns its nose up at anything stale.
It lounges in the warmest spot it can find and glares at anything that comes near. A Purugly's purr is deep enough to rattle a windowpane.
It eats a great deal and moves as little as possible. When it does decide to move, it waddles with a slow, rolling swagger.
It loves to be carried in a pocket or a hood and peeks out at everything that passes. A Chingling left on its own soon goes looking for company.
The cord on its head flutters in the slightest breeze. Young Chingling tug at one another's cords in play until an elder chimes them back into line.
It digs its den under hedges and fallen logs at the edge of fields. Farmers who hear it scratching at night leave the barn door firmly shut.
A Stunky raises its bushy tail high and stamps its front feet as a warning. Most wise creatures back away long before it has to do anything more.
It ambles across open country at night without hurrying, since few would dare to bother it. Its striped tail sways like a banner as it walks.
A Skuntank keeps its den neat and tidy and buries anything left over from its meals far away. Its fur has a faint scent of crushed herbs when it is calm.
It floats slowly through dim caves, turning in place as it drifts. Its bronze face catches the light of a lantern and flashes it back across the walls.
A Bronzor that bumps into a rock gives a dull clang and spins away. Its metal surface never rusts, however damp the cave where it rests.
It hangs motionless in the middle of large caverns for weeks on end. A deep hum rises from inside its body that cavers feel in their chests before they hear it.
The arms on its sides sway gently when it is about to move. A Bronzong is patient beyond measure and can wait out a whole winter in one spot.
It shuffles from rock to rock on stony hillsides, trying hard to look like a potted plant. Its three green balls tremble whenever it is startled.
A Bonsly follows older Sudowoodo about and copies the way they stand stock still. It is not yet very good at it and fidgets after a minute or two.
It waddles behind people in the street with a very serious look on its face. When they turn round, it freezes and pretends to be looking at the sky.
The round red tip of its nose bounces as it walks. A Mime Jr. practises silly faces in shop windows and claps for itself when it pulls a good one.
It toddles about in a pink skirt of fluff and is happiest in busy rooms full of people. It hums a cheerful little tune when it is given a hug.
A Happiny loves to sit with anyone who looks unwell and pat their hand. Nurses say it seems to know which patients need company the most.
Its feathers come in bright bands of colour that look freshly painted. A Chatot preens each band in turn, always in the same order, before it will fly.
A Chatot fusses over its glossy feathers after every rain shower. It flies only short hops from tree to tree, chattering with each landing.
Its swirling body of purple wisps never stays the same shape for long. The green marks within it shift about, and no two sketches of one ever match.
A Spiritomb can stay hidden in one spot for years without moving. Travellers who walk past at night feel a chill run up their backs.
It is a messy eater and leaves crumbs of rock and bone all over the cave floor. A Gible guards these scraps as if they were treasure.
Its big jaw is far too heavy for its stubby legs, so it often trips as it runs. It simply snaps at the ground and keeps going.
It digs long tunnels through sandy caves using the claws on its arms. The tunnels are wide enough that a person could crawl through them.
A Gabite sheds its old scales as it grows, leaving them scattered about the cave floor. Hikers who find a shed scale often keep it as a lucky charm.
It rushes out of caves in sudden bursts and tears across the ground faster than the eye can follow. Its fins whistle loudly through the air.
A Garchomp claims a whole cave system as its own and patrols it every day. Its scales gleam blue-grey in the light from the cave mouth.
Its arms grow into great blades and its body lengthens. It flies low at a crushing speed and tears open the ground as it goes.
In this form it is wilder and more bloodthirsty. Its wings cut the air like knives, and sandstorms whip up in its wake.
It takes on a dark, glossy shell and its eyes burn with a strange light. Its long wings hum as it floats just above the ground.
In this form it is cold and eerie, and it drifts without a sound. A silent shadow, it glides down on prey from the sky.
It waddles along the forest floor searching for anything that smells sweet. A Munchlax will happily nap right next to the bush it has just stripped bare.
Its round belly drags along the ground when it sits down to eat. Campers learn to keep their bags hung high once one has visited.
It spars with its parents from a very young age, copying each stance with great care. A Riolu that lands a hit cheers so loudly it forgets to dodge the next.
