A Riolu is curious about everything and sniffs at new things carefully before it touches them. It quickly learns to recognise the people it meets every day.
It meditates on high mountain ledges with its eyes closed, quite still for hours. The black appendages on its head twitch gently as it concentrates.
A Lucario moves with calm, measured steps and wastes no motion in battle. It holds a deep respect for any trainer who keeps their word.
Its aura is so strong that it bursts out in streaming tendrils from its head. It senses everything around it and fights with total focus.
In this form it is powerful and calm. It reads the flow of battle and strikes in a quick succession of blows.
It is wrapped in a shining coat of aura, and its eyes glow a bright blue. It stands as still as a statue, then moves in a flash.
In this form its senses sharpen to a razor's edge. It guards its friends with a shield of its own energy.
It wallows in warm sand with only its eyes and nostrils showing above the surface. Its stubby legs make it a slow walker on firm ground.
Hippopotas live in herds that travel together across dry lands. The young walk in the middle of the herd, kept safe by the larger ones around them.
Its wide jaws can open far enough to swallow a whole bush in one bite. It plods slowly across the desert and stops to rest only at sundown.
A Hippowdon yawns hugely in the midday sun, then rolls over in the sand and dozes. It is surprisingly gentle with its herd's young.
It crawls slowly across dry ground with its tail curled up over its back. Its claws click quietly against the stones as it walks.
A Skorupi cleans its tail claws carefully after every meal. Young ones cling to their mother's back until they are big enough to walk on their own.
Its heavy armour plates slide over one another as it walks, and grit that works between them is ground into fine powder. It is a patient and thorough fighter.
A Drapion's rattling armour can be heard long before it comes into view. It defends its territory with fierce determination against any rival.
It sits on rocks beside marshes making a low, gurgling croak. A Croagunk will grin at anyone who passes, but it is hard to tell what it means by it.
It leaps from mud bank to mud bank with surprising speed. Croagunk often gather in groups at the water's edge to soak in the shallows.
It wades through swamps up to its chest and seldom makes a sound. It squats for hours on a favourite stump, its yellow eyes half closed.
A Toxicroak trains its strikes against reeds and thin trees until they snap. It keeps its knuckles tucked in when it is relaxed.
Its jaws snap shut with a loud clack, and the sound carries a long way across the swamp. It spends the day swinging lazily from branch to branch.
A Carnivine can sense a change in the weather through its leaves and folds them up before a storm. Its bright jaws are easy to spot among the grey moss.
Its fins ripple like ribbons as it swims in shallow coastal waters. Shoals of Finneon glide past rocky shores in the early morning light.
A Finneon darts quickly between the strands of seaweed in rock pools. It is a playful swimmer and loves to race the shadows of passing boats.
It swims with long, slow sweeps of its four tail fins, as graceful as a dancer. A Lumineon seldom chases anything and seems content to drift.
Pairs of Lumineon swim side by side for life and are rarely seen apart. When one rests, the other circles above it until it wakes.
It skims just under the waves in warm seas, flapping its wide fins in a lazy rhythm. Schools of Mantyke play together in the wake of boats.
A Mantyke rests on the sandy bottom when it is tired, its body flat against the seabed. Fishermen sometimes spot its antennae poking up from the sand.
It stands among the pine trees on snowy slopes and is almost impossible to pick out. Snow gathers on its head like a little white cap.
Snover huddle together on the coldest nights to keep their berries from freezing solid. By morning the group is buried under a single mound of snow.
It stomps through drifts on heavy feet, leaving prints as wide as a cartwheel. Climbers have mistaken a standing Abomasnow for a snow-laden fir.
An Abomasnow is shy despite its size and backs away from strangers. It is fond of children, though, and will let them climb its shaggy arms.
Its body grows broad and thick, and it kicks up a blizzard that stretches across the mountain. It is silent and slow but unstoppable.
In this form it is a towering snowman with a fierce glare. Its footsteps shake the ice and its breath turns the air to snow.
It races through snowy forests at night, slipping between the trees without a sound. Its long claws leave deep, clean cuts in the ice.
A Weavile is clever and impatient. It sharpens its claws on icy rocks every evening, and the scraping sound carries far through the frozen woods.
It hovers over power stations and factories, drawn by the hum of machines. Its three units turn slowly, each one tracking a different direction.
A Magnezone's antenna crackles with static when a storm is near. It often floats for hours above an electrical tower without moving at all.
It sits down wherever it pleases and refuses to budge until it feels like moving. Trainers have waited half a day for one to get up from a doorway.
Its round belly is soft and pink, and it pats it happily after a big meal. It is slow and good-natured, and rarely loses its temper.
Its body is heavy enough to sink into soft ground, so it keeps to rock and hard earth. Bridges creak and groan whenever a Rhyperior crosses them.
A Rhyperior charges with its head down and its drill spinning. It is hard to stop once started and often runs far past its target before it can turn.
Its tangle of vines sways and rustles as it walks through thick jungles. Small Pokémon sometimes hide among its vines when it is resting.
A Tangrowth stretches its vine arms toward sunlight in the morning. It sits for hours in clearings, soaking up the warmth on its leaves.
It loves storms and stands on hilltops to watch the lightning, roaring with delight at every flash. Thunder never seems to frighten it in the least.
An Electivire beats its chest when it is excited, sending bursts of light from its body. Its tail cables twitch and spark constantly.
It stands in hot springs for hours, the water boiling round its legs. Its body glows bright orange when it is ready for battle.
A Magmortar's arm cannons smoke gently after it has been fighting. Its skin feels as hot as a fresh coal from the fire.
It glides gracefully over open fields with its wide white wings spread. A Togekiss lands softly enough that it barely bends the grass beneath it.
A Togekiss takes in orphaned bird Pokémon and raises them in its nest until they can fly. It is gentle with every living thing it meets.
It zips over ponds and marshes in sudden bursts of speed, its wings humming loudly. Reeds sway and ripple in its wake long after it has passed.
A Yanmega rests on tall reeds in the heat of the day, its wings spread flat. It guards its favourite pond from every other Yanmega.
Its ears and tail are shaped like broad leaves and curl up at the edges when the air is dry. It drinks dew from flowers in the early morning.
A Leafeon sleeps curled among the roots of old trees. Its fur is soft but bristles like grass when something frightens it.
It lives in snowy places and loves to roll in fresh powder. Its pale blue fur sparkles like frost in the morning light.
A Glaceon's paws leave tiny frosted prints on stone, even on warm days. It prefers to rest on cold rocks, even in the middle of summer.
It rides warm air rising out of canyons, steering with its long tail. A Gliscor can stay aloft for hours, circling over the same ridge.
A Gliscor grooms its wing membranes carefully, pulling out thorns and burrs with its fangs. Its large eyes glint in the dark as it watches over its territory.
It lumbers through blizzards, its shaggy fur coated with snow and ice. Herds of Mamoswine can travel for days without stopping to rest.
A Mamoswine's tusks curve far ahead of its face and can split thick ice with a single push. The young follow closely behind the elders.
It jerks and twitches as it floats, its movements never quite smooth. Its eyes flicker as if it were reading something nobody else can see.
A Porygon-Z sometimes stops in mid-air and spins in place for no reason anyone can tell. Its makers are still unsure what it is thinking.
It stands with its arms held ready, the blades along them gleaming. A Gallade studies an opponent in silence for a long time before it moves.
It practises slow, careful forms in quiet courtyards at dawn. A Gallade never draws its blades against those who cannot defend themselves.
Its elbow blades grow long, and it fights like a noble knight. It senses the heart of a foe and strikes with great precision.
In this form it wears a flowing white cape and a graceful poise. It will draw its blade in defense of the weak.
It glides slowly through caves, its great moustache bristling with iron filings. Small pebbles cling to its body wherever it has been resting.
A Probopass rarely moves quickly. Hikers lost underground have followed its slow trail along the tunnels to find their way out.
It drifts through dark forests at night, its single eye glowing faintly. Its large hands can reach out and pass right through the trees as if they were not there.
A Dusknoir hums low, droning notes as it floats. Those who hear the sound feel a cold chill run down their backs.
It drifts down snowy slopes in silence, its body pale as moonlight. Travellers caught in blizzards sometimes glimpse it watching them from the swirling snow.
A Froslass is said to dance alone on frozen lakes when the moon is bright. Its sleeves trail behind it like streamers of mist.
Its icy robe flares wide and its eyes burn with a pale blue flame. It glides over the snow, and its chill is felt from afar.
In this form it is colder and taller than before. A frozen mist trails behind as it stalks through the blizzard.
It zips about in short bursts, leaving a faint smell of a thunderstorm in the air. A Rotom stops dead whenever it hears music and sways along.
A Rotom giggles with a crackling sound when someone notices it. It is curious about every glowing screen and button, and it presses them all.
It has taken over a microwave oven, and it throws flames from its body. It is hot-tempered and flares up when it is startled.
A glowing orb slips into the oven and fills it with a roaring heat. It cooks up trouble wherever it goes.
It lives inside a washing machine and sprays water as it spins. It sloshes about, leaving puddles in its wake.
A cheerful sprite that splashes around and soaks everything nearby. It hums a tune as the drum turns.
It has settled into a refrigerator and gives off a chilly mist. It is cool and clever and loves to freeze a foe in place.
The cold light inside the fridge is its home. It bursts out with a gust of icy air when the door is opened.
It has taken the place of a fan's motor and blows out a stream of wind. It whirls about and kicks up a gale.
A little spirit that turns the blades of a fan at a dizzying speed. It breezes through a room and scatters whatever is loose.
It inhabits a lawn mower and slashes through the grass with whirling blades. It races across a lawn, leaving neat stripes.
A tricky spirit in a garden machine that cuts down plants with a roar. It zips about and makes a mess of the flower beds.
It floats so still that dust settles on the air around it. Scholars who visit its lake say they leave with answers to questions they never asked aloud.
Its two tails trail softly behind it as it floats, and the gem on its brow shines like a polished stone. It has never been seen to hurry.
It flies across lakes and rivers at great speed and is seldom seen in one place for long. People who glimpse it feel a sudden rush of joy.
Mesprit's twin tails sway like streamers as it flies. Villagers near its lake say that the water sparkles brighter when it is near.
It darts about in short, sharp bursts and halts without a wobble. Azelf is seldom seen, and those who claim a sighting describe it differently every time.
Azelf's red jewel glows brightly whenever it chooses a path. It is said to guard its lake against anyone who would disturb the peace there.
A pulse of light runs through the lines of its armour with every beat of its heart. Old murals show it surrounded by turning rings of stars.
When Dialga roars, the air around it seems to waver and slow. Few have seen it, and those who have can never agree on how long they stood before it.
Its body is covered in diamond-like armor and its great shoulders glow. It holds back time itself, and the world falls silent around it.
In this form it is faster and fiercer than ever. Time stretches and folds as it roars, and clocks stop all around.
It moves with great grace, and the air around it ripples as though a curtain were being drawn aside. Its tail sweeps behind it with each step.
The pearls on its shoulders pulse with a soft pink light when it is stirred. Ancient carvings depict it with its arms spread wide, as if holding the world apart.
Its body is draped in pearl armor and it stands with great wings spread wide. It bends space with a flick of its tail.
In this form it holds sway over distance and direction. The air twists in its presence and the land seems to shift.
It lives in the molten heart of a volcano and walks the rock walls on feet that melt solid stone. Steel in its body shines like polished metal.
Heatran's footprints are cut deep into the cave ceiling. When it grows angry, magma pours from its cracked hide.
A furnace roars within it, and its body glows with a blazing, molten light. It lumbers on with a shaking step and burns the ground to cinders.
In this form its steel plates glow white-hot and flow like lava. Volcanoes seem to wake when it passes.
Legends tell of how it pulled whole continents with ropes and shaped the land. It is calm and dozy until the three ancient golems call it awake.
Regigigas sits in a hall of ice, its enormous arms resting on its knees. When woken, it moves slowly but strikes with great force.
It moves through shadows like a ghost, its great wings folding and unfolding in silence. Its roar is said to echo from places that cannot be seen.
Giratina's body is so vast that it seems to fill whatever space it enters. Those who have glimpsed it say the ground beneath their feet feels unsteady.
Its wings fold away and its long body trails behind it like a serpent. It lives in a hidden world, where it floats in silence.
In this form it keeps to the strange world it comes from, where nothing has a fixed place. Its eyes burn like twin red moons.
The glittering wings it wears are said to look like a crescent moon. Those who sleep near it dream peaceful dreams.
Cresselia shines in the dark and glides overhead on quiet nights. Its trail of light is said to ward off bad dreams.
Its small body floats on the open sea, held up by a round tube on its head. Schools drift together in warm currents, sometimes for months.
Phione blows bubbles from its tube and bobs around on the swells. When the water turns cold, it heads toward warmer seas.
It drifts with warm ocean currents, its antennae twitching as it swims. Sailors say that following one leads to calm, clear waters.
A Manaphy can feel the moods of those around it and responds with its own little gestures. It glows softly when it is happy.
It drifts into the dreams of those who sleep and fills them with terrible nightmares. It appears on moonless nights and fades at dawn.
Darkrai seems to want to be left alone, and is said to guard its dark island. It is sad and cold, though few ever see that side.
Its dark cloak flows out into the night and swallows all light. A sea of nightmares follows, and those who sleep nearby cannot wake.
In this form its shadow stretches over the whole town. Its sorrowful eyes watch from the darkness as the dreams turn black.
It blooms in fields of flowers and spreads a gratitude that turns scorched earth green. It is kind and quiet, though it hides when it sees people.
Shaymin's back is covered with grass that bursts into flowers when it is happy. In the sky, it spreads its soft petals and glides.
Its fur turns sleek and a flower on its back unfolds into a long scarf. It soars across the sky, scattering seeds over the land.
In this form it is graceful and quick, and its body is lighter than air. It flies to a new place with the changing of the seasons.
In the oldest stories, it came before everything else and shaped the world with its thousand arms. Many believe every living creature descends from it.
Arceus is believed to have formed the skies, land and sea. Its pale body is ringed by a golden wheel.
It wears a plate that glows with the strength of a fighter. It plants its feet and meets a foe head on.
In this form it brims with fighting spirit, and its body is firm and strong. It holds a stance that never wavers.
It is wrapped in a plate that shines with the colors of the sky. It floats on the wind and feels no weight at all.
In this form it is light and free. It circles above the clouds and sends a great gust rolling over the land.
A purple plate hangs about it like a heavy cloak. A bitter mist seeps from its body and withers all it touches.
In this form it is wrapped in a venom as old as the world. Its glance poisons the air itself.
It wears a plate of earthen brown, and its steps shake the land. The ground itself seems to rise to meet it.
In this form it is steady and strong. Dust drifts up from the soil as it treads over the rocks.
Its plate is as rough and heavy as a cliff face. It stands unmoving and weathers any storm without a mark.
In this form it feels as old as stone itself. A thick, gray armor lines its body and rumbles when it moves.
A green plate shimmers like the wing of a beetle. Tiny lights buzz around it as it drifts through the grass.
In this form it hums with a restless energy. It moves in quick darts and its eyes glint like gems.
Its plate is as pale as a mist and its body flickers like a candle. It passes through walls with no more than a shiver.
In this form it is cold and silent and seems to be half in another world. A faint wail rises when it appears.
It wears a plate that gleams like polished metal. Each step rings out with a clang as it stands firm.
In this form it is hard and cold and nothing can dent it. A silver light spreads across its body.
A plate of deep red covers its chest, and fire flickers at its hooves. The air around it ripples with heat.
In this form it burns with an unquenchable blaze. The ground glows where it steps and the sky turns orange.
Its plate is the deep blue of the sea. Cool mist gathers around it, and the sound of waves follows it everywhere.
In this form it is calm and flowing. Drops of water bead on its coat and run to the ground like rain.
A green plate covers it like moss on an old stone. Little flowers open in the grass wherever it walks.
In this form it is gentle and full of life. A fresh scent of leaves rises in its wake.
It carries a bright yellow plate that crackles with sparks. Its hooves hit the ground with a flash and a boom.
In this form it is bursting with energy. Lightning arcs along its golden body and the air hums with static.
A pink plate glows over its chest, and its eyes seem to look straight into the mind. A strange, quiet pressure fills the space around it.
In this form it moves things by thought alone. A soft, pulsing light dances across its body.
Its plate is as pale as frost, and a freezing mist curls round its feet. Everything it passes is dusted with a glaze of ice.
In this form it is clear and cold. Its breath makes tiny crystals that glitter in the light.
A plate of deep blue lines its body, and its eyes burn with a fierce light. The air hums with ancient power when it rears up.
In this form it carries itself like a lord of old. Its roar echoes from the mountains and the clouds part before it.
It wears a plate as black as a moonless night, and shadows gather at its hooves. It slips through the dark without a sound.
In this form it is calm and cold, and its eyes seem to see through lies. Darkness bends toward it like smoke.
A plate of soft pink hangs about it like a veil. A gentle glimmer drifts from its body and leaves a sweet, bright scent.
In this form it is kind and bright, and tiny sparkles trail behind. A hush of wonder settles on those who see it.
It brings victory to those who stand beside it. Energy streams from its two ears and gives its partner endless strength.
Victini is playful and daring and loves a challenge. When it feels the spirit of a fight, its body warms with fire.
It soaks up sunlight to power itself, and it moves quickly and quietly when the sun is warm. A cold, cloudy day makes it sluggish and prickly.
Snivy holds its head high and rarely lets anyone see it hurry. It deflects blows with the flick of its tail.
It slips between branches without a rustle, holding its curled tail aloft. Quick to shed its skin, it grows more composed each time.
Servine hides in the shade and strikes with vines from the cover of leaves. It will not move to fight unless it has to.
It curls like a length of vine around a tree and stares calmly at the world. Its glare alone can make opponents hesitate.
Serperior glides with elegant grace and rarely hurries. Its patience is such that fights are usually decided before they begin.
A warm snort of flame leaves its nose when it sneezes or laughs, and it sometimes chars a berry before eating it. Roasting is a favorite pastime.
Tepig likes to nose around for nuts under dry leaves and snuggles up to its trainer on cold nights. Its curly tail wiggles when it is pleased.
It puffs out thick smoke with every stout breath. Its round belly is warm to the touch, and its fiery heart makes it eager to dash.
Pignite charges straight ahead, trusting to its heavy frame. It is not good at holding back, but it is a hard worker.
Flames burst from its chin when it is angry and heat rolls off in waves. It has the strength to flatten a boulder and the heart to lift a friend.
Emboar sets its fists ablaze and pounds the earth in a rhythm. It is fiercely loyal and always puts its partner first.
Its flames blaze up into a great mane and its arms grow thick as logs. It stamps and roars and the ground splits under its weight.
In this form it is wilder than ever, and its fire never fades. It charges at a foe like a fiery boulder rolling down a hill.
It carries a smooth scallop on its belly and uses it to open shells and to clear a path. The shell is polished daily and is its pride.
Oshawott floats on its back along rivers and enjoys the sun. It practices with its shell near the water at dawn.
Two shells are held in its hands like twin swords, and it slices through the air as it practices. It trains with great discipline every day.
Dewott knows its own skill and bears itself with dignity. It will duel only on fair ground and never in a hurry.
A long blade extends from each of its forelegs, and with the horn on its brow it fights with a steady calm. It values honor above victory.
Samurott stares down an opponent without a flinch. Its big, strong body shrugs off most blows.
It lived by a rough coast and fought with a blade carved from its own shell. It stands tall with the calm air of a seasoned warrior.
A dark and stern Samurott that guards the northern shore. Its swordsmanship is quick, and it never wastes a stroke.
Rising onto its hind legs, it scans the area around it and warns the others of anything strange. Its cheeks bulge with seeds stored away for later.
Patrat lives in burrows dug at the edge of fields. It is a careful watcher that rarely wanders far from home.
When it spots trouble, its stripes glow and it stands at attention. It communicates with signals made with its long tail.
Watchog stays alert with its eyes wide open, even while it eats. It takes its role as a lookout extremely seriously.
It is a brave little pup that stands its ground against bigger dogs. It is quick to bark but easy to train and eager to please.
Lillipup tags along behind the family it likes and wags its tail. It sniffs out lost objects and brings them back proudly.
It stays loyal to its trainer without question and will guard a home or lead lost travelers back. Its thick fur gives it the look of a shaggy rug.
Herdier follows commands calmly and carries things in its mouth. In a crowd it never loses track of its owner.
It is known for finding people lost in the snow. Its long coat keeps it warm, and it digs down with its big paws to reach a person buried underneath.
Stoutland has a calm, gentle manner that puts nervous people at ease. It sniffs out trails even after heavy rain.
It acts sweet and innocent, then snatches a snack from your hand and darts away. Its sly eyes gleam when it is up to something.
Purrloin slinks through alleys in search of leftovers. It likes to curl up where it can be seen yet not caught.
It prowls at night without making a sound, and its eyes glow in the gloom. Sleek muscles make it a wildly fast sprinter.
Liepard approaches prey from behind, patient and silent. A cool beauty, it keeps its distance from strangers.
The leafy tuft on its head is fragrant and tasty, and it is fond of sharing food with friends. It grumbles if no one wants a taste.
Pansage plucks berries from the treetops and passes them down to its pals. Its tail flicks when it is happy.
Its thorny tail is both a whip and a weapon. It is short tempered and will lash out at any who disturb its trees.
Simisage crashes through the foliage with a mighty whoop, hauling bunches of fruit. Its ferocity is a bluff more often than not.
A flame flickers at the end of its tail and never dies out, warm enough to heat a small room. It enjoys cooking berries and gets sulky if they burn.
Pansear is a hot-blooded little monkey that gets overheated easily. It sits in the shade between bursts of energy.
Its head is crowned with a bright blaze that flares when it fights. It stokes the fire by blowing on it and rubbing its paws together.
Simisear loves spicy food and spits embers when it laughs. It is bold and mischievous and enjoys a prank.
Water gathers in the tuft on its head, and it sprays the contents in a fine mist to cool its friends on a hot day. It dozes off when the tuft runs dry.
Panpour fusses over its tuft and rinses it in clean streams. A leaky, dirty one leaves it sulky and out of sorts.
Its tail draws water up from the ground and lets it go as a strong jet. It brings fresh water to dry places and puts out small fires.
Simipour is stubborn and sharp-tongued, always ready to scold a lazy friend. It hates to see good water wasted.
It drifts through the night and gobbles up dreams, leaving pink mist behind. If it eats a sweet dream, the mist turns brightly colored.
Munna naps often and hangs on to whoever is nearest. Its forehead mark gives off a soft glow when it feeds.
The mist rising from its forehead shows the dreams it has gathered, and the pictures drift above it like small clouds. It lives in a haze of sleep.
Musharna slumbers through most of its life, and its dream smoke can lull a whole town. It moves only when it must.
It bobs its head as it walks and is not shy of crowds. Parks and plazas are its favorite haunts, where it picks up crumbs.
Pidove can find its way home from far away. It makes a soft, cooing sound whenever it feels safe and well fed.
It never loses its way, even when carried a long distance in the dark. People used to send messages on its wings.
Tranquill glides over rooftops and tall buildings without effort. Its sense of direction is excellent.
The male struts about with a bright head crest and fans it out to impress, while the female flies with swift, precise turns.
Unfezant takes long strides and prefers to run before it takes off. Its glossy plumage is cleaned many times each day.
The stripes along its mane spark when it gallops, and it takes off at the first rumble of thunder. It is skittish and quick to bolt.
Blitzle gathers static as it runs and lets it go in a flicker. It enjoys racing with the wind and the rain.
It gallops so swiftly that its hooves are almost silent, and a thunderclap booms behind it. It can outrun almost any foe.
Zebstrika's mane glows bright when it is angry. In a storm it stands on a hilltop and neighs at the flashes.
It has no ears, but it can sense sounds through the vibration of the ground. A faint tapping comes from within its body as it rolls about.
Roggenrola lives under the earth and sometimes tumbles out of the walls of a cave. Its shell is every bit as tough as the stone around it.
Orange crystals sprout from its back, and the harder it fights, the brighter they glow. Miners treasure the energy they hold.
Boldore rolls along tunnels with a deep rumbling. When angry, it hurls sharp stones from its crystals.
It soaks up sunlight in its crystals and fires it out in a beam that can bore through solid rock. Its huge body is as sturdy as a mountain.
Gigalith's crown of crystals pulses with light as it fights. It is gentle at heart and stays close to its mine.
It hangs upside down by the dozen on the ceilings of caves, and if you meet one, it may leave a heart-shaped mark on you. It is a very social flyer.
Woobat settles on the walls of dark places and hums softly. A strange smell clings to its fur.
Its wings send out sound waves that you cannot hear but that can make rocks crack. It flutters in the air to show it likes someone.
Swoobat swoops down from its perch with a gentle flap. Its noise blasts can bring down an entire cave roof.
It spins its claws like a drill and tunnels faster than a person can follow. It leaves long, curved trenches behind it.
Drilbur is as eager as a young digger on his first day of work. It likes to pop up from underground and surprise travelers.
Two steel drills at its head rotate at high speed to tunnel through rock, and it can dig a mile in a single day. It loves nothing more than digging.
Excadrill burrows in the dark, using its large claws as picks. It has a fierce, restless temper.
Its drills spin like twin tornadoes and its body turns as hard as a bunker. It bores through rock and steel in a heartbeat.
In this form it digs faster than any machine. Its claws shear through rock and the walls of tunnels tremble in its wake.
Its feelers can hear a heartbeat from a distance, and it loves to check on how others feel. Hurt creatures often find their way to its side.
Audino is a kind, caring creature, and its soft fur is pleasant to touch. It carries an extra spare of food for those who are hungry.
Its feelers stretch out and sway like soft ribbons. A warm glow comes from its body and soothes the sick and the wounded.
In this form it is even kinder and more caring. A hushed, gentle hum fills the air and eases every pain.
It carries a stout piece of lumber around with it as a tool and a toy. Builders appreciate its help hauling beams.
Timburr wields a log with ease and swings it at any obstacle. Work makes it happy, and idleness makes it fidgety.
Its steel beam is carried everywhere, and it can hold up whole buildings. Hard labor builds up its muscles day after day.
Gurdurr gathers with others at building sites and trains in teams. Its eye looks sharply upon anyone who slacks.
It wields two big concrete pillars, and swings them with mighty force. Some say it is the master of building, and its help is much sought after.
Conkeldurr is a stern but kind veteran, always ready to lend a hand. Its muscles ripple as it works.
It sings by vibrating its tail, and the sound carries underwater to others. Its fellows join the chorus until the whole pond is humming.
Tympole drums softly against a rock to call its friends. A cold, rainy night is its favorite time for a concert.
The bumps on its body give out gentle pulses and make the water around it ripple. It lives near still lakes with soft mud.
Palpitoad's tongue is long and sticky, and it uses it to snag insects on the wing. In the evening, it slips out of the water to hunt.
It strikes the ground with the knobs on its arms and sends out quakes that numb its foes. Its pulses are felt through the whole swamp.
Seismitoad flings sticky toxin from its skin. Its steady, thundering song rolls over the marsh at night.
It grabs its foe by the belt and flings it over its shoulder. It tightens its belt before a fight, and a loose belt means it has lost its nerve.
Throh trains in the hills with a group of friends. Only a worthy challenger is invited to a bout.
It trains by punching and kicking at the stone and bark. The sharp snap of its blows echoes among the trees.
Sawk tightens its belt and bows before a match. It will not stop until it is truly defeated.
After hatching, it stitches leaves into a cozy cloak. It nibbles on the stitching when it is hungry, and sews a bigger one when it grows.
Sewaddle moves along leaf stems and chews through the veins. In the evening it rests wrapped up in its garment.
It hides in a snug bundle of leaves to stay safe while it changes. The wrap is turned to the sun to keep it warm.
Swadloon almost never moves, but its leafy shell gives off a gentle, fresh scent. It prefers the shade.
It makes clothes for its young by stitching leaves with thread from its mouth. The layers it makes keep the little ones warm.
Leavanny watches over smaller bug Pokémon and brings them food. Its sharp claws work with great skill.
It is quick to strike with its venomous fangs and scurries through leaf litter in all directions. It has a short fuse and a fiery spirit.
Venipede crawls among stones looking for a meal. Its many legs drum against the ground when it is angry.
It curls up inside its shell and spins like a wheel, charging forward with great speed. Its spiky armor repels a bite.
Whirlipede rests in a tight coil and builds up energy for the change to come. Touching it carelessly can bring a nasty sting.
Its body is long and strong, and it ties foes up with its coils. It jabs with venom from two sharp horns at the front.
Scolipede hunts down its prey with a relentless drive. Its speed is amazing, even over rough ground.
Its body grows longer and wraps in thick, spiky plates. It coils around a foe and crushes it with a tight squeeze.
In this form it charges ahead like a runaway train. Its venom flows in torrents and its legs thrash with a rhythmic clatter.
It floats in the wind like a bit of fluff and sneaks into homes through open windows. A soft breeze carries it along.
Cottonee likes to gather in great white drifts. A strong gust can blow it away, but it simply drifts back.
It plays tricks and slips away like the wind. If caught, it leaves tufts of cotton behind and vanishes.
Whimsicott flies on a breeze and hides in clouds. The cottony puffs it leaves can spoil anything they land on.
Its leaves soak up sunlight and use it to grow, and a gloomy day makes it sulky. It plants itself in the earth for a nap and drinks the rain.
Petilil is gentle and shy, with a lovely, soft scent. A sweet bud on its head blooms when it is happy.
It carries itself like a dancer and sways with graceful steps. Folk tales say the bloom on its head brings good luck to those who see it.
Lilligant has a sweet fragrance that calms those around it. It is an elegant, delicate creature that looks after its petals.
It lived in the high, cold meadows and had to fight to survive. It practices a graceful, forceful dance with the blooms it wears.
A tall, tough flower that grows among the rocks. Its fighting style is quick and elegant, and it trains in the wind.
A big school of them can turn a quiet lake into a boiling froth. They are aggressive and will attack anything that comes into their territory.
Basculin has a sharp temper and a strong jaw. It is easily recognizable by the red or blue stripe across its body.
A cool blue stripe runs along its body. This school is calm and keeps to quiet pools, though it bites at anything that comes too close.
It prefers to live in clear water and is wary of the red-striped kind. A group of them moves together in one flowing line.
A pale stripe marks its flank, and it is timid and gentle for its kind. It hides among the weeds and slips away at the sight of a stranger.
It lives in deep, still water and shows itself only at dusk. Its calm manner makes it a quiet neighbor.
It hides under the sand with only its eyes poking out, watching for something to eat. Thick skin keeps in its moisture in the heat of the day.
Sandile has a bad habit of nipping at people. It swims through the dunes as though they were water.
Its eyes are shielded from the sun and the sand, and it can see well in the dark. It scrambles after prey in a pack.
Krokorok's tail swings when it hunts. It grabs onto its prey, and does not let go.
It is a ferocious hunter that tears through prey with powerful jaws. Its glare is so fierce that others back away.
Krookodile's pulling power is immense, and it can tow a loaded truck. It sees almost everything as a threat.
It rolls about like a ball and is round and lively. At bedtime it tucks in its limbs, and the fire inside it shrinks to a flicker.
Darumaka is hot-blooded and takes pride in its stubborn spirit. It bounces back every time it is knocked over.
It lives in the cold north and keeps itself warm by eating snow that melts inside its body. It rolls through the drifts with a cheerful grin.
A pale, round Darumaka that sleeps in a ball. Its inner fire has turned to a cold glow, and it trundles about with a gleeful bounce.
It has a fiery temper and powerful fists, and it pounds the ground in rage. After a fight, it sits in a meditative pose to calm down.
Darmanitan lives in the desert and wears a thick mane of flame. When pressed, it flies into a frenzy.
It sits down with its legs crossed and goes still as a statue. The fire in its body dwindles and a quiet strength gathers inside.
In this form it is calm and deep in thought. Its eyes are closed, and its mind reaches out in waves of psychic force.
Its body is as white as snow and its breath is a cold mist. It rampages across the ice with a hard, cheerful grin.
A powerful Darmanitan of the cold north that smashes boulders with its fists. Icy fumes steam from its mouth as it fights.
It closes its eyes and sits in a deep trance, and flames of pale blue flicker on its head. The air around it grows quiet and cold.
In this form it is calm, and both ice and fire swirl within it. It sits unmoving in the snow and waits for the right moment.
It dances on dry plains and shakes the seeds on its arms like maracas. The rhythms it makes can be heard from far away.
Maractus loves a lively beat and grows stronger when there is music. Its wide flower blossoms in warm sun.
It digs out a rock and takes it as a home, and then it carries its shelter wherever it goes. It uses the shell's size as a measure of its worth.
Dwebble leaves its stone to feed in the cool of the evening. A very good rock draws arguments with its neighbors.
It bears a massive boulder on its back and stands firm against all comers. Two of them will heave their rocks at each other to settle who is stronger.
Crustle's rock home has been in its care for years. It moves slowly under the weight but cannot be shifted.
It wears its baggy skin like a loose pair of trousers, and kicks up a fuss if someone tries to tug it. A rough crowd is its typical company.
Scraggy has a hard head that it uses to knock down obstacles. It runs in gangs and is always looking for a scrap.
It holds a leader's place among a gang of troublemakers, and its kicks are swift and heavy. A tough crest keeps its head safe in a scrap.
Scrafty rules the back alleys with a dry stare. Its loose hide is an excellent shield and lets it shrug off blows.
Its crest grows large and its glare gets even meaner. It stands with its fists clenched and stares down a whole gang.
In this form it is a tough street boss that never backs down. Its kicks are like a sledgehammer on the pavement.
It circles over a ruined city on a set route and swoops down on anyone who strays beneath. The patterns on its wings look like old carvings.
Sigilyph guards a place that has been long forgotten. Its strange eyes flash as it hovers on the wind.
It clutches a mask that looks like a face from long ago, and if it gazes into it, it weeps. It drifts among old stones in the evening.
Yamask rarely lets anyone see what its mask hides. Its sad, silent steps never leave a track.
It was once a creature that drifted in a cursed desert, and its mask is cracked from age. It trudges along with a sad and heavy step.
A stone-gray Yamask that mourns for its past. It carries a broken mask and stares at it for hours.
Its golden casket is painted with elaborate designs and holds a hidden figure. It moves with a slow tread and its lid creaks shut over its prey.
Cofagrigus lingers in tombs and keeps an old, hollow stare. Its four arms are rarely still.
It swam in ancient seas and ate shellfish that lay on the sea floor. Brought back from a fossil, it has a dull, gentle look.
Tirtouga retreats into its shell when threatened, then pushes out its head to bite. It is a strong swimmer in cold water.
Its shell is armor that has weathered countless seas, and it dives deep to hunt. It walks on two legs when on land.
Carracosta's powerful jaws can crack open hard-shelled prey. It carries its heavy shell with ease.
It cannot truly fly, but it can glide from cliff tops. Fossil hunters have revived it from long-buried stone.
Archen lived in trees and leapt from branch to branch. It flaps its wings wildly but doesn't get far.
It runs on strong legs and takes off to hunt in the sky. Its whole body is heavy, though, and it tires quickly when it flies.
Archeops lands with a thud and a loud cry. It fights with sharp claws and its feather crest.
It lives in back lots where people leave their garbage, and it feeds on what others discard. A foul smell clings to it.
Trubbish carries a bag of junk and does not mind the stink. It is quite at home among old cans and broken toys.
Poison seeps from the trash heap on its back, and its arms drip with sludge. It lumbers through the dump in search of a meal.
Garbodor grows larger when the dump is full of good things. It does not seem to notice its own smell.
A huge mound of garbage towers over the field and spews a toxic haze. Its many arms swing about like heavy hoses.
Giant energy swells its heap of rubbish into a mountain. The stench alone can make a person faint at a great distance.
It can take on the form of a person or Pokémon to trick those who wander too close. The disguise falls away when it is frightened.
Zorua plays pranks on people in the woods and then watches them from the bushes. It can look like anyone, but its tail always shows.
It lived in snowy mountains and became a restless spirit. It tricks travelers into the fog, and then watches them wander in circles.
A pale and lonely fox that drifts through the mist. Its eyes glow with a ghostly light, and it disappears without a trace.
It uses illusions to protect its family, and it creates whole landscapes to confuse hunters. A lone traveler may wander in circles for hours.
Zoroark is fiercely devoted to its pack. It moves with a silent stride and then vanishes in a blur.
It haunts the cold mountains and stirs up strange illusions in the snow. Anyone who follows it is led astray.
A fierce spirit that seeks vengeance for the lost. Its white mane flows like a mist as it prowls through the pines.
It sweeps its home clean with its long, soft tail and keeps it spotless. If it finds dust, it starts to tidy up on the spot.
Minccino loves a neat nest and gets upset when anything is out of place. Its fur is sleek and silky.
Its coat is covered in a fine oil that repels dust and dirt. It wraps its tail around itself like a scarf and wears it with pride.
Cinccino is elegant and graceful and slaps its foes with its tail in quick, light flurries. It holds a grudge against messy spaces.
It stares at things for a long time with big, unblinking eyes. In the dark it may look at nothing in particular, and that makes people uneasy.
Gothita wears a ribbon-like bow on its head and moves quietly. It is shy, but it follows people about at a distance.
It is said to watch the stars at night and read the future in them. Its gaze seems to follow you wherever you go.
Gothorita holds its arms out as it moves, and its mind is hard to read. A small bow of dark hair sways above its eyes.
It looks to the heavens on clear nights and can sense the paths of the stars. Some insist it can read what the future holds.
Gothitelle wears a gown of black and hides its eyes in the shadows. Its mysterious power draws many towards it.
It floats in a bubble of fluid that shields it from harm, and it lets out thoughts that people can sense. It is a quiet and thoughtful being.
Solosis can talk through its mind and communicates in short bursts. A tiny cell drifts slowly through the air.
Two minds are better than one, and each half of it thinks independently. When they disagree, it seems to freeze in place.
Duosion hovers silently and lets its thoughts drift about. Strangers find it hard to read.
It shakes hands to link minds and share thoughts. Its brain is so large that it can work out a complex puzzle in an instant.
Reuniclus is calm and wise, but its power is strong. It is said that its gel cells let it send waves of force.
It splashes in the shallows and makes a fine bubbling chatter. Wet or dry, it is much better at swimming than flying.
Ducklett dives for water plants and paddles through the reeds. A mother will lead her flock in a tidy line.
It begins its dance at dawn and rises on its wings like a graceful ballerina. Its white feathers are brushed back and kept clean.
Swanna is known for gliding gently over lakes. It shows great pride in its pure plumage.
Born from fresh snow, it drinks in cold air and breathes out a fine powder of ice. It likes to bask in the cold and melts if it grows warm.
Vanillite is a sweet little treat that floats about on chilly days. Children think it looks like a cone of ice cream.
Its twin heads draw in cold air and breathe it out as a harsh blizzard. It is safe only in a place where the air stays frosty.
Vanillish glitters in the sun, but the sparkle is only frozen water. It becomes sluggish when the weather gets warm.
The twin heads fight against each other and make blasts of snow when their tempers rise. The cold from its body can freeze the ground.
Vanilluxe builds up a storm inside itself and breathes it out. It comes from a distant mountain of ice.
Its coat shifts in color with the seasons, matching the pink of spring, the green of summer, the red of autumn or the gray of winter.
Deerling lives in woodlands and its fur smells of flowers. Its soft step makes no sound on the forest floor.
In summer its coat turns a lively green like the leaves of the trees. It sprints across the meadow with a gleeful bound.
This Deerling basks in the heat of the sun and loves a good splash in a stream. Its coat is cool and fresh.
When fall arrives its coat takes on the red-orange of fallen leaves. It trots through the woods with a soft, rustling step.
This Deerling's coat blends into the forest floor in the cool season. It nibbles on acorns before the cold sets in.
Its fur turns gray and thick in the cold, and a small tuft puffs up on its back. It paws through the snow to find food.
This Deerling huddles with its herd in a sheltered spot. Its warm breath rises in tiny clouds.
Its antlers sprout in a new array of flowers or leaves in each season. It leaps through the trees with a gait full of grace.
Sawsbuck herds travel together and signal the change of season with the colors of their coats. Their antlers are admired by all.
Its great antlers sprout lush green leaves, and its coat is bright as new grass. It strides through the woods with a proud, bright gaze.
In summer this Sawsbuck leads its herd to cool streams. Flowers bloom on its horns in the warm sun.
Its antlers are crowned with leaves of gold and crimson. It leads its herd through the woods with a calm, stately walk.
This Sawsbuck's coat is a deep brown like soil after a rain. It gathers with its kind as the leaves fall.
Frost clings to its antlers like silver lace, and its coat is thick and gray. It treads through the deep snow with a steady step.
In winter this Sawsbuck guards its herd and keeps them warm. Its breath turns to mist in the still, cold air.
It stores electricity in its cheeks and releases it in a spark when it is spooked. Its flaps of skin let it glide between trees.
Emolga plays in the tops of the trees and sleeps in a hole in the trunk. It gets shocked if it eats too many nuts.
Whenever it spots one particular rival, it charges with no thought at all. When they are near, its jaws snap open in a fury.
Karrablast lives in the dark depths of the woods and can't help but rush into danger. Its tiny jaws are tough and sharp.
Its armor is stolen from another and worn like a suit of iron, and it guards itself with a lance. It fights fiercely without letting go of its weapon.
Escavalier thrusts with its twin lances in rapid strokes. Its stiff steel plates make it very hard to hurt.
Its cap is patterned like a ball left lying on the forest floor, and it waits for the curious to come close. When they reach down to pick it up, it releases a cloud of spores.
Foongus sits patiently among the ferns and plays at being a toy. It dances when no one is watching.
It sways its arms to lure prey in with a hypnotic dance. The pattern on its cap draws the eye while it blasts a cloud of toxic spores.
Amoonguss prefers to stay on the ground and wait for a meal to come by. Its odd shape confuses hungry newcomers.
It floats on the ocean currents and wraps its frilly arms around any ship that comes too near. Its eerie glow draws curious people into the water.
Frillish drifts around in the warm seas, slowly pulsing. It is said that the male and the female can be told apart by their color.
Her frilly skirts are a soft pink, and she drifts on the tide with a dreamy air. She glows softly and floats toward faint lights.
This Frillish has a gentle face and delicate fins. She drifts in calm waters and avoids the roar of the surf.
It drags lost ships down to the depths and keeps them in its watery lair. Sailors say it haunts shipwrecks at night.
Jellicent lives in the dark of the ocean where it hides sunken treasure. Its massive form fills the water with a pale glow.
She wears a long, flowing veil of pink and white and glides through the water like a queen. She rules the deep with a quiet grace.
This Jellicent guards sunken ships with a patient watch. She is as fair as she is dangerous to those who intrude.
It heals sick or injured fish with a special mucus, and it seeks out those who need help. It swims close to the wounded and nudges them along.
Alomomola is a gentle healer that never fights. Its pale pink body hovers among the waves, always looking for someone in need.
It clings to larger creatures and takes a little of their static to store in a sac on its body. A swarm can hide a whole tree trunk.
Joltik is small, but a pinprick of its electricity is a nasty surprise. It likes to hitch rides on the backs of other Pokémon.
It spins a web of electric threads and waits for prey to touch them. When it senses a tug, it shoots out a stinging charge.
Galvantula runs along the web with a skittering rush. The charged strands crackle and spit in a thunderstorm.
It clings to the roof of a cave and sucks iron from the rock. When threatened, it fires spikes in all directions.
Ferroseed has a body of hard metal and spiny quills. It may seem harmless, but its prickly coat is a warning.
It hangs by its vines from cave ceilings and lashes out with whip-like tentacles. Its spiky shell is covered in thorns.
Ferrothorn hardly moves, and it weighs more than it appears. When angry, it whips about with a clanging rattle.
Two gears mesh in its body, and when they turn it hums. It is peaceful and unlikely to cause trouble.
Klink looks for a gear that fits its own and spins with it in perfect time. If they don't match, it gets upset and clicks about.
Its pair of gears are matched and turn against each other to power its body. They never leave one another's side.
Klang can fire a spinning gear at a target. The hard shell is cold and smooth to the touch.
The red core rotates and holds energy in reserve. Its gears are one of the oldest designs in the world.
Klinklang fires a beam of focused power from the core. The drive that turns its great gears makes a regular, ringing beat.
Alone it is feeble, but in large groups the sparks it makes can fry a whole boat. It swims in schools near the shore.
Tynamo is the tiniest of electric fish, and it gives off a faint glow. It seems to enjoy storms.
It wraps around its prey and zaps it, and its mouth shows rows of tiny, sharp teeth. It slips out of the water and slithers over the ground.
Eelektrik gives off powerful charges, and it uses the lights on its body to see in the dark. In the wild, it lives in caves with water.
It crawls from the water and takes hold of a foe with its limbs and fangs. Then it blasts it with a surge of power.
Eelektross uses its strong arms to grip. Even a short touch from its fangs is enough to numb a hand.
Its body is covered in a net of crackling cables, and it surges with a wild current. It slithers about and strikes with a flash of lightning.
In this form it is longer and thicker. An electric glow lights up the whole swamp as it rises from the water.
Its big head holds a mind that can send out waves to nudge its surroundings. It hums quietly to itself and rarely looks anyone in the eye.
Elgyem is reported to have fallen from the sky. When it is curious, its eyes glow a mild yellow-green.
It points its long fingers and lights them up to talk in flashes of color. A pale beam of the same glow can twist the memory of a witness.
Beheeyem sits in the dark of a field and takes in its surroundings. Farmers who meet one tend to lose the thread of their memories.
It sheds a faint, cold glow, but the flame on its head draws the spirit from those it burns. It likes to shine near places where people have died.
Litwick glides into view at dusk, a little wax candle moving by itself. Travelers who follow its light end up lost.
It haunts hospitals and houses where someone is about to die. It floats close by, patiently waiting.
Lampent glows with a ghostly blue fire and goes quiet when it is spotted. It sucks in the spirit of anyone it sees falling ill.
Its fire is the color of a ghost, and it entices travelers with a swaying dance. Anyone who gazes into the flames is lost.
Chandelure waves its arms and sets alight the souls it has gathered. Its eerie elegance is a feature of old, dim mansions.
Its flames burn pale and cold and its form sways like a ghostly chandelier. It lures in the lost and stirs a deep hush.
In this form it burns with an eerie light that never flickers. A circle of ghostly fire spins slowly around it.
The tusks on its jaw grow back after they fall off, and it sharpens them on stone to keep them keen. It scratches marks on trees to show its territory.
Axew likes to chew on anything hard. It cuts a deep scar into the ground when it digs in its heels.
It trims its tusks against a rock to keep them in prime condition. It is proud of them and loses its temper if they are snapped.
Fraxure is a fighter that charges any rival that crosses its path. Its sharp tusks can slice through a thick trunk.
Its massive tusks could cut through steel, and yet it is calm unless it is provoked. It is a fair fighter that will not strike a defenseless foe.
Haxorus is feared across the mountains, but it can be kind and protective of those it knows. Its tusks are fit for a king.
The icicle under its nose grows long when it is healthy and fresh. It sniffles in cold weather, and its snot freezes in a flash.
Cubchoo gets sick if its nose runs dry. When winter sets in, it trudges about looking for a hearty meal.
Its breath turns to a freezing wind and makes ice crystals on its fur. It scales icy cliffs with a firm grip of its claws.
Beartic stalks the frozen sea in search of fish. It grows a thick coat of icicles and holds its ground in the blizzard.
It is formed of ice crystals, and it flows across the sky with a trail of snow. It hides in clouds, and it falls only to catch something to eat.
Cryogonal is a six-sided shape of pure frost. When it is held, it freezes the hand and shatters if dropped.
It wears a hard shell like a helmet and cannot move well without a partner. It does best when it works with another Pokémon.
Shelmet is slow and sticky and leaves a trail of goo as it creeps. Its shell is nice and warm.
Without its heavy shell it moves like a flash, and it hurls its body around in rapid bursts. Its strikes are too fast to see.
Accelgor flings itself about and leaves a spray of liquid in its wake. It avoids attacks by leaping out of the way at the last second.
It lies buried in mud with only its eyes showing, and waits until a victim steps on it. It zaps its meal with a jolt of power.
Stunfisk keeps its mouth turned up in a permanent frown. It has a flat body that lets it blend into the muck.
It lives in sour, muddy water and has a grim, jagged face. It buries itself in the silt and waits with its mouth open.
A rusty and spiky fish that bites down hard on those who step on it. It endures with its grumpy look through the hardest times.
It practices by flinging its limbs at the air and is quick to learn new moves. Its supple body lets it strike from many angles.
Mienfoo sets itself in a stance and bows. Its steps are light, and it dodges blows with a twist of its waist.
The fur on its arms is used like a whip and cracks through the air. Its kicks and strikes are lightning fast.
Mienshao keeps up a constant flow of strikes. Its trained body is flexible and hardy, and its mind is calm.
It lives in a cave and ambushes whoever passes. It lies in wait with its mouth shut, then lunges with a roar.
Druddigon has a rough, red hide that is tough as rock. It sleeps in the sun to warm its body, and its wings are used as a cloak.
It was made out of clay by someone long ago, and it moves on a strange, slow march. No one knows why it was built or who built it.
Golett roams around ancient ruins with a blank, dull stare. When it gets going, its stiff legs thump on the ground.
It guards its home with a steady watch, and a plate set into its chest is what holds its wild power back. It flies when it is sent after a threat.
Golurk stomps forth with a heavy tread. Legend says it protects the people that live near its ruins.
Its body grows huge, and a ghostly glow seeps from its seams. Its fists fly with a speed that no one expects from such a giant.
In this form it is a ruthless guardian, and it acts without orders. Its steps sound like a drumbeat from the underworld.
Its body is covered in blades that it keeps sharp, and a gang of them will fight as one. It gladly follows a strong leader.
Pawniard slashes at its foes with its arms and head. It rubs its blades against each other to hone them.
It rules over a pack of lesser blades and commands them with cold looks. A leader of cold steel, it will cut down anyone who disobeys.
Bisharp shows no mercy, and it fights without pity. Its sharp arms can shear iron plates.
It charges head first with its great curly afro and shrugs off blows that would topple a wall. It will wreck a truck with its thick skull.
Bouffalant herds are stubborn and will not give way. It prefers to settle disputes by butting heads.
Small as it is, it picks fights with much bigger rivals and often loses. It trains by diving at foes again and again.
Rufflet is bold and reckless and flaps its wings loudly. It gets back up and tries again.
It is a brave flyer that fights to the end to defend its flock. Even when it is wounded, it stays in the air.
Braviary is a symbol of courage and protects its friends. It dives with great speed and grabs prey in its talons.
It soars above the highlands with a calm, wise look. Its mind is sharp and it can sense a storm long before it breaks.
A noble eagle that guards the high peaks. It sends out waves of quiet power and glides in great circles.
It wears a bone on its tail as a diaper of sorts, and the young one cannot fly well. It gets by on carrion and leftover scraps.
Vullaby lurks among the rocks until a bigger predator leaves its meal. It flaps awkwardly and often falls.
It circles over its territory, looking for scraps. It carries bones for the wear of its young and uses them as weapons.
Mandibuzz keeps a cool eye on the landscape below. It hunts the sick or weakened and never wastes a thing.
Its tongue is a flame that it uses to hunt for ants, and it licks them up with a hiss. It lives where it can find its favorite prey.
Heatmor slurps up anything it can reach. A flame burns inside its mouth, and it snorts out a stream of fire.
It lives in colonies in deep burrows and bites with steel jaws. A group will team up to take on prey much bigger than themselves.
Durant digs endless tunnels through the rock. Its enemy is a certain large insect that raids its nest.
It has no sight and bumps into everything, and it tries to bite whatever it touches. It is a danger to anyone who is nearby.
Deino is a hungry little fellow that gnaws at anything within reach. Its roughness comes from not knowing what it is chewing.
Each head has a mind of its own, and the two are always bickering. When they pull in different directions, it goes in circles.
Zweilous feeds twice as much as other Pokémon and fights for each bite. It lives in the dark and bites the unwary.
Three heads and six wings make it a fearsome sight. It rampages over towns, eating everything it meets, and then flies on in a rage.
Hydreigon's heads work together to devour a foe. It is called a brutal beast, and no one dares to stand in its way.
It basks in the heat of a volcano and spits out fireballs when angry. Its body is as warm as a heater and its sting is hot enough to burn.
Larvesta is wrapped in white fluff. When it is time, it gathers heat and heads up in search of a place to sleep.
It scatters a fiery dust as it flaps and lights the sky like a little sun. Long ago, it is said to have shone in place of the sun when it was hidden.
Volcarona's six wings beat in a steady rhythm and keep the air around it hot. It is a gentle sight when it floats in the dusk.
It is said to protect Pokémon from the cruelty of people, and it appears as a blue knight with steel horns. Its body is tough as a shield.
Cobalion has a kind heart and a stern gaze. It leads its allies with firm and calm confidence.
It once smashed a castle wall to save its friends, and its charge can break through any rock. It has a powerful, muscular frame.
Terrakion lives high in the cliffs and clears away obstacles with a charge. It has a strong sense of justice.
It moves through the grass like the wind and can slash with the sharp horns on its head. It does not make a sound as it runs.
Virizion is a graceful, gentle fighter, and strong enough to make a foe back off without a word. It gets along with those who treat nature with care.
It flies through the sky on a whirl of wind and brings storms wherever it goes. It spins its tail like a propeller and makes a roaring gale.
Tornadus has a wild temper and vanishes in a blink. Its swirling winds can rip roofs from houses.
It is a quiet and focused wind spirit, and it hovers with its legs tucked in. It glides over the land and its gale carries a chill.
In this form it rushes with a fierce gaze. It sweeps over towns like a gust of fate and then drifts away.
It is a restless thing that rides the clouds, and where its bolts strike, the ground is scorched. It flies at the center of its own storm.
Thundurus cackles and darts about, flinging lightning. Its tail glows like a spark in the dark.
It floats in a crouch and sends out a rolling thunder. It is cool and deliberate, and it drinks in the energy of storms.
In this form it is calm and dangerous. The sparks about its tail snap and hiss, and the air tastes of rain.
A white dragon that is said to represent truth. Its tail ignites with a flame so powerful it can scorch the very sky.
Reshiram's flames can melt the strongest stone. It is said to have helped build a land with an ideal of truth.
A black dragon that is said to represent ideals. Its tail is a generator of lightning, and it can shake the sky with thunder.
Zekrom is a mighty creature that is said to have helped a hero. Where it flies, the clouds turn dark.
It brings a good harvest wherever it passes, and its soil is rich and fruitful. Farmers revere it as a god of the fields.
Landorus stays low over the land and steers the winds to bring rain. Fields it has crossed are known to flourish.
It rides on a cloud of dust and settles on the earth with a wise look. It rules the land with a quiet pride.
In this form it is firm and watchful. Its steps leave a trail of fertile soil that turns green within days.
It sleeps in a freezing cave and has a body that is hollow like a gaping void. It freezes anything that comes near.
Kyurem exhales a breath so cold it can turn the air to ice. Its empty frame hungers for something to fill it.
It fuses with a white dragon and takes on a flame within its frozen frame. Its body blazes with an icy fire that nothing can bear.
In this form it is half cold and half burning, and its roar shakes the glaciers. Its tail glows red and sheds a blinding light.
It fuses with a black dragon and gains a pulse of dark lightning. Its body crackles and its icy frame is lit with a sinister glow.
In this form it is wild and cruel. A great bolt shoots from its tail and freezes everything it passes.
It is a swift colt that runs across the water as if on land, and it fights fiercely for its friends. A keen, sharp horn rises from its brow.
Keldeo's speed is incredible, and its hooves skim above the waves. It is a loyal and brave fighter.
It draws a long blade of water from its hooves and holds it with quiet resolve. It stands tall on the shore like a knight at dawn.
In this form it is firm and unyielding, and its will cannot be shaken. Its blade glitters like a wave in the sun.
Its voice is an enchanting melody that can lift the spirits of all who hear it. It dances on a gentle breeze and its songs can change a mood.
Meloetta sings with such beauty that it soothes the angriest of hearts. When it dances, its form shifts to match the rhythm.
It spins on its toes in a swift dance, and its fighting spirit rises with every turn. Its hands snap out in quick, sharp strikes.
In this form it is full of fire and rhythm. Each step is a beat of a fierce, driving tune.
An ancient bug brought back with a cannon on its back, it was altered by some unknown party. It flies with great speed and fires a beam of energy.
Genesect was a fearsome hunter long ago, and now a rebuilt one roams the world. Its body is armored in strong steel.
It carries a blue drive on its back that sprays a cool beam of water. Its cannon fires with a steady hiss.
In this form a cold stream shoots from its weapon. The cannon is cool to the touch and smells of the sea.
A yellow drive on its back crackles and hums, charging its cannon. Its beam of lightning leaps across the field.
In this form sparks race over its steel frame. Its cannon sends out a bright arc that lights up the air.

A Greninja with a close tie to its partner, whose trust brings out a stronger form. It dashes about with a calm and sure grace.

It is small and bold, and it sings a tune with a loud clear voice. Territorial fights break out often, and it fluffs its feathers to look bigger.

This Scatterbug grew up in a quiet garden. Its soft colors match the blooms around it.
