It moves with great speed and dashes at a foe with a quick flurry of punches. A thunderous clap follows each blow.
Pawmot is a sturdy fighter that trusts in its fists. It is calm until it is time for a fight.
It always travels with a partner, and the two keep close and never separate. They share their food and rest by turns.
Tandemaus pairs off and lives as a couple. If one is lost, the other will search all over for it.
A family of mice that moves as a group, with a mother, a father and two young. They carry food home to share with each other.
Maushold scurries around as a tight-knit clan. They use their paws to pick up and hand over food.
A tight-knit trio of a mother, a father and a little one, who stick close together. Each shares food equally.
This family of three scurries about in perfect time. The little one rides on its parents' backs and squeaks.
It is a puppy made of dough that gives off a yeasty scent. It is so soft that you can knead it, and it warms up when it is happy.
Fidough follows its trainer with its tail wagging. The more it is petted, the fluffier it gets.
It has baked itself to a golden-brown crust, and its body is crispy outside and warm inside. It keeps an eye on its master's home.
Dachsbun is a loyal and protective dog that loves a good meal. Its long body wiggles when it runs.
It carries an olive on its head and presses it for oil that is used in cooking. The oil is bitter at first, and sweet after a time.
Smoliv is a small and cheerful seedling that grows slowly. It spends sunny days sitting still.
Its oil is rich and smooth and is used to treat sore skin. It carries a pair of fruits on its back and shares them with friends.
Dolliv grows in orchards and is tended by farmers. It rubs oil on its fur to keep it glossy.
It forms a lush tree with olives that ripen in the sun. It is calm and kind, and it shares the harvest with everyone.
Arboliva gives off a pleasant, herbal scent. Its oil is prized for flavoring and is said to heal.
It lives in flocks and screeches at the top of its lungs. The color of its feathers decides which group it belongs to.
Squawkabilly is rowdy and quarrelsome, and it fights over food. It follows a leader and flies in a noisy crowd.
Its feathers are a calm, bright blue, and it flies in a tidy group. It calls out sharply and keeps watch over its flock.
This Squawkabilly is the sort that loudly organizes the others. Its blue plumage shines in the sun.
Its feathers are a sunny yellow, and it is the loudest of the lot. It squabbles about everything and never stops chattering.
This Squawkabilly is bold and hot-tempered and starts fights over scraps. Its bright colors make it easy to spot.
Its feathers are as white as snow, and it moves with a graceful air. It is calmer than its relatives, though still noisy.
This Squawkabilly sticks to its own kind and keeps a watchful eye. Its pale plumage makes it stand out in the shade.
It is a cube of salt that came to life, and it lives in a cave where the rock is salty. It shines white in the dark.
Nacli loves to hide in the crevices of a wall. A lick of its body tastes of salt.
It is a tower of salt blocks that stands tall, and a pile of them moves in a line. It trudges with heavy steps.
Naclstack collects salt from the earth and builds itself up. Its stack leans a little when it walks.
It sprinkles salt on a wound and speeds its recovery. It makes the salt from the rock of a cave and keeps it as a treasure.
Garganacl stands firm with a gleaming body of salt. It is a gentle and protective giant.
It is born from the embers of a burned-out fire and wears armor of charcoal. A small flame flickers on its head.
Charcadet is an eager young warrior that trains with a stick. It dreams of a mighty blade.
It wears armor made of a hot, red material and wields a flame like a sword. Its heart is brave and it helps those in need.
Armarouge fights with a graceful, flaring burst of psychic fire. Its armor was made by a mighty hand.
Two blades of blue fire grow from its arms, and they flare when its anger rises. It lives to avenge a wrong from long ago.
Ceruledge burns with a grim spirit and attacks without mercy. Its armor is stained with ash.
It lights up the tip of its tail like a lamp, and sends signals to its friends. It lives in ponds and glows brightly after dark.
Tadbulb is a restless baby that dashes about. It flashes faster when it is excited.
It swells up its belly to store a huge charge, and the croak it makes is a booming clap. It stays still in its marsh and pulls prey in.
Bellibolt has a big, round belly full of electric power. A hop from it makes the ground shake.
It flies over the sea in a storm and makes electricity as it flaps. It is quick and small and rides on a gale.
Wattrel dives for fish with a sizzling dart. It sleeps on a rock when the weather is calm.
It spreads its great wings and rides the wind far out to sea. A charge of electricity gathers around it as it soars.
Kilowattrel sings with a loud cry as it dives. It has a bright, yellow chest that shines in the sun.
It uses a sly look to take its master's lunch. A gruff little rascal, it leads the other dogs on a merry chase.
Maschiff loves to play tricks and drag things about. It has a scar over one eye that gives it a tough look.
It guards its boss with a ferocious bark and the biggest scowl. It has a loyal heart and follows its leader to the end.
Mabosstiff is a stern guard that never lets its charge out of its sight. Its glare can make a thief freeze.
It lives in hidden corners of towns and has a taste for rubbish. It flicks its tail to spray a harmless-looking, but nasty, venom.
Shroodle is a cheeky creature that snatches scraps and runs. Its fur is dull and grimy, but its eyes are quick.
It scribbles on trees and rocks with a venom from its fingers, and every one of its drawings is different. It is a talented artist, but a bit messy.
Grafaiai dips its paws in poison and paints on rocks. It uses its long limbs to climb through the treetops.
It rolls over the dry earth and gathers up loose brush as it goes. It is the spirit of a weed that a traveler left behind.
Bramblin tumbles along in the wind and follows people who walk the road. It hides in a heap of dry twigs.
It unrolls its thorny vines to grab hold of the living and pulls them in. Its eerie, hollow face peers out of the tangle.
Brambleghast drifts like a ghostly weed and loosens its branches in a rustling heap. It is a lonely spirit that seeks company.
It walks on two thin legs, with a big cap of mushroom on top. It soaks up the damp and sleeps in shady places.
Toedscool pads about on soggy ground and leaves tracks in the mud. Its cap is dotted with delicate gills.
It sways its long tendrils to catch what drifts by, and it casts a fine mist of spores. It lurks in a gloomy, wet forest.
Toedscruel has a wide cap and a bunch of waving feelers. It wanders about in the fog, moving slowly.
It hangs upside down from a cliff and waits for prey to pass by. When it spots a meal, it lets go and snaps its claw shut.
Klawf sits in its hole all day and flexes its pincer. It turns red with anger when someone gets too close.
It is a sprout that tingles on the tongue. Those who handle it with bare hands may find their skin burning.
Capsakid stands in the sunshine and basks in the heat. It flicks its stem and lets off a peppery puff.
One head is spicy and the other is sweet, and they quarrel over everything. A bite of its flesh can set your mouth ablaze.
Scovillain shoots fire from its hot head and sprays a sugary mist from its sweet one. The two heads rarely agree.
Its two heads fuse into a fierce blaze, and the hot peppers on its body glow red. It spews a fiery spray that fills the air with a burning smell.
In this form it is sharp-tempered and wild. Flames lick around its pods and set the grass alight.
It rolls a ball of dung bigger than itself across the ground. It pushes with all its might and covers its precious ball with a layer of sand.
Rellor makes a ball with care and takes it home to a hole. It works hard and is proud of its job.
It lives inside a sphere, and its mind is tuned to the tiny world around it. It watches from within a round shell and moves it by thought.
Rabsca rides on a ball and spins as it goes. It sends out a mysterious wave from a pair of eyes.
Its frill is covered in tiny feathers that lets it float above the ground. It zips through the grass and darts away with a trill.
Flittle is a timid and swift runner. It uses its psychic power to fly a short way.
It stares at its prey with glowing eyes and sends out a wave that freezes it in place. Then it kicks at a speed beyond belief.
Espathra lashes out with strong legs and runs at a furious pace. Its large eyes are made for hunting by night.
It makes a hammer from a piece of metal it has found, and it swings the hammer with a merry clink. Its work is crude but fills it with joy.
Tinkatink is a little smith that hammers away and hums. It carries a lump of iron to use for repairs.
It forges a hammer that is perfectly balanced and swings it with great skill. It is fiercely proud of the work of its hands.
Tinkatuff clangs away in its workshop with a steady rhythm. It scowls at anyone who touches its tools.
Its large hammer is so big and heavy that it can crush a rock to dust. It fights with a bold and gleeful spirit.
Tinkaton is a master of its trade and shapes metal with a mighty swing. It is a bit bossy, but dependable.
It is a slender eel that hides under the sand with only its head showing. When it is startled, it ducks down and pops up in a new place.
Wiglett burrows in the shallow bed of the sea and watches the world from a hole. Its sleek body slips through the sand.
Its three bodies act as a single unit, darting in and out of the sand. Each one is tied to the others by a bond of trust.
Wugtrio ties itself up in a knot to catch its prey. It is a quick and sneaky hunter.
It carries a bundle in its beak and drops things on those below. It picks up objects and drops them from the sky as a prank.
Bombirdier soars over the cliffs, looking for something to throw. It has a fondness for shiny things.
It is a playful dolphin that jumps and splashes, and it makes a high-pitched sound to talk to its friends. It leaps over waves for fun.
Finizen loves company and keeps close to a boat. It spins a whirlpool when it feels happy.
It looks meek until a friend is in danger, then it swims out to the deep and changes. It returns as a hero with a heart of steel.
Palafin trains in secret and hides its strength. With a bold dive, it rushes in to save the day.
It has shed its meek look and become a mighty swimmer with a bold frame. It charges through the waves to rescue its friends.
In this form it is brave and strong, and its fins ripple with muscle. The tide sings of its heroic deeds.
It lives inside the engine of a car and feeds on exhaust. It sputters and growls with a motor of its own.
Varoom revs and makes a roar when it is cheerful. A cloud of toxic fumes follows it down the road.
It drives off with a loud rumble, and the exhaust leaves a poisonous trail. Its engine is a roaring force with many cylinders.
Revavroom races on the highway, and its power is enough to leave others in the dust. It likes to rev with a growl.
It lets a rider sit on its back and zips along at breakneck speed. It enjoys a long run across the plain.
Cyclizar is quick to anger and hates to be passed. It turns sharply on the bend and does not slow.
It bores through the earth and digs tunnels with its metal body. It can regrow a lost segment, and it shrugs off a bad blow.
Orthworm hauls its heavy body along underground. It fires a long steel tentacle at a foe.
It sprouts crystals from its body and takes in minerals from the rocks. Its toxic surface is a warning for the unwary.
Glimmet glimmers in a cave, which makes it look like a pretty gem. The shine fades if it is moved to the sun.
It grows great crystals that burst when it is hurt, and sprays a deadly mist. It floats in the dark, shimmering like a star.
Glimmora blooms like a flower of stone, and its toxic petals shatter with a bang. Its glow draws the curious.
Its crystals stretch out in a huge, blooming crown, and a toxic glow spills from them. It shimmers like a field of poisonous flowers.
In this form its body is covered in gems that shatter and fly. A storm of venomous shards scatters across the cave.
It follows its master like a loyal hound, and never leaves its side. It is the spirit of a dog that was left alone.
Greavard gnaws on a bone and plays in a graveyard. Its long fur hides its sad eyes.
It lives near a graveyard and howls at the moon. It stays beside those who show it kindness, and guards them from harm.
Houndstone is a gentle ghost dog with a faithful nature. Its body is as pale as a tombstone.
A flock stands in a row, and each bird moves in time with the others. If one of them is attacked, the group strikes back at once.
Flamigo tucks its neck in and kicks with its long legs. It looks calm, but is quick to lash out.
It lives on a frozen plain and eats the moss that grows there. A herd moves slowly, bobbing along on short legs.
Cetoddle is plump and slow and dozes in the snow. It is gentle, though it looks sleepy.
It stomps across the tundra in a great herd. Its massive body is covered in fat, which keeps it warm in the storm.
Cetitan roars at its foes and charges with its tusks lowered. Herders of the cold north call it the guardian of the snowy lands.
It strips away its own flesh to speed up, and darts through the water like a blade. The extra weight gone, it slices through the waves.
Veluza is calm and clever and likes to take its time. It is able to detect a target with its mind.
It has a huge appetite and swallows whole schools of fish. It is dim and slow, but strong enough to crush a boat.
Dondozo cruises the sea with its mouth open wide. Often it lets a small pal ride inside its mouth.
It hides in the shell of a larger fish and passes for its friend. It lures prey in and spits out a blast of water.
Tatsugiri is shy and keeps close to a bigger partner. It poses and spins to look as charming as it can.
It has a tired, drooping posture and a lazy, half-closed gaze. It lets its partner do most of the work.
This Tatsugiri lounges around and rarely moves. It sips water with a bored sigh and hardly ever hurries.
Its body grows into a great, shining dragon with curling whiskers. It swims through the air in a graceful loop.
In this form it is proud and lively and shows off its curling frame. It spits a fierce jet of water at a foe.
It grows into a long, weary dragon that drifts along with a sleepy air. It coils lazily, then lashes out with a sudden burst.
In this form its tired look hides a deep power. It yawns and a heavy wave rolls over the field.
Its body is long and slim, and it stretches out like a ribbon. It slips through narrow gaps and keeps a stiff, upright pose.
This Tatsugiri is neat and quick, and it holds itself straight. It uses its length to dart at prey from a distance.
It grows into a huge, graceful dragon that stretches high into the air. Its body is as thin as a thread and as strong as a cable.
In this form it moves like a streamer in the wind. It can wrap its long body around a foe and squeeze.
It trained until it lost its mind, and is racked by an endless fury. It howls with an anger that cannot be calmed.
Annihilape strikes without fear and throws itself into a fight. Its rage is a mystery even to itself.
It sleeps in the mud, and sprays toxic spikes that stick in its enemies. It is calm, and doesn't mind if others are close.
Clodsire plods along the shore and leaves a trail of footprints. It forgets its own spines and stabs itself by mistake.
Its tail has a mind of its own and makes the animal wary. It gazes about from a great height and watches all that goes on.
Farigiraf can strike fast with its long neck and a bite from its tail. The two minds coordinate to avoid a threat.
It digs a burrow with many rooms and secret doors. It uses its tail to dig, and hides in the earth when it feels danger.
Dudunsparce has a long, coiling body that stretches through its home. It rests in a maze of tunnels beneath the ground.
Its body has an extra segment, and it digs a deeper and larger burrow. Its longer tail can pound the ground and dig great tunnels.
This Dudunsparce is rarer than its two-segmented kin. The long body lets it hide in a labyrinth under the hills.
It leads a whole army of blades and rules from a cold throne. The great blade on its head is sharpened by hard use.
Kingambit commands with a stern voice. It will punish a rebel without mercy and fights without fear.
It is a tough, heavy creature with tusks like a mighty plow. It tramples all in its way, and nothing stands in its path.
Great Tusk is a massive beast that smashes the ground with each step. It is said to resemble a being from the distant past.
It has a fluffy tail and a loud voice that rings across the land. A person who hears the cry can feel their ears ring for hours.
Scream Tail is lively and bold, and tales hint at a being from the ancient past. Its tail is soft and bouncy.
A creature in the shape of a mushroom that has an ancient and wild look. It sprays spores with a stinging odor that burns the throat.
Brute Bonnet crashes through the undergrowth and swings its fists. It resembles a mushroom from a very old tale.
It has a long pink mane that flutters in a ghostly wind. Its strange, glowing eyes stare at those who stray.
Flutter Mane floats above the ground and whispers a faint curse. It resembles a being mentioned in a very old book.
An insect with a thick, hairy body that crawls in a fast, sliding way. Its glowing wings leave a trail of light.
Slither Wing is a fierce brawler that lunges at a target. It resembles a creature from an old record.
It draws magnetism from the ground and bristles with sand that crackles. Its sparks fly off in all directions.
Sandy Shocks wanders the desert and zaps whatever it meets. It resembles a being from an old legend.
It has wheels in place of legs and rolls over rough ground with a clank. Its metal body is cold and hard.
Iron Treads rolls along like a machine and tears up the soil. It resembles a mighty beast of lore.
A small, bundled-up machine with a pair of tiny hands. It shoots a freezing stream of water from its head.
Iron Bundle looks like a round parcel with arms. It resembles a being from a story of the future.
It has big arms with powerful fists, and it pounds with great strength. Sparks leap from its steel knuckles.
Iron Hands lifts a boulder with ease. It resembles a mighty fighter of the future.
It has several heads that sprout from its body, and each one flaps and glares. It flies with an eerie hum.
Iron Jugulis flies in great loops and attacks from above. It resembles a creature from a tale of the distant future.
It has fragile wings of light and a cold, steel frame. It scatters a toxic dust that burns the ground.
Iron Moth glides through the night in silence. It resembles a being from a story of a time to come.
It is a heavy machine covered in sharp spikes. It stomps around and crackles with a strong charge.
Iron Thorns smashes a rock with a thundering blow. It resembles a mighty monster of tomorrow.
It digs a nest in the ice and keeps its body cool using the frozen walls. It hates warmth and pants in the heat.
Frigibax is a young dragon that nibbles on ice for its food. It grips the ground with the claws on its feet.
It uses the sail on its back as a blade to cut through ice, and its jaw is strong enough to bite through a glacier. It is ever hungry.
Arctibax lives in the coldest cave and glides on its belly. It is growing fast and hopes to become a mighty dragon.
It freezes the air with its breath and slices foes with its icy blade. A fierce hunter, it charges down the glacier on its belly.
Baxcalibur rules over the snowy peaks and keeps a harsh watch. Its mighty fin is a weapon like no other.
Its great blade of ice grows into a towering wall, and its body is wrapped in thick frost. It howls and the blizzard obeys.
In this form it is a fierce ruler of the glacier. Its icy breath turns the land into a field of crystal.
It hides in a chest and lures in people with its coins. If someone touches its treasure, it leaps out and attacks.
Gimmighoul wanders in search of coins and collects them in its chest. Its shy, small body is a ghostly mass.
It has left its chest behind and wanders about on a pile of coins. It scurries from place to place and sneaks away with any treasure it sees.
In this form it is small and nimble, and it rattles as it runs. It stays hidden and bolts when someone gets too close.
Its body is made of countless coins that were melted together, and it throws them at its foes. It longs for friendship, but frightens most people.
Gholdengo collects gold with a hungry gaze. The coins that it hurls are said to carry a curse.
It was sealed beneath a shrine and has laid a curse on the land. The plants that it touches wither and rot.
Wo-Chien rises from its prison with an ominous glow. It is a brooding, vengeful spirit that saps the strength of the land.
It strikes with a sword of ice and spreads a bitter frost across the sea. The cold from its body makes even the strongest shiver.
Chien-Pao runs across the snowy peaks with a mournful howl. It was locked away for a crime of the past.
It stomps on the ground and starts an earthquake. Its massive jar-like back holds a store of cursed sand.
Ting-Lu is a hulking beast that rampaged across the land. A shrine was built to seal its wrath.
Its body burns with a crimson flame, and the heat it gives off can melt stone. Its fiery rage cannot be put out.
Chi-Yu darts about and casts a curse of heat on the land. It has been sealed for a sin long forgotten.
A dragon in a rage, it flies through the air with a howling roar. Its wild cries tear the sky, and few creatures dare to face it.
Roaring Moon batters a foe and will not stop. It resembles a legend from a time long before ours.
It is a knight in a suit of shining armor. Its blade flashes in the dark with blue light.
Iron Valiant is a brave and righteous warrior. It resembles a hero from a story of the distant future.
A creature from the ancient past that is built for a fight. It races across any terrain with the strength of a fierce beast.
Koraidon has a fiery spirit and a keen eye. It is a proud and tough fighter that never gives up.
Its power is held back, and it can barely run or climb. It plods along in a plain, hunched stance, with its strength waiting to wake.
In this build it is stiff and weak and can do little more than walk. It looks up at the sky and waits.
It tears across the ground on powerful legs at an incredible speed. Its claws kick up clouds of dust as it races.
In this build it is fast and fierce, and it never seems to tire. It runs for the thrill of the chase.
It plunges into the water and paddles with its strong arms. Its red body cuts through waves like a boat.
In this build it is calm and powerful in the water. It rides the current and shakes off the spray.
Its arms spread wide and catch the wind, and it glides from cliffs. It rides the air with a keen eye.
In this build it floats gracefully over canyons. It lands with a thud and a proud cry.
A being from the distant future that is designed for speed. It dashes over land and water as if it were flying.
Miraidon hums with a bright electric glow. Its body is a wonder of cold, clever machinery.
Its power is held back, and its body is dim and sluggish. It moves with a stiff, slow step and rarely sparks.
In this mode it saves its energy and lets little show. Its eyes flicker faintly as it waits to be charged.
It tears across the ground like a racing machine, and sparks fly from its wheels. Its engine hums with a fierce note.
In this mode it runs flat out and its body glows with electricity. A trail of blue light follows it.
It skims the water like a sleek boat, and its body crackles over the waves. A fine spray flies from its flanks as it speeds along.
In this mode it cuts through lakes with a smooth and steady glide. Sparks dance on the surface behind it.
It unfolds its wings and soars on the wind, with lightning flickering along its edges. Its flight is smooth and quick.
In this mode it rises on a rush of air and sweeps across the sky. A bright arc of electricity trails behind.
It strides on powerful legs and brings a rush of water with it. It is a wild force that lashes out at anything it meets.
Walking Wake churns up a roaring surf as it walks. It resembles a creature in a tale of ancient times.
A galloping blade of green, it slashes with a razor-sharp leaf. Its steel body gleams among the trees.
Iron Leaves moves with a swift, silent glide. It resembles a being in a story of the age to come.
It grows its own sweet syrup, and the syrup draws a crowd of little creatures. Two small heads take turns sipping from a fruit.
Dipplin lives in a candied apple and enjoys a sticky treat. It is gentle and likes to be near its mate.
It hides in a tea bowl and waits for someone to take a sip. A spirit of matcha, it makes its tea in the shape of a hand.
Poltchageist is the ghost of a tea ceremony that went wrong. A swirl of green steam hangs around its shell.
It lives in a bowl made by a master potter, and its glow is warm and sure. The tea it holds is a rich and fragrant brew.
This Poltchageist takes pride in its fine craft. It hovers quietly and offers a sip to those who respect it.
It serves tea to guests with great politeness, but the brew drains energy. Its stirring is a gesture that leaves no room for refusal.
Sinistcha pours a cup for all who sit down. Its host duties are carried out with a polite, cold smile.
It serves tea from a priceless old bowl, and the brew is deep and wonderful. Its bearing is that of a master of the art.
This Sinistcha has the elegance of a great tea master. Its cup is a treasure, and a sip of its tea fills a body with calm.
It is a loyal dog that serves its master with a bark and a growl. Its strength is boosted by a powerful toxin.
Okidogi is a fierce guard with tough muscles. It stays by its master's side in a wicked scheme.
It is a cunning and sly monkey that has a way with words. It lures others into a trap with strange mind power.
Munkidori is a faithful servant of its master and loves to tease. It laughs with a sly grin.
It is a showy bird that preens its feathers and acts with an air of charm. Its pretty song has a deadly sting.
Fezandipiti is proud of its looks and serves its master with a smile. Its feathers hide a venom.
It wears a mask and dances as a way to please its heart. A kind child that is full of joy, it gets angry if its friends are in trouble.
Ogerpon skips about with a leafy hat on its head. When it puts on a different mask, it takes on a new power.
It wears a blue mask and dances with a bubbling cheer, and a stream of water flows from its feet. It leaps about with joy and splashes everywhere.
In this form it is bright and cool. A fresh spring wells up where it dances and the grass sparkles.
It wears a red mask and dances with fire in its steps, and sparks fly from its feet. Its dance is fierce and bold.
In this form it is full of heat and spirit. A warm glow lights up its path, and the ground steams where it stamps.
It wears a gray mask carved from stone and dances with a heavy tread. Each stomp makes the ground rumble.
In this form it is stubborn and strong, and it shrugs off blows with ease. It plants itself like a pillar.
It resembles a bridge made of steel and builds up a powerful charge. A mighty blast shoots out from its body.
Archaludon stands tall, with a body like a girder. It dares anyone to try to knock it down.
Its heads are tied to a stem, and each one has its own idea. Their bickering is a source of constant noise and a deep, sweet smell.
Hydrapple is a dragon of the orchard that fights with its many heads. It spits a syrup that sticks to its foes.
It has a blazing mane and roars in a rage. A strong blast of flame sweeps the field as it charges.
Gouging Fire is a ferocious beast with fiery tusks. It is said to look like a monster from ancient scrolls.
Its body crackles with lightning that flares up when it is angry. A mighty thunderclap rolls from it as it strikes.
Raging Bolt leaps with a roar and lets off a flash. Scrolls of old tell of a creature like it.
It is a heavy knight of steel with a boulder-like head. It sweeps a mighty sword in wide arcs.
Iron Boulder charges and cleaves with a ringing blow. It resembles a warrior in a story of a future age.
It has a crown of steel on its head, and it uses a mysterious power to control its body. Its blade shines with an icy glow.
Iron Crown stands with a regal air. It resembles a king in a story of a distant age.
It holds the energy of a crystal and can shift its form to protect its power. A small body holds a vast and brilliant force.
Terapagos shelters in a shell of shining crystal. Researchers trace the strange crystal changes of this land back to it.
A glittering shell of crystal covers its body, and it shines with every color of the rainbow. Its power flows from the shell in waves.
In this form it is heavy and strong and well protected. It draws the energy of the land into its crystal.
It is wrapped in a dazzling cloak of stars, and its body glows like a night sky. A strange, deep energy pulses within it.
In this form it holds the full power of the crystal. Tiny lights swirl around it and the air hums with a silent song.
It is a sly little thing that can control others with the mochi it makes. Those who eat its sweets fall under its spell.
Pecharunt hides in a ball and hums while it plots. Its poison is a sweet that is hard to resist.
Its front teeth have hardened into chisels of steel that never stop growing. It gnaws through pipes, fence posts and even stone walls to keep them worn down.
Ratchisel lives in warrens under old towns and farmyards. A colony can hollow out the ground beneath a barn in a single season, so farmers keep a careful watch.
Its beak has grown as long as a spear. Lancerow circles high above the cliffs, then folds its wings and drops onto prey with a single precise strike.
The ring of hard shell around the base of its beak takes the shock of every dive. Old birds bear scratches from countless battles on it.
The pattern on its hood has opened its eyes. While Najarok looks one way, the face on its hood keeps watch in the other, so nothing can sneak up on it.
When it rears up and spreads its crown-shaped frill, both faces glare at once. Most foes flee before it ever has to strike.
The quills on its back have turned to sandstone spines as hard as a rampart. It shelters in dry canyons and digs with claws like picks.
Sandspire curls up and rolls down slopes when it is in a hurry. Its spines grind against the rocks and throw up a trail of dust behind it.
Legends say a Ninetales that has lived for centuries becomes Kitsunox. Pale violet flames burn at the tips of its nine tails without giving off any heat.
It appears in old forests on moonlit nights. Those who show it kindness are guided home, while those who mock it wander lost until dawn.
The mushroom has taken over its host completely and now walks the hollow shell. Pale threads trail from the rim of its cap and spread spores wherever it goes.
Spots on its broad cap glow faintly in the dark. Cordyhusk gathers in the deepest parts of damp forests, where it sways slowly among fallen logs.
The scales it sheds from its long-tailed wings carry strange dreams. Anyone who breathes them in falls into a deep and pleasant sleep.
It reads the thoughts of other creatures through its large compound eyes. Somnimoth flies only at night and is drawn to the light of the moon.
Five heads now rise from a mound of earth that finally shows itself. Nobody has ever seen what lies underneath the mound, and researchers argue over it.
When Molemount tunnels beneath a field, the ground swells and rolls like a wave. Boulders stuck in its slopes are pushed up from far below.
The gem on its brow has split into a crown of three. It walks with its head held high and expects others to step aside for it.
Regalynx collects shiny coins and keeps them in a hidden hoard. Households lucky enough to win its favor often find their purses full by the end of the year.
The gem on its forehead has become a glowing third eye. Through it Psyduke can sense what will happen moments before it does.
It meditates while floating on calm lakes. The headaches that troubled its line long ago are gone, replaced by a clear and powerful focus.
It is the beast of legend that old scrolls describe. Its long mane flows like a festival banner and two swept-back horns crown its brow.
Kirinine is said to appear only before a just and faithful trainer. It crosses mountain passes faster than the wind and leaves embers glowing in its tracks.
A tall sail rises from its float and carries it across the open ocean. Whole colonies drift together and paint the waves pale violet.
Its trailing tentacles stretch for many meters below the surface. Fishing boats change course when they spot a gathering of Medusarch ahead.
Two wings of flame spread from its shoulders, and it runs until it lifts into the sky. It races the sun from dawn until dusk.
Solarion is seen only on clear days. Its spiral horn glows white hot, and its hooves leave scorched prints where it touches down.
The Shellder on its tail has grown into a spiral shell that covers its back. Slowmantle sits inside it and rarely bothers to come out.
A pearl gleams at the mouth of its shell. It drifts in and out of sleep for days on end, yet seems to know everything happening nearby.
The leek it carries has grown into a long staff tipped with green leaves. It guards the fields where its kind gathers and drives off any intruder.
Porrigard wears a cape of white feathers at its shoulders. Young Farfetch'd follow it everywhere and learn to fight by watching its every swing.
Each of its three heads wears a crest of plumes in its own color. They raise and shake them to show their mood to the herd.
When it spreads its fan of tail feathers, all three heads cry out together. The display can be heard across an entire valley.
A long spiral tusk grows from its brow and cracks through sea ice with ease. It hauls its heavy body onto the floes to rest.
Thick fur at its neck keeps out the coldest winds. Glacitusk travels in small pods and calls to the others with deep, booming barks.
Its body has thickened into a dark, glossy tar. Old bones and stones lie half sunk in it, and bubbles burst slowly on its surface.
Where Sludgemire rests, the ground beneath turns to a bog of sticky poison. Nothing grows there again for a long time afterward.
Its shell has grown into a spire of many shells fused together like a reef. Small sea creatures make their homes on its slopes.
A second, smaller face peers from a side shell. Nobody knows whether it is part of Clamspire or a guest that moved in and never left.
Three coins circle on a fine chain around its hand. Anyone who follows them with their eyes for long falls under its spell.
Mesmeryx wanders towns after dark and feeds on the dreams of sleepers. People wake the next morning remembering nothing at all.
Its great claw has tempered into steel. One squeeze is enough to crush a boulder, and it uses the claw like a battering ram.
Pincerex rules the rocky shores it lives on. Other crabs give way when they see the crown of spikes on its head.
A band of steel now circles its body, and arcs of current spin around it. It was first seen near a strong magnetic field inside a mountain.
Dynamorb rolls at tremendous speed and crackles with electricity. Compasses spin wildly when it passes close by.
Two trunks rise from a single root, each crowned with leaves and heads. A fourth head grows low where the trunks join.
The heads argue all day about which way to walk. When they finally agree, Palmagus marches off with surprising speed.
It carries a long bone staff topped with a skull. A pale blue flame burns in the eyes of its great horned helmet.
Ossugard watches over the resting places of its kind. It is said to guide lost spirits back to where they belong.
Its legs have grown longer and springier than ever. It leaps high into the air and lands kick after kick without touching the ground.
Savateur wears a short cape of brown hide that flaps as it spins. It trains on rooftops and jumps from building to building.
Its gloves have hardened into steel gauntlets. Each punch lands with a ringing clang that can be heard across the arena.
Pugilord wears a gold belt at its waist as proof of its many victories. It bows to every opponent before the match begins.
A third ball of gas has joined the other two. Rings of fire burn along the seams where they meet, and smoke rises from vents on top.
The gas inside Smoglom is hot enough to ignite. It floats over factories and old dumps and grows larger whenever it feeds on fumes.
Its child has grown and now wears a helmet of its own. The two fight side by side, and the parent never lets the young one out of sight.
A family of Matriroo protects an entire grassland. Even large predators give their territory a wide berth.
Its horn has grown into a blade as straight as a sword. It cuts through rapids and waterfalls with powerful strokes of its tail.
Sabrefin is admired for the elegant patterns on its scales. Anglers who hook one rarely manage to keep it on the line.
A third star turns slowly between its two, and a swirl of light glows in its core. It shines brightest on clear nights at sea.
Some say Stellamir fell from the night sky long ago. Sailors steer by the colors flashing from its gem.
It holds a pane of light between its floating hands and shapes it into walls, doors and stages. Its performances draw huge crowds.
Mimestro conducts its invisible orchestra with sweeping gestures. Its audience swears they can hear music that is not really there.
Its long pale hair glows with the shifting bands of an aurora. Its gown of ice crystals chimes softly when it moves.
Aurorelle sings on the coldest nights of the year. When its song reaches the sky, northern lights ripple across the stars.
Its dark horns are edged with red teeth and snap shut like a guillotine. It hunts at night and grips its prey with crushing force.
Mandibron and the great beetles of the forest are bitter rivals. Their clashes can be heard echoing among the trees at night.
It leads the herd from the front. When it lowers its broad, ringed horns and charges, the earth shakes beneath its hooves.
Bovarch settles arguments within the herd with a single bellow. Younger bulls follow it without question.
It has grown two clawed forelegs and a great fan of fins. Typhonarch rides the storms that its own rage stirs up.
Whenever this furious dragon appears, heavy rain begins to fall. Ancient records describe whole coastlines changed by its anger.
Its shell has spread into a wide deck topped with a crest of ice. It carries travelers across the sea and never lets one fall.
Small pines of ice grow on its back, and seabirds nest among them. Ferrisle sings to its passengers to keep them calm in rough waters.
A flowing mane of fins trails behind it as it swims. Naiadeon can melt into the water so completely that it seems to vanish.
It appears only to trainers who have raised it with great care. Pale wave patterns ripple along its body when it is happy.
Its spikes sweep back into white-tipped bolts. When it stands still, sparks dance from every one of them.
Fulgureon runs faster than the eye can follow. The air smells of rain and lightning wherever it has passed.
Small flames dance at the tips of its thick ruff. Its body is so warm that snow melts away wherever it walks.
Pyreon curls up beside a trusted partner on cold nights. The heat it gives off is gentle and comforting, never harmful.
Its spiral shell is huge and ridged, with spikes along the outer whorl. Fossils show its kind once ruled the ancient seas.
Ammonarch drifts in the deep and snares prey with many long tentacles. It can draw itself completely into its shell when threatened.
A jointed tail ending in a flat paddle drives it through the water. Its huge scythes and second pair of claws make it a fearsome hunter.
Eurypterox stalks the sea floor at night. Scientists believe its ancestors were among the largest hunters of the prehistoric oceans.
A great crest crowns its skull, and its wings stretch wider than a house. It soars over mountain peaks on rising currents of air.
Amber stones run in a ridge down its back. It is said Azhdarch once ruled the skies before any bird existed.
It has slept so long that a forest has grown on its back. Small trees and flowers sprout from its mossy mantle, and birds nest on its head.
Dozemount wakes only a few times a year to eat. Travelers have been known to camp on it, thinking it was a hill.
A veil of aurora streams from its tail, and ice crystals glitter on each wingtip. Wherever it lands, the first frost of winter follows within a day.
Glacirune appears only to those who have braved the coldest mountains. Its cry can freeze a lake solid in an instant.
A crown of storm cloud gathers around its head. Lightning flashes from its jagged feathers whenever it flaps its wings.
Fulguris brings thunderstorms that last for days. Old tales say it nests in the eye of the greatest storms.
Its fire has turned white at the core, and a halo of embers crowns its head. Three long streamers of flame trail from its tail.
Legends say Pyrevant is reborn from its own ashes. It is seen only once in a lifetime, heralding the start of spring.
When the first snow falls its striped coat turns white all over, leaving only the tip of its tail black. A hunting bird watches the tail and misses the rest.
Ermilong slips through burrows and gaps between rocks as easily as water. On cold nights a family curls together into one long, warm knot.
The gold marks around its eyes shine faintly under moonlight. Villagers once climbed to its roost before a harvest to ask whether the season would be kind.
It keeps a third eye closed on its brow during the day. Noctaugur opens it only after midnight, and is said to see the weeks ahead.
The five spots on its shell glow pale yellow after dark. Swarms of them drift through the treetops like a slow river of stars.
Coccinova trains by punching falling leaves before they reach the ground. Its padded mitts land a flurry of blows faster than the eye can follow.
It carries a small round web between its hind legs and casts it over prey from above. The spiral on its back warns others away.
Orbweavix spins a single great web between two trees and waits all night without moving. Travelers who walk into it are kept until dawn, unharmed.
It lives in the deepest trenches, where no sunlight has ever reached. Rows of tiny lights along its flanks flicker to signal others of its kind.
The third light on its brow is bright enough to blind a diver. Fishermen who see a glow far beneath their boat turn for home at once.
The pattern on its folded wings has become a second carved face. It stands motionless on cliff tops from dawn until dusk, staring at the horizon.
Totemsight is believed to watch the past with one face and the future with the other. Old villages carved poles in its likeness to guard their gates.
After years of pretending, a heavy rain finally lets it take root. Its leafy crowns are real now, and it can stand still for a whole season.
Bark has cracked across its stony body. Mimicedar no longer flees from watering cans and even enjoys a summer storm, though it still hates being found.
The disc of its face glows like a small sun. It turns slowly through the day to follow the light, and its petals smoulder at noon.
Fields where Helianthra grows ripen weeks before others. Farmers welcome it, though on hot afternoons the grass around its feet sometimes catches fire.
Moss and reeds grow thick on its broad back. It lies at the bottom of its marsh for days, and the frilled gills on its head barely stir.
Mirelord has ruled the same pond for longer than anyone remembers. Smaller marsh Pokémon come to rest in its shade, and it never seems to mind.
A halo of light circles the gem on its brow at midday. Its three tails sense the faintest shift in the wind and the moods of those nearby.
Zenitheon grows only from an Espeon raised with great care. It is said to know what its trainer needs before they themselves do.
The rings on its body have narrowed into thin crescents like a darkened sun. When it is angry they burn brighter at the rims.
Eclipseon keeps watch through the longest nights without tiring. A thick mane of black fur at its neck protects it from any attack from behind.
The shell on its head has grown into a crown set with three jewels. It wears its ruff like a royal cape and carries a staff of coral.
Slowmonarch speaks slowly but never wrongly. Coastal towns once asked it to settle their disputes, and its judgments were obeyed for generations.
The dark shape that grew from its tail now leans over it like a twin. Some believe the shadow is the true Pokémon and the blue body only a mask.
Its front shines like a mirror, and any blow struck against it returns twice as hard. Wobbulwark never attacks first, but nothing it faces gets away.
Its shell plates have stacked into towers topped with battlements. Through the gaps a glowing core can be seen, hot enough to melt iron.
Pinecitadel fixes itself to a great tree and never moves again. Bug Pokémon of the forest shelter in its walls when storms come.
Clear crystals have grown at the joints of its iron body. They glow faintly in the dark tunnels it carves deep below the mountains.
An Ironwyrm can be older than the mountains it tunnels through. The pressure there has hardened it until no drill or pick can scratch its hide.
It wears a studded collar it will let no one remove. Though it looks fierce, it is gentle with children and guards a house as its own family.
Mastiffang's jaw can bend a steel bar. Burglars who meet one at the gate rarely try again, even when it is only wagging its tail.
It stays half puffed at all times, a ball of purple spikes. The band of thick spikes round its middle can break the hull of a small boat.
Fugumace scatters loose spikes over the sea floor around its den. Divers who explore near it wear thick boots, and still come home limping.
A blade runs along each jaw of its pincers. It closes them so quickly that a falling leaf is cut in two before it touches the ground.
Guillotyne hardly moves in battle. It waits for one opening and ends the fight with a single strike, then folds its pincers and walks away.
Its shell has grown into a cluster like a hive. Berries stored in the openings slowly ferment, giving off a sweet scent that fills its cave.
Mountain villagers trade fresh berries with Fermentoise for the juice it makes. The drink is strong enough to keep a hiker warm all night.
Two shorter horns have grown from its shoulders beside its great one. It can lift a fallen tree with the three of them and toss it aside.
Atlascross guards the sap of the oldest trees in the forest. It drives off rivals by locking horns and pushing until one gives way.
The shell on its back has become a small volcano. Smoke rises from the crater at its top, and lava bubbles inside when it is angry.
Calderon crawls into hot springs to rest, and the water boils around it. Its cooling crust flakes away as it moves, leaving trails of black rock.
A crown of coral has grown on its head, with a pearl set at its middle. Small fish make their homes among the branches.
Wherever Reefcrown settles, a new reef begins to grow within a few years. Coastal people protect them, because the fishing nearby is always good.
Its mouth has lengthened into a ringed barrel. It fires bursts of scalding ink that leave a trail of steam across the water.
The suckers on its arms glow orange when it prepares to fire. Krakannon can hit a target on the shore from far out at sea.
It wears goggles against the wind and carries a heavy bag over its shoulder. It flies through blizzards to deliver food to Pokémon trapped by the snow.
Sleighwing never forgets a place it has visited. Lost climbers who follow it are always led safely down the mountain.
Long pale streamers trail from its wing tips as it glides above the waves. It can stay aloft for hours on the sea breeze without a single beat.
Raysail flies in partnership with the Octillery that clings beneath it. The pair hunt together and share whatever they catch.
Its flight feathers have become long, narrow blades. It nests in thorny bushes on cliffs, and its chicks are raised among the steel.
A fan of blades spreads from its tail as it lands. Swordsmiths prize the feathers it drops, which never dull or rust.
Two smaller heads have grown from its shoulders. Each watches a different direction, so nothing can approach the pack's den unseen.
Old tales say Cerberhound guards the way to the world of the dead. Its triple howl at midnight makes the bravest travelers turn back.
Its armour plates are edged with steel and a heavy shell rides on its back. When it charges, the ground shakes for a long way around.
Siegephant once carried soldiers into battle in the shell on its back. Today herds roam the dry plains, and smaller Pokémon ride along in safety.
It paints whole walls in a single night with the brush of its tail. No two of its murals are ever alike.
Muralist wears a beret it found long ago and never takes off. Towns compete to be chosen for its work, which draws visitors for years.
Its single horn now twists into a spiral drill. It spins so fast that it bores straight through rock and comes up behind its foe.
Gyrodrill trains on hard stone floors until they are covered in holes. Its kicks land like a hammer from every direction at once.
The bell on its collar rings softly as it walks. Herds of other Pokémon follow the sound to fresh pastures each morning.
Pastorine's milk is said to heal any sorrow. Farm children grow up beside it, and it remembers each of them for its whole life.
Its mane has grown into a towering storm cloud shot with lightning. It races across the land, and thunder follows a moment behind.
Raitenko is said to appear only beside the rainbow-winged bird that gave it life. Where it lands, lightning strikes the same place again.
A ridge of glowing rock runs down its back under a mantle of smoke. When it roars, the ground cracks and steam bursts from the earth.
Enkaiou is said to rise whenever a new volcano is born. It walks the land beside the bird that revived it, burning a path through the hills.
Four ribbons stream behind it like flowing water, and a mist gathers wherever it treads. Any spring it touches becomes clear and pure.
Suiseiren travels with the north wind across lakes and rivers. Those who glimpse it are said to be cleansed of every trouble.
A long crest of black fur runs down its back. It leads the largest packs, and the others follow its every signal without a sound.
Hyaenarch bears a pale scar over one eye from the battle that won its place. It never lets a member of its pack go hungry.
Its stripes have stretched into straight bands along its body. It digs in perfectly straight tunnels, and breaks through walls rather than turn.
Streakoon can run faster than a bicycle on open roads. When it eats until it is full, its strength doubles for a short while.
Its forked tail has grown long and swept like the fletching of an arrow. It dives from the clouds at prey so fast that the air whistles.
Swiftarrow flies in a straight line from one horizon to the other. It migrates over oceans without stopping to rest.
A cap of darker feathers sits on its head like a sailor's. It flies ahead of storms, and its cry warns harbours to bring in their boats.
Pelicaptain's great bill can hold a whole crate. Port towns trust it with parcels, and it delivers them to the right door in any weather.
A third pair of wings has grown, each marked with a staring eye. When it spreads all six, attackers think they face a crowd.
Ocellwing skims over ponds after a rain. The eyes on its wings seem to follow anyone watching, and children find it eerie.
Its arms end in gloves of fungus that burst with spores at every punch. Foes who are hit soon grow drowsy and slow.
Sporepugil grows stronger when poisoned, so it keeps a small toxic charm close at hand. Its cap is ringed with glowing spore pockets.
It moves so fast that only the hum of its wings is ever noticed. Two curved blades at its forelegs strike before a foe can turn.
Shinobuzz hides in the shadows of the treetops by day. At night it hunts so silently that its prey never knows it was there.
It wears a thick white rope belt with paper streamers, the mark of a grand champion. Wrestlers bow to it before every match.
Yokozan can push back a landslide with its palms. It trains by slapping a mountainside until whole boulders crack and fall away.
A pale crescent glows on its brow under the moon. It walks with such grace that it seems never to touch the ground.
Felinelle is fond of comfortable homes and chooses its own trainer. It ignores anyone it finds dull, no matter how many treats they offer.
It ate so many gems that crystals have begun to grow out of its back. They glow blue and red in the dark caves where it lurks.
Gemwraith guards a hoard of jewels deep underground. Miners who take even one stone hear its laughter echoing behind them for days.
The jaw behind its head has grown a row of steel teeth along its whole edge. Two horns sit at its root like a second face.
Deceivore smiles sweetly to make foes lower their guard. Then the great jaw swings round, and whatever it bites is never let go.
It floats cross-legged in a trance for weeks without eating. A ring of light hangs behind its head as it meditates.
Ascetrance has trained its mind so deeply that its body seems weightless. A single strike from it lands with all the force of its focus.
Its mane has become a cloud that crackles with sparks. It runs ahead of thunderstorms, and lightning seems to follow its path.
Fulmenhound howls into the rain to call down the storm. It nests where lightning has struck, and the ground there stays warm for days.
Red pompoms glow on its cheeks and tail. It grows only beside its partner, and the two together light up a whole field at night.
Anodion cheers for its friends with showers of sparks. When it senses danger to its partner, it gathers a charge strong enough to stun.
Blue pompoms glow on its cheeks and tail. It grows only beside its partner, and the spark between them never fades.
Cathodion is calm and careful, balancing its lively partner. It soothes injured Pokémon with a gentle current that eases pain.
Its ringed tail light shines brighter than any lantern. On summer nights it draws signs in the dark that others of its kind can read.
Photurion leads the evening dance of fireflies over the ponds. The shapes it traces are said to spell out a message to the stars.
A trail of glowing motes follows it as it flies. Its sweet scent guides the lights of the swarm into beautiful patterns.
Lampyria grows only beside the partner whose dance it leads. Couples who see the pair together are said to have long and happy lives.
It can swallow a whole car tyre without chewing. Its stomach dissolves almost anything, and its thick bands swell after each meal.
Gulpgorge has no teeth and never seems full. Its long whiskers ooze a poison that keeps rivals away from its food.
A second row of teeth has grown behind its first. It tears through steel nets and can bite a small boat in half.
Megalodax hunts in the open ocean at incredible speed. Sailors say its fin is the last thing seen before a storm.
It is so vast that islands have been mistaken for its back. Barnacles and scars cover its hide from a lifetime of travel.
Leviawhale sings in a voice so deep it carries across whole oceans. Its spout hangs in the air as a mist for minutes afterward.
A third cone has risen between the humps on its back. Lava glows in all three craters, and it can erupt at will.
Volcamel crosses deserts of ash without drinking. The heat it stores lets it go for months before it must rest.
Iron bands wrap its shell and short chimneys rise between them. It burns coal inside its body and pours out molten metal.
Smeltortoise once worked beside smiths in mountain towns. The tools it helped forge are said never to break.
A third pearl has formed on its brow. Through it, Boarcane sees the thoughts of those around it as clearly as words.
It bounces less than it once did, preferring to sit and think. Villagers seek its counsel, offering pearls in exchange for advice.
It staggers and sways as it fights, never in the same place twice. Foes lose track of it and are knocked down by blows they cannot see.
Whirlpanda's spots, like Spinda's, are never the same twice. It carries a gourd at its hip and never seems to drink from it.
Its arms branch out like a desert cactus, and white flowers open on them at night. It stands perfectly still for days in the sand.
Saguarox stalks lost travelers across the dunes after dark. It waits until they tire, but it only ever takes their water.
A mantle of cloud surrounds its whole body. Its song carries over the mountains and calls flocks to gather at dawn.
Nimbusong sings to those it trusts. Its voice is so beautiful that listeners report feeling lighter than air for hours afterward.
The scars of countless battles have spread into stripes down its back. It has defeated more Seviper than any other of its kind.
Ravagoose stands guard over grasslands where vipers live. It will travel for days to find its rivals and challenge them.
The blade of its tail has curved into a scimitar. It strikes at Zangoose from the tall grass, and its fangs drip with venom.
Scimitail grew strong only after winning many fights against its old enemy. The red edges of its gold bands are said to be stains from those battles.
Its crescent has closed into a full disc with craters across its face. It hovers highest in the sky when the moon is round and bright.
Selenolith floats in silence above old ruins. Scholars believe it fell from the moon and is slowly growing toward its shape.
A corona of light blazes around its many points. It gives off as much heat as a small sun, and the air around it shimmers.
Heliolith appears at dawn over deserts. Ancient people built temples to it, believing its light kept the sun in the sky.
A rocky plate has formed on its head, and cracks of light run along its flanks. When it thrashes, the whole lake bed trembles.
Namazuro senses earthquakes days before they strike. People living near its marsh watch it closely and leave when it grows restless.
Its pincers have flattened into blades it keeps sharp on river stones. It wanders from pond to pond, challenging the strongest it finds.
Crayronin carries a shell like a straw hat on its back. It belongs to no territory and serves no master but its own code.
A ring of eight eyes circles its body, and four hands float around it. It was shaped from clay by an ancient people and given life.
Dogunarch is said to remember the civilization that made it. It speaks to no one, but stands watch over ruined cities.
A crown of fronds sways from its tall stalk. It anchors itself to the sea floor and filters food from the passing currents.
Crinolith lived in ancient seas long before people. Restored from fossils, it has learned to settle quietly in sheltered bays.
Its claws have become curled grasping limbs that seize prey and draw it to its mouth. A fan of plates at its tail drives it through the water.
Anomalorex was the greatest hunter of the ancient seas. Restored from a fossil, it still stalks the shallows as if nothing had changed.
Its doubled tail fan shifts through every colour as it moves. A single glimpse of it calms the angriest heart.
Prismaria rests in the clearest lakes. Its scales scatter sunlight across the water, and rainbows appear wherever it surfaces.
It can fade until only a faint outline remains. Its frill flashes shifting stripes of colour when it wants to be seen.
Chromeleon slips through walls when it fades completely. People sometimes find small things missing and blame it, often rightly.
It is patched with scraps of other cloth. A second zipper down its chest is half open, and a glow leaks from inside.
Effigrim gathers grudges from abandoned toys and keeps them inside itself. Opening the zipper on its chest is said to release a terrible curse.
Two bunches of fruit hang from its neck, and its leaf wings spread like a canopy. Young Pokémon gather beneath it to eat.
Musadon walks slowly through tropical forests, scattering seeds wherever it goes. Its fruit is said to be the sweetest in the world.
Three bells hang one below another from its cord. When the wind blows, they ring a melody that echoes across the valleys.
Carillone is cherished by mountain temples. Its chimes are believed to drive off misfortune and bring peaceful sleep.
A second horn shaped like a crescent has grown opposite the first. Its white mane spreads like wings, though it cannot fly.
Omenblade appears before disasters to warn people of danger. Those who heed it and flee are always spared.
A jagged iceberg has formed around its face, and four horns crown its head. It can freeze a river solid with one breath.
Bergmaw drifts through frozen caves, swallowing anything that wanders too close. Its broad jaw can crush stone.
The lure on its tail has grown into a second glowing fish. Prey swims toward the light and straight into its wide jaws.
Gulpereel lurks in the deepest trenches. Its glowing spots flicker in patterns that confuse and draw in its meals.
Ribbon fins run along its whole graceful length. Its song drifts up through the water and lures sailors toward the rocks.
Sirenyss is the most beautiful creature of the deep sea. Its fine snout drinks the fluids of prey in a single gentle sip.
Its lobed fins have grown long, almost like limbs. It is said that its line changed little in a hundred million years, and then changed at last.
Aeonfin rests on the floor of the deepest sea. Scientists believe it may be the oldest living Pokémon, older than the continents.
A reef of small pink coral hearts grows along its back. Couples who find one together are said to stay together for life.
Heartreef gathers lost Pokémon around it and leads them to safety. Its warmth makes even the loneliest feel cared for.
Its seven dots have grown into a ring, and a crown of stone sits on its head. It was shaped by the master of all golems.
Regimonolith carries boulders in its arms and fixes cracks in its body with stone from the land it walks. It never tires.
Its body has become a crystal of countless faces, and spires of ice rise from its shoulders. It is colder than any glacier.
Regiglacier came from the deepest ice of the last age. Only the master of the golems can bring it to grow.
Rivets line its seams and a vault-like plate covers its chest. A ring of lit bolts glows red where its dots once were.
Regiferrum is said to keep a secret behind the plate on its chest. Not even its maker remembers what it guards.
Gold edges its swept-back wings, and a star glows on its chest. It flies only beside its brother, faster than any jet.
Aurelias understands the feelings of others and shares visions through its mind. Those who touch it see the places it has flown.
Gold edges its long blue wings, and a pale blue star shines on its chest. It flies only beside its sister, across whole continents in a night.
Aurelios can render itself invisible by bending light around its body. It shows itself only to those who have earned its trust.
Its tail is a broad paddle scored like sawn planks. One Dambarel can wall off a river in a single night, and whole villages have grown up around the ponds it leaves.
It carries a twig behind one ear and never seems to hurry. Engineers study its dams, which hold back floods that would sweep away concrete.
One arm has hardened into a steel blade and the other into a bow. Drawing one across the other, it plays melodies that carry for miles over the fields.
Each Maestrikket leads an orchestra of Kricketune at dusk. Should a player miss a note, it taps the offender sharply with the flat of its blade.
Its skull has grown as hard as the fossil its ancestors were revived from. It charges cliffs head first to bring down the rock it nests in.
The club at the end of its tail balances the weight of its crown. When two meet, the crack of their heads is heard across the valley.
Its face is a gate of three plates with a rim like a castle's battlements. Nothing it has ever shielded behind that gate has come to harm.
Bastionsaur sleeps standing, its plated back to the wind. Herds of smaller Pokémon shelter in its lee through the worst storms of the mountain winter.
The stripes on its wings have become pale gold eyes that glow after dark. It drifts from hive to hive, sipping honey while the guards sleep.
Its feathered antennae can taste nectar on the night breeze from a mountain away. Travellers lost in the forest follow its lantern-like wings home.
Its gown of comb is now two tiers tall, and honey glows amber in some of the cells. Thousands of Combee live inside it and never leave.
Hivempress rarely moves, ruling from the heart of the forest. When it rises into the air, every swarm for miles falls silent and turns toward it.
The membrane between its limbs crackles with sparks. It leaps from treetops and rides the current it makes itself, sailing farther than any other squirrel.
Voltglider hoards balls of static in hollow trees for the winter. Forest fires have been blamed on its stores, though it guards them very carefully.
Its twin tails have become propellers of three blades each. With its float ring inflated, it can tow a fishing boat back to harbour against the tide.
Coastal towns treat Tidestoat as an honoured lifeguard. It patrols the surf at dawn and dives at the first cry for help it hears.
Once the Sun Stone touched it, its petals opened and never closed again. Two rings of pink blossoms circle its face, and petals drift wherever it walks.
Even on grey days Sakurabloom keeps its bloom, glowing as if lit by sunlight. Orchards it visits flower out of season, to the farmers' delight.
Its frills have spread into a mantle of ruffles wide enough to cover a tide pool. Whatever it slides over is left glistening and slick.
Gastromire's colours blend the shades of both seas. Fishers say a calm tide follows wherever it surfaces, so they welcome it near their nets.
Four tails, each tipped with a hand, let it juggle fruit, swing between branches and steal hats all at once. Its arms have become almost a spare pair.
Quadripom leads raids on orchards with a wide grin. It is so nimble that farmers rarely see more than a purple blur and an empty basket.
Its body has stretched into the long, ribbed envelope of an airship, with a gondola of ghostly cloth slung beneath. It drifts silently over mountain passes at dusk.
Four streamers trail from its sides. It is said that the souls it gathers ride in its gondola until they reach a place where they can rest.
Its ear fluff has unwound into long ribbons that trail as it spins. It dances through the forest, and its kicks can snap a sapling clean in half.
Lapinova performs only for trainers it loves. Its routine mixes graceful leaps with blows so fast that onlookers see only the ribbons flying.
Red gems shine along the band of its tall, bent hat. It points its staff of shadow and murmurs curses that turn into charms for those it likes.
Hexmagistra appears at crossroads on moonless nights. Anyone who greets it politely is said to find good fortune for a whole year.
A broad-brimmed crest with a white band shades its eyes, and a cape of black feathers falls from its shoulders. Every Honchkrow in the district answers to it.
Corvicapo seldom flies itself. It sits in the tallest tree and sends its Murkrow out on errands, rewarding loyalty with shiny trinkets.
Its tail is knotted tightly round its waist like a belt, and one ear is torn from countless fights. Alley cats scatter when it saunters past.
Brutabby takes the warmest corner of any rooftop for itself. It will share it with a stray kitten, though it would never admit to doing so.
Its tail has split into two plumes, each wreathed in haze. The cloud it releases can drift across an entire town and linger for a week.
Mephitarch keeps a sprawling den beneath abandoned buildings. Other Pokémon pay it tribute in berries to be spared a blast of its fumes.
A ring of smaller bells hangs from its rim, and three spires crown its top. When it tolls, every bell in the temple it guards rings in answer.
Ancient texts describe Dotakuron as a bell cast for rituals that called the rain. Its raised patterns record prayers no one can read today.
The two notes on its head have joined into a beamed pair. It can sing four voices at once, imitating a whole choir from a single throat.
Cantatot learns every song it hears and blends them into new ones. Flocks of Chatot gather in the jungle canopy to rehearse under its direction.
Two keystones are stacked into a small cairn, and twice as many faces swirl through the vortex above them. Green wisps leak from the cracks in the stone.
Ossuarion is said to hold two hundred spirits. Those who disturb its cairn hear murmuring voices for days afterward, wherever they go.
Its four aura sensors have grown long and glow a steady blue. With them it can read the feelings of everyone in a valley from its peak.
A mantle of black fur lies over its shoulders. Aurasage teaches its art of aura only to trainers who have shared every hardship with it.
Plates of sandstone armour its back, and sand pours from its pores in torrents. A single yawn can whip up a storm that buries a road.
Desert caravans steer wide around Behemowdon's resting places. When it wades into an oasis to cool off, the water level drops by half.
Serrated claws and a second tail make it a fortress of a Pokémon. Armour plates rise along its back like the walls of a siege tower.
Dreadpion can crush a car with one pincer. It hunts by night across the marsh and the desert, and its venom eats into stone.
A black sash is tied at its waist, and its knuckle claws are longer than daggers. Its throat sac swells with a deep croak before every strike.
Venomsensei runs a school deep in the marsh. Croagunk and Toxicroak come from far away to train under it, and few last a single season.
It has grown two jaws on two necks, and a sweet drop glistens at their edges. Prey drawn by the scent is seized by both mouths at once.
Flytrapex hangs from trees over the marsh, motionless for days. Rainstorms rouse it, and then its vines lash out in every direction.
A long lure dangles from its brow, and the pink spots on its fins glow with rings of light. It lights up the sea floor far below the sun's reach.
Lumifathom stuns prey with pulses from its fins. Submarine crews have reported whole trenches flickering as schools of them pass.
Its fur has frozen into a cloak of ice, and icicles tip every branch. Where it stands for long, snow falls even in the middle of summer.
Glaciarbor grows only near a rock where the snow never stops. It shelters lost climbers in its branches and carries them down the slopes at dawn.
Its claws have lengthened and turned white with frost, and its crest has split into three feathers. It no longer hunts in packs, but alone.
Rimeripper carves warning marks into glaciers to claim its territory. Even a pack of Weavile will abandon its prey when one appears.
Its tongue is now long enough to coil twice round its body. It can reach fruit at the tops of trees without moving from where it sits.
Lickolossus tastes everything it meets. A single lick leaves a numbing tingle that lasts for hours, so most Pokémon keep their distance.
Leaves and small flowers sprout all over its vines, and a crown of ferns rises from its head. Its arms end in roots it can sink into the ground.
When Tanglewood settles to rest, it becomes a thicket in a matter of days. Forests it has slept in grow back faster after a fire.
A third pair of small wings lets it hover perfectly still. It is the size of the insects that ruled the skies of a primeval age.
Meganeuron's huge eyes see in every direction at once. The beat of its six wings can snap tree branches as it passes overhead.
A mane of leaves frames its face, and three leafy tails sway behind it. Small flowers bloom among the leaves when spring arrives.
Dryadeon is said to be the spirit of an ancient grove. When it lies down to sleep, seedlings sprout in the shape of its body.
Its diamond fur has grown into a mantle of crystals, and a pale aurora shimmers along its back. On clear winter nights it can be seen from miles away.
Borealeon chills the air around it until breath freezes into glittering dust. It prefers the stillest, coldest hours just before dawn.
Claws grow at the joints of its wide wings, and its fangs are longer than ever. It glides on night winds without a single wingbeat.
Fangliscor hangs upside down from cliff edges, watching for prey below. Its hooked stinger can pin a foe to a rock until it tires.
Five Mini-Noses circle it in the shape of a star. Its red cap points north like a compass needle, whatever happens around it.
Lodestarch's magnetism is so strong that ships' instruments spin when it nears the coast. Miners follow it to find iron seams deep underground.
Its sleeves trail into a veil of falling snow, and a crown of ice crystals sits on its head. Its long red ribbon flutters even in still air.
Legends of the snowy peaks tell of a bride who waits forever for a traveller. Those who follow Frostbride into the blizzard are never found.
A third red gem has formed on its tails, and a ring of light circles its head. It is said to hold every memory the world has ever made.
Uxinous appears only beside the guardian of emotion. Knowledge without feeling, the old tales say, can never grow any further.
The lobes on its head have lengthened and sweep back like hair. A halo floats over its head, and its tails carry three red gems.
Mespathos feels the joy and sorrow of everyone near its lake. It grows only with the guardian of willpower beside it.
The three points on its head have lengthened into a crown. Its tails shine with three red gems, and a band of light encircles its brow.
Azelthymos gives resolve to anyone who meets its gaze. Its strength grows only with the guardian of knowledge at its side.
It stands on its tail through the night at the edge of the burrows. The lit rings along its back pulse slowly, and the colony sleeps soundly while they shine.
Its stripes flash in a code that only its own kind can read. A warning passed from one Beaconwatch to the next can cross a whole prairie before a hawk lands.
Its shadow moves a heartbeat before it does. Prey that keeps its eyes on the cat is caught by the dark shape it forgot to watch.
A violet glow marks the tip of the shadow that trails it like a second tail. City alleys go quiet when that faint light slips along the walls.
It looks after the trees of its forest the way a gardener tends a bed of roses. Berries grow to twice their size wherever it has slept.
The crown of branches on its head puts out new leaves every spring. Troops of Pansage gather beneath it to learn which shoots are safe to eat.
It keeps the fire at the heart of its troop alive through the coldest winters. The flame in the cup of its tail is said never to have gone out.
Embers drift from its arms when it is excited. Villagers once carried a spark from its tail home to light their hearths on the longest night.
The water in its tail pours out and fills again without end. Farmers in a dry summer leave fruit by their fields hoping one will pay a visit.
It douses quarrels between other Pokémon with a sudden cold shower. Its wrists are ringed with pale foam that never quite settles.
It floats above a sleeping town and spins the dreams of its people into the cloud around its body. Nobody it watches over wakes from a nightmare.
Shapes drift through its ring of cloud: castles, oceans, faces of the dreamers below. By sunrise they fade, and it sinks to rest until dusk.
Its gallop drags a thundercloud along behind it. A herd crossing the open plains is easily mistaken for a storm rolling in from the horizon.
Its forked mane splits like a bolt in the sky. Sparks ring each hoof, and grass it races over is left scorched in two straight lines.
It flies to anyone who is weeping and beats its wings in time with their heart until they grow calm again.
The paired hearts on its face glow soft pink in the dark of its cave. Lost explorers have found the way out by following that gentle light.
Its two spiralling crests turn against each other and grind through bedrock. It can bore straight through a mountain between dusk and dawn.
Cities lay their underground railways along the tunnels it leaves behind. Miners leave a share of their lunch at the mouth of any fresh shaft it digs.
It presses its coiled feelers to a patient's chest and knows at once what ails them. Hospitals across Unova keep one on every ward.
The red cross of fur on its brow appears the first time it nurses another Pokémon back to health. Its apron of fur is always warm.
It ties a new belt around its chest each time it defeats a rival worth the name. One was once seen wearing seven at the same time.
Its black belt is edged with gold thread it earned in its first great match. It trains only alongside a Sawk, whose style it respects above all others.
Its strikes are so swift that a log it has hit breaks apart only after it has bowed and walked away.
Hardened skin covers its forearms like armour plates. It meditates beneath waterfalls for days, and the water parts around its fists.
Its fluff has grown into a small cloud that carries it on the breeze. It drifts over towns, dropping cotton into gardens as a harmless prank.
Children chase the shadow of its cloud across the fields on windy days. It giggles and rises just out of reach whenever they come close.
It spins on the tip of one leaf as lightly as a dancer on stage. The flower on its head opens fully only during a performance.
Gardeners compete to grow the bloom it chooses to rest beside. It is said to dance only for those who tend their flowers with real care.
Its stripes have darkened, and its jaws can bite through an oar. Even a group of Basculin scatters when its shadow crosses the river.
It hurls itself head first at anything that enters its stretch of water. Boats are steered well clear of the rapids where it lives.
Its stillness is now its own and no longer a trance. Within its round body burns a fire that has not cooled in a hundred years.
It sits motionless on a desert ridge for weeks at a time. Pilgrims who meditate beside it say the heat of its calm settles their own minds.
It is a whole band on its own, shaking a maraca in every hand. Travellers lost in the desert follow its music to the nearest oasis.
Flowers bloom along its arms whenever it dances. The rhythm of its rattles is so catchy that other Pokémon of the dunes join in.
The slab on its back has grown into a fortress of layered stone. Smaller Pokémon of the badlands take shelter inside its towers.
It chisels new rooms into its shell with its claws when it has nothing else to do. An old one carries a whole maze on its back.
It leads a gang of Scraggy and Scrafty and settles every quarrel with a single kick. The skin it pulls up over itself now reaches its chest.
Its high kick can dent a steel shutter. Despite its scowl, it shares its food with the youngest of its gang before eating a bite itself.
The patterns on its body have grown into a whole written script. Scholars believe it records every place it has flown over.
