It circles the ruins of an ancient city every night. Those who can read the glyphs on its wings claim they foretell the following day.
It is the golden tomb of a forgotten dynasty. Its many hands seal away any treasure hunter who dares to lay a finger on its gold.
Its painted face is said to be the likeness of a long-lost ruler. On moonlit nights it murmurs orders in a language no one living speaks.
It ruled the shallow seas long ago, and its shell is ridged like an ancient reef. A single bite from its beak can split a boulder.
Fossil hunters say it once swam beside the first birds. It basks on rocky shores for days, its shell warming under the sun.
At last it flies as well as it runs, gliding from peak to peak on broad feathered wings. Yet it still loses heart once tired.
Its plumage is brighter than any living bird's. Researchers watch it to learn how the very first fliers took off from cliff edges.
It has eaten so much scrap metal that its body is now plated in it. Its armour rattles like a junkyard when it walks.
City workers welcome it to the dump, where it sorts the waste it swallows. What it cannot digest becomes another sheet of its plating.
Its illusions are so vast that an entire town once saw a forest that was not there. Only its own kind can see through its tricks.
It guards its pack by hiding their den inside a mirage. Hunters have walked past that den for years without ever knowing it was there.
Its white fur has become as fine as silk, and it wraps itself in a long scarf of it. Dust and grime slide off without leaving a trace.
It grooms every Pokémon it befriends until they shine. Weavers prize the strands it sheds, though it gives them away only to friends.
It leads its flock's dance across the lake at dawn. Each movement of its long neck is copied by every swan behind it.
Its wings beat up gales strong enough to lift a rowing boat from the water. It is gentle with its flock, though, and fierce only toward intruders.
Its antlers have four branches, and each one bears a different season. Spring buds, summer leaves, autumn colours and winter frost grow side by side.
Wherever it walks the seasons mix together for a day. Woodland folk say that a forest it lives in never lacks for food the whole year round.
The membrane between its limbs has grown into a kite of storm cloud. It rides the wind ahead of thunderstorms, crackling as it glides.
It stores so much electricity in its cheeks that its whiskers glow at night. A flock of them sailing overhead looks like a string of lanterns.
Its lances have grown long enough to pierce an oak. It charges in a straight line and never once stops to look back.
It travels only alongside an Accelgor, whose old shell it still wears. When the two meet a challenger, they fight as one.
A ring of toadstools grows around it wherever it settles after the rain. Any Pokémon that steps inside the ring soon falls fast asleep.
It rules the damp forest floor from the middle of its circle. Its spores glitter in the mist, and the scent drifts far through the trees.
It rules the sunken halls where ships once vanished. The frilled crown on its head is said to be made from the masts of wrecks.
Sailors pass the deep waters where it lives in silence. Those who look down on calm nights see a pale glow rising toward the hull.
Its healing membrane now spreads wide enough to wrap a whole shoal. Wounded Pokémon from across the sea come to rest under its fins.
Divers who meet it say their aches fade the moment it brushes past. It never fights unless its patients are in danger.
Its web is a net of lightning that hums softly in the dark. Anything that touches a strand is held fast until the spider arrives.
Its eyes see the faint glow of electricity in every living thing. It weaves new webs across cave mouths during each storm.
Its iron spikes have grown so large that it seems to become part of the cave. Explorers have mistaken it for a rock formation.
It hangs from cave ceilings and drinks the iron dripping from the stone. When it drops to the floor, the ground shakes like thunder.
The lights on its fingers have grown into a ring of lamps circling its body. They flash in patterns that seem to speak with the stars.
It appears in fields on clear nights, and the lights in nearby houses flicker. People who see it often forget the hour that followed.
A glacier rides on its back and grows with every blizzard. It carves trails through frozen peaks that other Pokémon later follow.
Its icy beard has become a ruff of frozen fangs. It fishes beneath thick ice by smashing holes with a single blow of its paw.
At the Ice Rock its single crystal multiplied into a lattice of many. It floats so still in the cold air that snow gathers on its points.
Its icy chains can freeze the air around it in an instant. Travellers on the mountain say they hear it chime faintly before a storm.
So quick is it that an afterimage lingers on every branch it leaves. Its wrappings flutter like the tails of a ninja's scarf.
It travels only with an Escavalier, whose old shell protects it. The two are said to train together in the woods each dawn.
It sinks into the mud beside rivers, and the mud around it becomes a field of sparks. Stepping near it feels like stepping on a bee.
Its flat body crackles with static during storms. Fishermen notice its glow under the water and steer their boats away from it.
It is the grand master of its school, and its sleeves strike like whips. Students travel across the region to learn from it.
It practises its forms on mountain peaks at dawn. The wind from its sleeves can bend tree branches from far across a valley.
Its wings have finally opened, and they are rough as stone. It warms itself in the sun at the mouth of its cave before heading out to hunt.
Its craggy scales are tough enough to blunt a blade. When it roars, small rocks rattle loose from the walls of its tunnel.
It was built long ago by a whole city to guard its people. Its fists are said to carry the strength of a thousand workers.
It stands silent among the ruins it once protected. Ancient carvings show it walking across the land to bring rain to fields.
It carries the strength of a whole stampede in a single body. Its huge afro absorbs blows from any direction.
When it charges, the ground shakes far across the plains. Other herds move aside, and even rivers seem to slow as it passes.
It soars over its territory each day, and its cry echoes between the peaks. Smaller birds gather beneath its wings for protection.
Its feathers gleam red and gold in the sun. It fights fiercely to defend its flock and never retreats from any challenger.
It decorates its nest with bones it has gathered and wears a crown of them too. The larger the crown, the more feared it becomes.
It circles the wastelands at night, searching for remains. Its tattered wings make no sound as it glides above the dunes.
It breathes fire into nests of Durant and melts their armour. The vent in its tail roars like a furnace when it inhales.
Its soot-grey fur is warm to the touch even in winter. Villagers sometimes invite it to light their forges on cold days.
It rules a nest of a thousand Durant from deep underground. Its armour is said not to melt even in Heatmor's fiercest flame.
Its folded wings let it fly short distances between tunnels. Workers follow its commands without question and defend it fiercely.
Old tales tell that one of these took the sun's place when it was lost in a long winter. Its wings give off both light and warmth.
Its ring of eight wings shines like the sun's rays at noon. Crops grow faster in valleys where it nests through the cold months.
It is the one the others follow. Its resolve has never bent, and the steel of its crest sweeps back like a drawn blade.
It appears only beside a Keldeo it once taught. Together they defend any Pokémon threatened by people who would harm them.
It once broke through a castle wall to free the Pokémon held inside. It can carry the weight of a mountain on its back.
Its crown of four horns can shatter boulders in one charge. Travellers in the mountains sometimes find paths carved by its passing.
It moves through a forest without stirring a single leaf. Its blades strike only those who have harmed the weak.
Its mane of leaves sways gently as it walks. Where it rests, new grass and wildflowers spring up overnight.
The ends of its great ears have hardened into broad scoops tipped with iron nails. It can bore a tunnel straight through a hill between dusk and dawn.
Farmers welcome Excavabbit to their land. The soil it throws out behind its burrows is so loose and rich that a whole new field can be sown on it.
A crown of flame points stands up around the male's head, and its tail ends in a second, smaller mane of fire. Every pride bows to it.
When Blazemonarch shakes its blazing crown at sunrise, each pride within a day's walk answers with a roar, so that the whole plain wakes at once.
Its horns have grown into great spirals with moss in their ridges, and its hooves are rimmed with stone. It never slips, even on bare ice.
Alpicorn carries riders up cliffs that no rope could reach. On the way it pauses to nibble the moss that grows in the grooves of its own horns.
It carries a whole stalk of bamboo across its shoulders like a staff. A long coat of black fur hangs to its knees, and old scars cross its brow.
Young Pancham follow Bambrawler wherever it goes. It settles each quarrel in its gang with a single tap of its staff, and no one ever needs a second.
Its white fur has grown into a mantle that trails along the ground behind it, and a plume of fur stands up on its head like a sentry's crest.
No groomer's shears can cut the coat of Majesthound. It obeys the one person it has chosen for itself and pays no heed to any king.
Its long ears hang down like a hood that it holds closed with its paws. Inside them, a second pair of painted eyes glows a faint blue.
When Occulynx lowers its ears, the eyes inside them stare out into the night, and anything caught in their gaze rises gently off the ground.
Its curls are piled into a powdered wig of three tiers, and a train of plumes sweeps out behind it. Wisps of scent drift wherever it walks.
The fragrance of Perfumelle shifts with the mood of whoever stands closest. A single breath of it is said to end even the bitterest argument.
A tall crown of airy cream rises from its head, and ribbons of icing are piped along its sides. The tips of its ears are cherry red.
The crown of Soufflair puffs up when it is pleased and sinks when it sulks. Bakers keep one beside the oven to tell when the bread is done.
Ten tentacles hang above its upturned head, and the spots along its body have spread into a glowing spiral that turns ever so slowly.
Those who watch the turning lights of Mesmerquid in the dark for too long are found the next morning walking toward the shore with no memory of why.
Its rock has become a mound of living reef crusted with coral and tiny barnacles. Two more heads have grown at its shoulders, making nine.
The nine heads of Reefcolony share a single body. When they cannot agree on where to go, it stays rooted in one place for a whole season.
Its fronds have grown into a forest of trailing streamers, and its fins are edged with violet that glows faintly. Poisoned spines crown its head.
Sailors lost among the kelp beds sometimes drift right inside a Kelpdrake without knowing it. It lets them go, though only if they stay still.
A second barrel has grown beside the first on its great claw, and its smaller claw works like a loader's grip. Plates of armour line its back.
Salvoclaw fires its twin barrels one after another so quickly that the second blast lands before the roar of the first has died away.
Its frill opens into a complete ring of panels, like the corona of the sun, and a second, smaller frill fans out at the end of its tail.
At noon Coronafrill spreads both frills to soak up the sunlight. The power stored by just one can keep a desert town lit all night long.
Its white plumes have grown into a mane running down its spine, and rows of stone spikes line its enormous jaw. Its tail is heavy with plates.
Despotitan reigned over the ancient world for so many ages that the bones of its fallen rivals turned to stone beneath its feet.
The fins along its neck have become a ribbon of green and pink light that streams all the way to its tail. A crown of ice sits on its head.
On the longest night of winter, the glow streaming from Borealosaur can be seen from three valleys away, and travellers steer by it.
Its four feelers have become six, trailing behind it like a dancer's ribbons. A second bow sits beside the first, and the blue of its eyes is deeper.
The ribbons of Faerieon reach out to anyone in sorrow. A trainer who has earned its trust never feels alone, even in the busiest crowd.
Its mask now bears a crest of feathers like a champion's headdress, and a band of golden plumage circles its waist like a title belt.
Luchacondor wins its belt high in the sky and defends it there against every challenger. Not once has it been brought down to the ground.
Its whiskers have grown into two tall aerials with a small glowing dish at each tip. Its tail coils like a cable, and its cheeks bulge with food.
Signalmus relays warnings of a coming storm from one valley to the next long before the first dark cloud appears on the horizon.
Its shell has split open down the front like a geode, showing a hollow of violet crystals inside. Its crown of blue crystals has grown taller.
The crystals within Druzarion hum softly when touched, and the sound carries far through the tunnels. Miners call it the singing stone.
Its ring has become a great hoop hung with a dozen keys of brass and silver. One huge key at its base looks fit for a castle gate.
Chatelkey keeps the keys of houses that crumbled long ago. Any door it holds a key for will swing open, and any it lacks one for stays sealed.
Its branches have spread into a canopy draped with glowing wisps like moss. Three red eyes peer out from a knot in its trunk, and its roots trail behind.
Wherever Sylvanshade wanders, the trees of the wood lean over to follow it. By morning, the path it took has vanished without a trace.
Its pumpkin body is carved with a grinning face that glows orange from inside. Its hair has grown into a cloak of vines, and its stalk curls like a hat.
On the night of the harvest moon the face of Lanternhusk lights up, and those who have lost their way follow its glow safely home.
The iceberg on its back has grown into a castle of ice with a turret at each corner. Cracks of blue light shine deep within it.
Whole flocks of Bergmite nest in the towers on the back of Glacitadel and ride along with it as it crosses the frozen sea.
Its ears have grown into twin horns of sound ringed with green, and a third speaker has formed at the end of its tail. Rings show in its wider wings.
The cry of Sonarwing can shatter a boulder on the far side of a gorge, yet it hums so softly to its young that they sleep through any storm.
The cream fur of its chest has grown into a collar it turns up against the wind. It can trail a quarry for days at a time and is never once noticed doing so.
A ring of pale fur circles one eye like a magnifying lens. Once it has followed a scent back to a den, it remembers that scent for the rest of its life.
The fur over its pincers has frozen into gauntlets of blue ice hung with icicles. Every fight cracks them, and they grow back thicker overnight.
It climbs to frozen lakes near the summit and punches holes in the ice to fish. The ridge of frost along its shell never melts, even at the height of summer.
Its collar has become a crown of round pollen puffs gathered from a hundred kinds of flower. It tends them as carefully as a gardener tends a hedge.
When it shakes a single puff loose over a bare meadow, the field is in full bloom by the next morning. Farmers leave saucers of honey out to welcome it.
The rocks of its mane have spread into a mantle of stone over its shoulders, banded in sand, red and gold. When it howls, the mantle rings like a bell.
A pack chooses as its leader the wolf whose mantle rings loudest. It hunts in the brief hour between day and night, when prey cannot tell shadow from stone.
Three of them grow together on a reef, their domes joined at the rims, and they never separate again. Their spines are longer and darker than a Toxapex's.
Small fish that dart between the three domes are never seen to swim back out. Divers mark the reefs where it lives with red buoys.
Rain softens the mud on its back, and the sun bakes it again into plates of red clay that sit on it like a saddle. No axe has ever split one.
It wades into flooded fields during storms to coat itself afresh. Farmers harness it to their heaviest ploughs, and it pulls them from dawn to dusk without tiring.
It weaves a bell of silk below the surface of a brook and fills it with air. Small Pokémon swept along by the current take shelter inside.
The bubble that once covered only its head now domes over its whole back. A tiny bubble clings to the tip of each leg as it walks the streambed.
Its head frill has opened into an orchid's lip of white and pink. No flower in the jungle is brighter, and nothing lured in by its colours escapes.
Where Lurantis had two sickles of petal, it has four. A train of petals sweeps behind it, and it hunts only in full sunlight.
Its cap has widened into a glowing parasol. Travellers lost in the woods at night follow its lights in a slow circle and only find the path at dawn.
A ring of small caps grows around its foot like a fairy ring. These are its own young, and they glow a softer green than their parent.
A frill of pink rises on her head like a crown, and smoke trails from her shoulders wherever she goes. Every Salandit nearby falls in behind her.
Her gas smells sweeter than any perfume. Those who breathe it forget their own wishes and follow her orders for hours afterwards.
The black hood of fur has grown into a cape that falls to its knees. It has learned at last to hold back its strength, if only a little.
Its embrace no longer snaps a trunk in two, but it still carries anyone it is fond of back to its den, whether they wish to go or not.
A second ring of flowers has grown around the first, so the two make a garland in four colours. Three tails of vine trail behind it as it floats.
It lays its garland over a Pokémon that has fought bravely and gathers fresh flowers before dawn. The scent of the garland closes wounds.
Its fur hangs to the ground like robes, and a long white beard reaches its belly. It sits in the crown of the tallest tree and directs the forest below.
It carries a leaf fan in each hand, gifts from Pokémon it once helped. Scrummian climb up to ask its advice before every contest.
The mask of fur around its eyes has grown into a captain's band across its brow. It plans every play of its troop and calls them out with a single shout.
A troop that wins with it hands it the berry as a trophy, and it keeps a second one at its belt. It trains beside Arborsage each morning.
Its plates now overlap like a samurai's armour edged in gold, and a crest rises from its head. It no longer runs from any fight it might lose.
It patrols the shoreline and keeps the sand clean of litter. Any Pokémon that fouls its beach soon finds itself pinned in its claws.
It has three towers where Palossand had one, and a moat of dark sand runs around its base. A whole beach's worth of sand went into building it.
Its windows glow purple after dusk. People who wander into its moat are found the following morning fast asleep on some beach far away.
It now has two fists of innards, which it swings like boxing gloves. Anyone who flings it off the beach gets a punch on its way past.
Fishermen say people once laughed at it on the beach. Nobody laughs now, and the band of pink around its middle warns everyone to keep away.
It has never once woken since it hatched. It lies along a leafy bough instead of a log, a nightcap of fur drooping over one ear.
Those who nap beside it share its dream and wake knowing things they never learned. Its dreams run so deep that objects drift around it as it sleeps.
Its shell has risen into a cone with a glowing crater at the peak. When it loses its temper, that crater truly erupts.
Legends say several islands of the region grew from shells it shed long ago. It travels with a Drampa, whose cool breath calms it after each eruption.
The spine on its back has grown into a tall lightning rod striped in yellow. In a storm it climbs the highest roof in town and catches every bolt.
A town with one living on its rooftops has never lost a house to lightning. The ring of spines around its face crackles for days after a storm.
It stitched itself a new costume from cloth that ghosts had once worn, with neater seams, a hood and a trailing cape. A shadowy claw shows beneath the hem.
It is still lonely, and plays happily with anyone who does not look under its hood. Those who do look are never quite the same afterwards.
Its fins have grown into tall sails striped like a rainbow. Any Pokémon that stares at them is dazzled and drifts about in a daze.
It has two rows of teeth now, and grinding them sends psychic waves across an entire bay. Reef divers hear the sound long before they see the fish.
Its mane and beard of cloud trail all the way to its tail, and two wings of cloud carry it on warm winds. Four horns crown its head.
On the coldest days it flies down from its mountain to play with children in the villages. It is gentle with them and furious with anyone who frightens them.
Its seaweed has grown into a great sail of kelp, and two anchors hang chained together beneath its wheel. Barnacles crust their flukes.
It hauls a sunken wreck behind it as it wanders the sea floor. Ships that pass overhead often find their anchors torn away by its chain.
Its shell has grown into a totem mask of two plates, and a ring of four feathers circles its shoulders, one for each island of the region.
Once in an age the four guardians are seen together. The islands are said to stay calm for a hundred years after such a meeting.
The scales of light it scatters are thicker now and heal anyone they touch. Flowers spring up wherever it has played for a single day and bloom for a year.
It wears the totem mask and the ring of four feathers that all four guardians share. It grows only in the company of the guardian of the next island.
Vines hang from its long horns, and a ring of four feathers sits around its shoulders. When it shakes those horns, a forest swallows a ruined town overnight.
It spends most of its days idle and wakes only when the islands need it. Its totem mask is carved like the head of a great bull.
A mist of seawater swirls around its totem mask and its ring of four feathers. The mist washes the sea clean of anything foul it touches.
Sailors who meet it in the fog say it asked them a question they could not answer. None of them can remember afterwards what the question was.
It buries berries under every tree it passes and never forgets a single one. A wood where it has lived grows thick with berry bushes a few years later.
Its second tail is woven like a basket and always heavy with fruit. When it sits down to eat, it empties the basket first and its cheeks last.
It leaves a trail of false footprints made of light. People who follow them by night wake in the morning in a field miles from home.
The tip of its tail splits into three. Farmers who lose a hen blame Reynardine, though it is usually laughing at them from the hedge, empty-handed.
On a dry summer day it lets go of its crown and drifts across whole counties. Wherever one of its seeds lands, a meadow of soft white flowers follows.
Each spoke of its thistledown carries a seed at its tip. Children make a wish and blow at it, and it carries the wish off on the wind.
Its fleece is so thick that charging at full speed into a stone wall leaves it unhurt. Shepherds on the moors say one is worth a whole team of sheepdogs.
The two curls of its horns meet over its brow like a helmet. In spring, rival rams butt heads until the hills echo for days.
It lies in wait at the mouths of rivers with only its horned prow above the water. Old boatmen steer wide of any rock that seems to have a tooth.
Its shell is riveted like the hull of an ironclad. Once its jaw closes on something, it will not open again until the sun goes down.
It races to the horizon and back before the thunder of its first stride has reached the ears of those who watched it set off.
Three bands of current wrap each of its legs. On a clear day it runs for the joy of it, leaving the grass singed in long straight lines.
It nests in an old orchard and guards one apple for its whole life, carrying it like a shield. A tree it chooses bears fruit too sour for anyone.
Its wings are apple skin cut into feathers. Orchard keepers leave its tree unpicked, for it will chase off anyone who reaches for a branch.
A golden crumble crusts the top of its shell, and the smell of baked apples drifts from it over the hills on warm afternoons.
Children of the dales leave a bowl of cream on the step when they smell it nearby, hoping it will settle in the valley for the winter.
A desert where it lives moves a little every night. It shifts whole dunes when it coils, and the paths of travellers move with them.
It keeps sand in two sacks along its body and can blow out a storm from either one. The rattle at its tail warns others away.
It dives from the clouds and comes up with whatever it hit first. It has been seen trying to swallow a whole rowing boat, oars and all.
Its pouch is twice the size of Cramorant's and there is nearly always a tail sticking out of it. It brings its meals up again to chew them slowly.
Its jaw has grown into a blade of bright steel. It strikes faster than the eye can follow, and fishers find only a clean hole where their catch was.
Rapierfin hunts best in the rain, when the sea's surface hides its shadow. The fins behind its head guard it like the hilt of a sword.
When it plays the strings on its chest and back, the air sparks and smells of chemicals. Its crowds come from miles away to hear it.
The spikes on its crest stand taller the louder it plays. It has been known to keep a whole city awake with a single song that lasted all night.
Its body grows hot enough to melt iron. Smiths of the north once kept one coiled round the forge through the whole winter, and never ran out of heat.
Each of its segments opens like a furnace door with fire roaring behind. Its jaws are black with soot, and so is anything it curls up against.
It trains on the sea floor by throwing boulders. A diver who sees it practising should not stop to watch, since it takes watching as a challenge.
Each of its eight arms ends in a fist with knuckles of pale suckers. The belt round its middle shows how many rivals it has thrown.
It has moved into a tea urn of pale china that never goes cold. Its tea is always hot and always far too strong.
A house that pours a cup from its little brass tap hears china clinking in empty rooms for a week. Two cups float wherever it drifts.
It rules a band of Perrserker from a hall of driftwood. Its horned helm is so heavy that it never takes it off, even to sleep.
It carries a round shield of iron on one forearm and braids its beard in two before battle. Its band will follow it across any sea.
Where it settles, warm seas grow cold and grey. Divers say a reef it haunts still whispers of the bright colours it lost long ago.
Three ghostly spheres turn at the core of its bleached branches. Streamers of grey weed trail from it, and fish flee wherever its shadow falls.
It never runs from a battle and never strikes a foe who has fallen. Children of the south still play at jousting with leeks in its honour.
Its lance is a leek tipped with steel and its shield is bound in iron. It polishes its breastplate every morning before it eats.
Its runes carve a curse that no one has managed to read. People who try to trace them dream for many nights of a long road in the dust.
Two slabs of stone lean together over its shadowy body, with a capstone laid across them. The runes along both slabs glow red at dusk.
Whoever tastes its cream is happy for a whole day. At weddings in Galar, a cake shaped like Patisserene is said to bring the couple good luck.
It is built in three tiers like a great cake, its head crowned with swirls of cream. Piped hearts ring each tier, and a sweet sits on top.
Its troopers march as one, each behind a small brass shield. When it locks the shields together, nothing short of a landslide can break its line.
Seven troopers stand in two ranks behind a leader in a tall brass helmet. They drill from dawn until dusk and never once fall out of step.
In a storm it climbs to the top of the rocks and drinks the lightning. Tide pools near where it sits fizz and crackle for days afterwards.
The tips of its spines spark yellow when it is charged. Fishers who tread on one by accident cannot feel their foot until the next morning.
On the coldest nights it dances over the snow, and the sky above lights up in green and violet until the dawn comes.
Its two pairs of icy wings are banded with the colours of the northern lights. Its feathered antennae can taste frost coming a day early.
Once a year, at sunset on the longest day, the sun shines through the gap between its stones and it walks for a whole night.
Three standing stones under one lintel make up its body, its face carved on the lintel. A pale gold disc hangs in the space between them.
It rides its own floe out to sea and back with the tide. In the far north it carries small Pokémon across freezing water on its back.
The block of ice that covered its head has spread into a floe across its back. It slides on it faster than most Pokémon can swim.
It knows what its trainer wants before they do. A house it serves never runs short of tea and never loses a single key.
It wears its coat-tails like a full tailcoat and keeps a little gold chain at its waist. It reads the feelings of everyone in a room at once.
It eats every few minutes. Half its body is calm and half is furious, and which half is in charge depends on when it last ate.
Its cheeks are great pouches that spark when they are stuffed full. It hides seeds in every pocket it can find, including other people's.
Its green skin took a hundred years of rain to grow. It moved the stones of more than one old castle in Galar with its broad trunk.
Only the edges of its hide still show the old orange of new copper. It sleeps standing in the rain, and its tusks are as pale as old bone.
Restored the wrong way, it grew right of itself in time. Scholars still argue about which of its two halves came first.
A long neck now joins the feathered top to the tail of a drake. The spikes along its tail spark whenever it lifts its head to call.
It no longer shivers. The cold that once froze half its body is now a mantle of ice crystals it wears without noticing.
Its feathered top has grown arms long enough to reach the ground. It stalks frozen shores looking for something it lost an age ago.
It breathes as easily ashore as under the waves. Its jaws, once too strong for its own head, now bite with all the force they were made for.
Gills run along its throat where its two halves were joined. It hunts in deep water and rests on the shore with its finned tail in the waves.
Its head has turned the right way up at last, and it can finally eat with ease. It now eats a great deal, and very quickly.
It swims under the ice of frozen lakes for weeks without coming up for air. A frill of frost runs all the way along its back.
It runs round the world in a single day and always comes back to its maker. The power lines of a whole country hum as it passes.
Two rings of current cross round its body like the arms of an orrery. Seven dots of light in a cross make up its face.
Its maker gave it the shape of a dragon it had seen long ago. Standing beside its maker again, it grows into the whole of that dragon.
A second dragon's head of crystal has risen on its back. The orange crystals across its body glow brighter whenever its maker is near.
Its breath frosts a forest in a single night. Only its king can ride it, and it will carry no one else, however long they wait.
Its mask of ice has grown into a helm of hoarfrost with two horns. Icicles hang from its back like a cloak and chime when it trots.
It runs through the night without its hooves touching the ground. Only its king can ride it, and anyone it passes forgets it at once.
Its mane trails behind it as a pale blue flame, and its hooves have gone to smoke. A crest like a small crown rises from its brow.
Its antlers show those who look at them the place they long for most. People who follow it into the hills come back calm and quiet.
Six orbs glow along the many tines of its antlers. A mantle of thick fur lies over its shoulders, and its beard reaches nearly to its knees.
Its blades split stone as easily as wood. Old woodsmen in Hisui marked any tree it had touched and never dared to fell it.
Its axes have grown into halberds, long hafts of chitin ending in blades of black stone with a spike. Its wings lie flat like a stiff cape.
The spirits of every school it ever swam with ride along beside it. Rivers it travels are said to run silent for a day afterwards.
Seven pale ghosts trail round it like a shoal, where Basculegion had four. Its fins have worn ragged, and its eyes burn red in murky water.
It climbs sheer cliffs as fast as other Pokémon run on the flat, and its claws leave poison in the rock for years afterwards.
It has grown a second pair of claws on its feet for gripping stone. Its tall crest sweeps back when it leaps from one ledge to the next.
It drifts through the dark seas with its sail raised, and whole fleets of smaller Pokémon shelter in the shadow of its spines.
Its spines have grown into a forest of black spears tipped with purple. Ships that sail too close come away with planks full of holes.
Wherever it passes, flowers open out of season. It is gentle to those who are kind to the land, and hard on those who are not.
It rides a chariot of cloud with a heart-shaped prow, and a ring of hearts circles it as it flies. Its arrival is said to bring an early spring.
Its snout has broadened into a flat spade for rooting, and a wig of tight grey curls hangs over its shoulders. Two short ochre tusks jut from its jaw.
It snuffles out truffles buried a metre down. The earthy scent it leaves in the soil draws every hog of the valley along its tracks.
The legs it once folded over its face have hardened into a portcullis of grey steel bars. Strands of silver silk run from spine to spine along its back.
It wedges itself into a narrow doorway and waits there for days. Anything that pushes against its barred face is caught fast in the threads woven through them.
Its wings have grown long enough to carry it across whole provinces. A red band crosses its sharp visor like a mask, and its hind legs are striped red and black.
When one takes off at dusk, thousands follow it into the air. Paldean farmers watch the summer sky at sunset, dreading the moment it rises.
Six mice now live as one. The two parents wear scarves of white fur, two small ones stay between them, and the littlest rides on a parent's back.
Once a family has stayed together long enough, it invites its relatives in. Every berry is split six ways, and nobody ever argues over the last piece.
Its long body is a braided loaf glazed deep gold, scored along the back. Pale seeds dot its ears, and a curl of steam rises from it all day.
Children who doze off leaning on its warm side wake up smelling of fresh baking. Families that keep one say they never need to buy bread.
Its crest has grown into a towering swept pompadour, and a ruff of bright feathers circles its neck like a collar. One wing bears an old notch.
It perches high over the plaza and directs its gang with a single squawk. The flock does the stealing, and it never carries any of the loot itself.
Its helm has become a crested great helm, and a shield of gold plates guards one forearm. A mantle of flame burns across its shoulders.
People say the armour once belonged to a knight sworn to guard travellers. At dusk it still patrols the old mountain roads, lighting the way with its cannons.
Its two flame blades have fused at the hilt into one long glaive. A tattered cloak of blue fire streams from its shoulders, and dark spikes crown its helm.
The grudges sealed in its armour have smouldered for a thousand years. It hunts only those who break their oaths, and its cold blue flame warms nothing.
Its round belly has swollen into a drum ridged like a coil. The bulbs of its eyes glow yellow, and grey froth gathers around its feet.
When it pounds its belly during a storm, lightning strikes in reply. Fishers in the bay row for home the instant they hear its drumming.
Its wings have grown long and forked, and their edges crackle with sparks. Two long streamers trail from its tail, and its throat pouch has swollen.
It rides storm winds over the open ocean for weeks without landing once. The charge stored in its throat could keep a lighthouse burning all night.
Its jowls hang heavier than ever, and a thick chain with a gold plate replaces its spiked collar. A scar runs across its brow.
Every dog in town steps aside when it passes, yet it sees that every pup is fed. One stare from it ends a quarrel between rival packs.
Each of its ten fingers is dyed a different colour, and swirls of paint run over its chest. Its long tail serves as its brush.
Overnight it covers entire walls with murals in poison paint that turns harmless once dry. No two of its kind ever paint in the same style.
Its tangle of brambles now spins as a ring around a pale green ghostly core. Two long thorned vines hang from it like arms, trailing dust.
It whirls over the dunes faster than the wind that pushes it along. Whatever snags in its thorns is carried off and never seen again.
Its cap has spread wide, ringed by a crown of smaller caps. Pale threads stretch between its long tentacles, and its spots glow faintly blue after dark.
Its threads reach beneath an entire forest. When a single tree there is felled, it senses the loss even from the far side of a mountain.
Grey steel plates cover the red of its shell. One claw has grown far larger than the other, and its eyestalks lengthen under a heavy brow.
It clings upside down to cliff faces for days at a time. A single snap of its giant claw can split a boulder cleanly in half.
A third small head, still green, has sprouted between the other two. The red head's leaves droop like a jester's cap, and its body is ribbed like pepper skin.
The green head ripens only once the other two agree on something. Its spice is so fierce that the air around it ripples even on a frosty day.
The ball it rolls has become a glowing golden sphere circled by rings. Its legs have lengthened, and a pale sun marks its wing cases.
It pushes its shining sphere from dawn until dusk. People of ancient times believed it was this Pokémon that rolled the sun across the sky.
The fan of eye feathers now forms a complete ring around its head. The eyes on them shift between pink and blue, and its legs have grown longer.
When chased, it turns its ring of eyes on the hunter. The pursuer sees only an empty plain shimmering in the heat while it strolls away.
Six eels rise from the sand in two rings of three, the middle ones standing tallest. Each has bright yellow lips and a row of pale spots.
All six heads share a single body hidden under the beach. Divers have spent hours digging for its end without ever reaching it.
Its apron has become a satchel slung across its chest, always holding a boulder. Dark feathers band its eyes like goggles, and its flight feathers have lengthened.
It glides over rival nests and lets its boulder fall. The satchel it carries can hold a rock heavier than the bird itself.
It never puts on a hero's suit. Its swept-back fins carry it faster than any Palafin, and it reaches swimmers in trouble before anyone on shore has noticed.
A pale streak runs down its back like a racing stripe. It still smiles as it surfaces, and it leaves the rescued on the sand without waiting for thanks.
Its body has stretched low and long like a racing machine. Two extra exhaust pipes jut from its back, a steel spoiler sits over its tail, and lamps glow at its front.
The roar of its engine rattles windows a kilometre away. Racers who hear it closing in behind them pull over without a second thought.
Its frills have hardened into a saddle of overlapping plates, and two short horns curve from its head. Its long tail ends in a whip with an orange tip.
With a rider it trusts, it can cross Paldea from coast to coast in a single day. It allows no stranger anywhere near its saddle.
Its head ends in a drill of three ridged cones, and steel plates armour each of its many segments. Dust streams from its rear as it moves.
It feeds on the iron in the rock as it burrows. The tunnels it leaves behind are so perfectly round that people travel them as roads.
A second ring of crystal petals has opened beneath the first, their tips glowing pink. A crown of small crystals sits above its face.
Its petals chime like glass whenever a draught moves through the cave. The toxic crystals it sheds are prized above gold by those able to handle them.
The gravestone on its back has become a cairn of three stacked stones. A small white candle flame floats at its brow, and its ears hang long and ragged.
It keeps watch over ancient graves all night long. Lost travellers who follow the glow of its candle always find their way back to the road.
Its neck feathers have grown into a ruffled collar like a dancer's costume. A long train of tail feathers sweeps the ground, and red bands circle its knees.
When it begins to dance on one leg, every Flamigo nearby joins in. Its kicks always land exactly on the beat of its stamping foot.
Ice has built up over its back until it looks like a floating iceberg. Its horn has grown long and clear, and its icy tusks are thicker.
It plods across the snowfields at a slow, steady pace. Young Cetoddle climb onto its frozen back to ride from one mountain to the next.
Its fins have sharpened into blades along its back, and a finned crest covers its head like a helm. The pink stripe along its flank has widened.
It slices through a breaking wave without raising a splash. It is said to think most clearly once it has shed everything it does not need.
Its whiskers have grown long enough to trail far behind it, and a pale ridge runs along its back. Its lips have deepened to a rich pink.
It swallows the wake of a passing ship along with every fish in it. It swims wherever the Tatsugiri in its mouth points and nowhere else.
Its long upper fin curls into the shape of an admiral's hat. A cape of fin flows down its back, and a pale baton of fin hangs below its chin.
It gives its orders from deep inside a Dondozo's mouth. Every Tatsugiri in the bay obeys its commands without making a sound.
Its fin spines have grown into a crown of poison quills running down its back. Its face is rounder and calmer, and its tail has broadened.
It lies in the bog and never stirs, so the bog shifts around it instead. Its quills carry a poison that leaves limbs numb for a whole day.
The head on its tail has grown a neck of its own, so the two heads face each other across its back. Both have longer horns and matching stripes.
Its two heads have become equals. Each thinks half of every thought, and nothing can trick it so long as one of them is awake.
Its body now stretches across four segments, each with pale stripes. Its tail ends in a drill of three ridges, and its little wings have grown larger.
The tunnels it digs under the hills run so far that nobody has ever mapped them. It often loses track of where its own tail has got to.
A second, shorter pair of tusks has grown under the first. It rolls through the night across the crater's floor, and by morning a boulder field lies flattened behind it.
Its hide cracks like dry clay along the shoulders, and a coarse red mane runs down its spine. By day it sleeps half buried in the dust of the pit.
Its scream at night carries over a whole valley, and every Jigglypuff that hears it falls silent until dawn. The ruff round its head has swelled into a cloud of fur.
The tail now ends in two tufts, and the tips of its ears are pale violet. It keeps close to cliffs, where the echo makes its voice seem to come from everywhere.
It rests as a harmless toadstool by day. After dark its spores drift so thick that the trees around it fall asleep one after another.
A second row of fangs hides beneath its wide, scaly cap, and thick roots trail behind its body. It feeds on whatever dozes within reach of the spores.
Its weeping is heard at night above the ruins. Those who hear it see the ancient sky, full of beasts that no longer live.
Its feathered hair trails to the ground in a veil, and three red gems shine on its brow. The hem of the veil is ragged, as if torn long ago.
It flies only on moonless nights, beating its many wings so hard that the grass beneath catches fire.
Two extra pairs of wings run along its long body like the legs of a centipede, and flames flicker at their edges. Its six heavy legs grip the ground when it lands.
Compasses spin wildly within a mile of it at night. It drags iron sand into dunes shaped like the lines of a magnet.
A coat of iron filings stands on end along its back, and two horns of fused sand crackle on its head. The charge lifts small stones from the ground as it passes.
In daylight it races across the plains faster than any car, and the tracks it leaves are perfectly straight.
Its wheels have become twin treads, and a ring of blue light circles its body. The tusks are shaped into blades, which it uses to carve through fallen trees.
It speeds above the sea by day, and anything it passes freezes solid. What it carries in its packs remains a secret.
A second pack of gleaming plates sits on its back, and a visor of ice covers its eyes. Four jets under its body keep it hovering just above the waves.
Its punches crack bedrock at a single blow. It stands motionless by night and wakes the moment the sun touches it.
Each hand is armoured with four plates like a gauntlet, and coils glow along its arms. A crest on its head is shaped like a helmet and stores the light of the day.
It circles high on clear days, its three heads turning in every direction. Nothing that moves below escapes its notice.
A third head has grown at the end of its tail, and jets burn at the tips of its swept-back wings. A ring of lights glows round its neck while it hunts.
Its core burns as hot as the sun at noon. It drifts above the desert by day, and the sand beneath turns to glass.
A second ring of armour surrounds the core, and its antennae curl into two prongs. The tips of its wings blaze like torches, leaving smoke that smells of poison.
It stands still as a statue in the sun, drinking in light through its spines. Then it charges, and nothing can stop it.
A cage of crystal rods rises over its back, and sparks leap from rod to rod. Its jaw is a heavy plate that can crush a boulder in one bite.
It stands on a tall stack of coins in place of its board. A crown of coins sits on its head, and a gown of linked coins hangs down its body.
Every night it counts each coin it owns. Anyone who steals even one finds their own pockets mysteriously empty the next morning.
Eight wooden tablets now spread from its back in a fan, each carved with a glowing red seal. Roots trail from the mound of leaves on its shell.
Its tablets bear the names of a cruel king's servants. Each one it reclaims leaves the land around it a little greener than before.
Four blades of ice now jut from it, two at its jaw and two from its shoulders. A red seal glows on its brow, and its long fur is frosted.
Its blades were carved from the ice of an ancient king's tomb. A biting wind follows its pawprints for days after it has passed.
The vessel on its head has swollen into a great bronze cauldron marked with a glowing seal. Its antlers branch further, and its legs are heavier.
The cauldron it carries is said to hold the grudge of the whole land. Wherever it lies down to rest, nothing grows for a year.
Its fiery body has lengthened and grown fins of flame. Six glowing beads circle it in a ring, and a red seal burns on its brow.
Its six beads hold the fire of a jealous king's heart. It glides through molten lava as easily as other fish swim through a stream.
When the moon is full it soars over the crater's rim, and its roar shakes loose rocks from the walls for hours.
Its wings hang in ragged shreds like the sails of a ruined ship, and the horns on its head curl forward into a crown. The red of its belly glows brightest at midnight.
It moves faster than the eye can follow, and its lance leaves trails of light in the noon sky.
Its two blades join into one long lance, and a cape of light streams from its shoulders. The visor over its face has been honed to a sharper edge than before.
Its bowl has become an iron kettle, with a ghostly whisk hovering above. Wisps of matcha steam drift upward, and the green tea inside glows.
It invites anyone who sits still to a tea ceremony. The tea it pours slowly drains the guest's strength, though the cups are exquisite.
It once guarded a cruel master. Now it bows only to Pecharunt and smashes the boulders of the mountain in its rage.
A heavy mantle of chain links hangs over its shoulders, and its fur stands up like a lion's mane. Plates of poisoned muscle cover its thick arms.
It wanders through the forest by night, reading the minds of those it meets. It does as Pecharunt wishes and no more.
Its long tail now forks in two, and its fur is tipped with poison-green light. A collar of linked rings circles its neck, and it never takes it off.
It dances in the moonlight with its train spread wide. All who watch are charmed and forget what they were doing.
Poison-green eyes mark the feathers of its sweeping train, and a fan of dark plumes frames its throat. It serves Pecharunt gracefully and demands nothing for itself.
